lens: Contrarian / founder-market fit. US and EU teams mostly build trading and gaming apps. These four ideas go where they won't: the money problems of Seeker owners in the global south (cash ramps, savings circles, scams and drains), and West African risk-pooling culture (ajo/esusu) applied to ORE. The builder likely lives these problems in WAT. Each loop is still designed to work for the whole 121K-SGT base across 57 countries. I checked novelty on the web. P2P Protocol (p2p.me) plans a Solana launch in Q3 2026. Kin already ships bonded ROSCAs with an on-chain SGT check. Solflare Guards already simulates transactions. No MWA-proxy firewall, no Solana auction-ROSCA and no v3-grid ORE pool turned up.

ideas.name: Alert
ideas.one_liner: A peer-to-peer cash ramp where the seller's own Seeker is the oracle: when their bank's genuine 'credit alert' lands, a hardware-bound key the program caps releases the USDC escrow, so cash becomes crypto in under a minute with no exchange and no stranger holding your money.
ideas.core_concept: In Nigeria people say 'alert don land' when money hits. Every bank and fintech (Opay, Moniepoint, Kuda, GTBank) pushes a credit notification within seconds, and so do PIX in Brazil, UPI in India, M-Pesa in Kenya and Toss in Korea. Binance P2P left the naira market in 2024 and Paxful died, so millions of people cash in and out through P2P desks that fail on trust. The seller has to watch their bank app and release by hand, buyers get stuck, and fake 'credit alert' screenshots and SMS are a scam industry of their own. Alert makes the seller's phone the oracle. An on-device NotificationListener accepts only notifications posted by allowlisted bank apps whose signing certificate is verified, so fake SMS and screenshots cannot trigger it. It matches a unique fingerprinted amount (₦50,000.37) and the payer's name. A non-exportable Android Keystore P-256 key then signs a release, which the escrow program verifies through the secp256r1 precompile. The program limits that key to paying the specific buyer of a specific funded order, within per-order and daily caps. Even a fully compromised phone can only 'pay people who already paid you'. Merchants 'clock in' to a shift and earn the spread. Every settled trade updates an on-chain street-rate index for NGN/BRL/INR/KES, and that index becomes the home-screen widget people check every day. For the Seeker base the pitch is simple: cash out SKR or USDC to your local bank in about 60 seconds, with SGT-verified humans on the other side. Why now: the secp256r1 precompile, Android 16 Live Updates on Seeker, 250 ms slots and a record stablecoin supply have all arrived. P2P Protocol's planned Solana move confirms the demand, and the dApp Store has only one remittance app and no native ramp.
ideas.daily_loop: MERCHANTS (the core habit, because it is their income). Trigger: the morning QS tile or Live Update prompt 'Clock in as merchant'. Action: one Seed Vault double-tap funds the day's USDC float and arms auto-release caps. Variable reward: orders arrive all shift; each auto-matched alert brings a haptic thump and spread earned, and rate swings change margins. Investment: SGT-keyed merchant reputation raises limits and tiers and brings repeat buyers. EVERY OTHER SEEKER. Trigger: the widget shows today's on-chain street rate (the daily 'what's the dollar rate?' check Nigerians already do), plus threshold rate alerts. Action: sell or buy in three taps when the rate is right. Variable reward: rate moves and fill speed. Investment: trader reputation and saved payout rails. None of this needs an airdrop, because it is money people have to move anyway.
mobile_native_surfaces: NotificationListenerService with an allowlist of bank-app package names and signing certificates (defeats fake-alert SMS and screenshots)
Android Keystore / StrongBox P-256 release key, verified on-chain via the secp256r1 precompile
Android 16 Live Update (ProgressStyle promoted ongoing notification) for the merchant 'shift' and for a buyer's in-flight order
Quick Settings tile: Clock in / Clock out as merchant
Glance home-screen widget: live street rate plus open orders
Seed Vault double-tap to fund the float and for manual release above the cap
Share-sheet target: share a bank transfer receipt into Alert; ML Kit OCR attaches it as dispute evidence
On-device LiteRT-LM (Gemma 3 1B) fallback parser for unknown alert formats; bank data never leaves the phone
SGT on-chain gate plus .skr trader handles
Haptic confirmation on match and release
ideas.solana_integration: A custom Anchor or Pinocchio 'alert_escrow' program. Accounts: MerchantAccount PDA [merchant, sgt_mint] with the SGT verified in-program (Token-2022 owner, TokenGroupMember group == GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…, holder == signer). It stores the registered P-256 release pubkey, per-order cap, daily cap, rolling usage and supported rails. Order PDA [order, merchant, nonce] holds a USDC vault ATA, the fingerprinted fiat amount, the rate, the buyer and deadlines. Instructions: open_merchant, post_order, take_order, mark_paid, and release_by_device. release_by_device requires a secp256r1 precompile instruction in the same transaction, found via instruction introspection with a checked sysvar-instructions address (the Wormhole bug class). The signed message covers (program id, order PDA, buyer, amount, nonce, expiry), which makes it replay-proof. Fees are paid by a Kora relayer or by the buyer, so the phone needs no hot SOL key. Also release_manual (MWA double-tap), permissionless timeout refunds, and open_dispute and resolve. Disputes: both phones produce device-signed alert attestations (the buyer's phone sees the debit alert too), and only their hashes go on-chain. SGT-verified jurors bond SKR and vote by commit-reveal. A RateIndex PDA per currency is updated on every settlement (volume-weighted EMA) and any program can read it. Helius webhooks and Parsed Streams feed FCM pushes. It has to be on-chain because the escrow is non-custodial, the caps on the phone key are enforced by the program rather than a server, reputation is portable by device, and no website or regulator can quietly edit the rate index.
ideas.ore_detail: Not an ORE product. Bolting ORE on would fail the 'ORE must be the primary product' rule and blur the payments story.
ideas.skr_role: SKR is the dispute layer. SGT-verified Seekers bond SKR to sit on a dispute panel. The losing party pays the arbitration fee in SKR, and jurors who vote against the final majority are slashed. Merchants can also escrow an SKR performance bond to unlock higher release caps. This is program-held collateral, not the SKR staking program.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: Split screen, real phones, no cuts. Left: a friend's Android sends ₦25,000.37 through Moniepoint. Right: a Seeker lies face-down. The bank notification arrives, Alert's status-bar chip flips to 'Matched · ADAEZE O. · ₦25,000.37', the phone gives a haptic thump, and the escrow releases 16.10 USDC (Solscan tx on screen) before the sender has put their phone down. The left phone's widget shows the USDC has landed. Voiceover: 'In Lagos we say alert don land. On Seeker, the alert IS the settlement.' Then someone sends a fake credit-alert SMS, and nothing happens: 'Unverified sender, ignored.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: real-world stablecoin payments plus on-chain price discovery. The street-rate index is 'internet capital markets' for currencies under capital controls, and 250 ms slots make settlement feel instant. Mert: privacy by design (bank data is parsed on the device and only hashes go on-chain), with Helius Parsed Streams and webhooks driving every push. Chase: the 'first 10k users' consumer story, in markets US teams ignore, with a clean stablecoin narrative. Akshay: it opens Nigeria, Brazil, India and Kenya for Seeker and gives every owner a cash-out path Seed Vault Wallet lacks. Beeman: it is aggressively native (NotificationListener, Keystore, secp256r1, Live Updates, QS tile), with nothing a PWA could do. Ethelsec: a hot key whose worst case is bounded, an explicit threat model (package-signature defense against fake alerts, replay-proof precompile verification with the sysvar check, on-chain caps, no admin keys) and a founder who lives the fraud patterns first-hand.
ideas.closest_existing: P2P Protocol / p2p.me is the biggest direct competitor. It is live on Base, plans a Solana launch in Q3 2026, and supports UPI, PIX, QRIS and Nigeria, with ZK-KYC via Reclaim, staked merchants and on-chain disputes. It validates demand, and it is funded (MetaDAO raise). But its merchants still confirm fiat receipt themselves, and it is web/Telegram-first, not Seeker-native. Peer (formerly ZKP2P, on Base) uses zkTLS proofs from Venmo, Revolut and Wise, which are rich-country rails. Binance/Bybit P2P, Noones and Yellow Card are custodial CEX desks. Rampa (the 2025 BONK prize winner) does off-ramping, and PagCrypto handles BRL. The GitHub demo Osas-XLR8/crypto-escrow-p2p already sketches a PaymentNotificationListener, so the core idea is not unthinkable. The difference is a production Seeker app: program-capped hardware-key release via secp256r1, certificate-verified notification sources, SGT-keyed identity, Live Update merchant shifts and a public on-chain rate index.
ideas.technical_depth: A Rust program with about 12 instructions and LiteSVM/Mollusk tests, including adversarial cases: replayed P-256 signatures, a spoofed sysvar-instructions account, cap overflow, expired orders, and a double release race. A Kotlin/Compose app with a NotificationListener and a per-bank parser library, backed by a fixture corpus covering 20+ banks and fintechs in 4 countries, plus an on-device LLM fallback. The Keystore attestation chain is recorded for audit. A Kora fee relayer. A backend that does off-chain matching and pushes Helius webhooks to FCM, while settlement stays on-chain. THREAT_MODEL.md, and many granular commits across program, parser and app.
key_risks: Regulatory and personal legal exposure for a Nigerian founder: Nigeria SEC VASP rules, the 2024 Binance/naira episode in which executives were detained, and CBN pressure on AbokiFX over parallel rates. It needs a non-custodial framing, geofencing and legal review.
P2P Protocol may ship on Solana first, with funding and existing merchant liquidity.
Third-party-funded payments (stolen bank accounts) can get the seller's bank account frozen. This is the #1 real P2P risk; name matching only mitigates it.
Bank notification formats change, and some omit the payer's name, so the parser needs constant maintenance.
The notification-access permission scares users and needs very careful onboarding.
Two-sided liquidity cold start, since merchants are needed in each currency.
The demo needs real fiat transfers and multiple phones. Seeker availability and ownership in Nigeria is unverified.
US-based judges may see it as regional unless the multi-rail design (PIX, UPI, M-Pesa) is shown working.

ideas.name: Night Shift
ideas.one_liner: ORE mining crews that never clock out. Seekers across time zones take shifts on the grid, coordinate tiles so the crew is almost always on the winning square, and an on-chain esusu pact shares the luck, because a mining pool is just an esusu for Motherlodes.
ideas.core_concept: ORE's 5x5 grid runs a round every ~78 seconds, around the clock. A solo phone miner experiences the Motherlode (1/500 per round, ~312 ORE today) as pure lottery variance. ORE's mobile story is a PWA, and its dApp Store app has been stale since October 2025. West Africa solved variance centuries ago with esusu and ajo (pool fortune, rotate it, enforce it socially), and Bitcoin solved it with mining pools; Night Shift brings both to ORE on Seeker. You join a crew of up to 25 SGT-verified Seekers, one seat per device, spread across time zones (Lagos, São Paulo, Seoul). Each day you 'clock in' with a single Seed Vault double-tap that funds your own ORE Automation account for your shift window. Night Shift's DiscretionaryBps executor gives crewmates complementary tile masks, so the crew covers as many squares as possible. ORE's own invariant means your SOL can only be deployed or returned to you. Each member's ORE miner sits under a per-member vault PDA, which lets the program enforce the crew pact. A chosen percentage of each member's mined ORE, read trustlessly from ORE Miner.lifetime_rewards_ore deltas, is pooled and split in a weekly 'Sunday split'. So when Ji-woo's tile hits at 3am Lagos time, the whole crew eats. The economics are shown honestly: pooling does not raise expected value (production cost is ~$104 against a price of ~$85). It makes mining survivable and social, and the app shows expected cost per shift up front. Why now: ORE Automation plus DiscretionaryBps (Aug 17, 2026) made non-custodial third-party executors possible, Live Updates landed on Seeker, and ORE's own 'Proof of mobile, mine on Seeker, coming soon' promise was never shipped.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: the morning widget reads 'While you slept your crew mined 2.4 ORE · your share 0.19 · Motherlode 318', plus a push when your shift is about to start. Action: one double-tap clock-in (amount, split/solo mix, 'only deploy when the Motherlode is above X' using ORE's conditional deploys), after which it runs hands-free. Variable reward: a round resolves on the lock screen every ~78 s, with a haptic thump when the crew hits, a special pattern on a solo-tile win, the live Motherlode meter, and a handover push when the next time zone takes the grid. Investment: your crew seat and shift streak, unclaimed ORE earning ORE's refining fees (the protocol's own 'holding pays' hook), pact history and crew leaderboard rank. Weekly spike: the Sunday split. Without any airdrop, ORE itself is the reward, and your crew is counting on you to cover your time zone.
mobile_native_surfaces: Android 16 Live Update: a user-started mining shift with a status-bar chip and lock-screen board. It shows session progress, not a price ticker, so it stays within Google's rules.
Quick Settings tile: Clock in / Clock out (starts from the lock screen via a trampoline Activity to MWA)
Glance widget: a 5x5 crew board with coverage colours, .skr names on tiles and the Motherlode
Distinct haptic patterns for crew hit, solo tile and Motherlode
Seed Vault double-tap as the daily clock-in ritual (one signature funds the whole shift)
SGT-keyed crew seats verified on-chain; .skr identities on the board
FCM pushes driven by Helius / api.ore.com round and Motherlode events
Time-zone-aware 'follow the sun' shift scheduling; App Shortcut 'Clock in with last strategy'
ideas.solana_integration: ORE program (oreV3EG1…). Each member has an Automation account whose executor is the Night Shift executor, using the DiscretionaryBps strategy with the fee capped on-chain at ≤100 bps, or a zero-fee mode using ORE's permissionless executor. Conditions are set for minimum Motherlode, maximum production cost and split/solo counts. The Miner account's authority is a per-member vault PDA [vault, sgt_mint]. Night Shift program (Anchor or Pinocchio): Crew PDA [crew, id] (pact %, shift schedule, settlement epoch); Seat PDA [seat, crew, sgt_mint] with the SGT verified in-program (Token-2022 group member == GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…, holder == signer). Instructions: clock_in (member signs; SOL moves into the vault, CPI tops up the automation and the shift window is recorded). snapshot and settle, a permissionless crank that reads ORE Miner accounts after verifying owner == ORE program and re-deriving PDA [MINER, vault], computes lifetime_rewards_ore deltas per epoch, CPI-claims each member's pact share into the crew pot and distributes it. withdraw is member-only, available any time, minus any unsettled pact share. The executor backend subscribes to Board and Round accounts and assigns complementary tile masks per crew per round. It has to be on-chain because the luck-sharing pact must be enforceable without trusting a crew captain or the app, and ORE's own accounts are the trustless source of who mined what.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the entire product: the native Seeker client for the v3/v4 grid that ORE never shipped. It uses Automation accounts, conditional deploys, refining-fee-aware claim UX ('hold unclaimed to earn refining'), ORE-denominated pact settlement, and in-app ORE Reserve and 'buried' stats. It meets 'ORE is the primary product, live and user-facing', and the milestone metrics fall out naturally: miners per round added, SOL deployed, active crews. It also revives ORE's abandoned claim_seeker 'Proof of mobile' idea at the app layer, with one seat per SGT.
ideas.skr_role: SKR is the shift-reliability bond. Taking a crew seat locks a small SKR bond, which is slashed to the crewmates who covered for you if you miss your committed time-zone shift without handing over. SKR secures a coordination promise, not yield. It is also used for .skr-to-.skr tips after solo or Motherlode hits. To be honest, SKR is secondary here.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: A locked Seeker on a desk at night. The status-bar chip reads '⛏ Night Shift · crew on 23/25'. The lock-screen Live Update shows the board filling as the executor deploys for members in Lagos, Seoul and São Paulo, with .skr names on the squares. A round resolves: tile 17 flashes gold, the phone thumps, and it reads 'ji-woo.skr (Seoul) hit · crew +0.31 ORE'. Cut to morning: the widget says 'While you slept your crew mined 2.4 ORE.' One double-tap: 'Clocked in. Lagos has the grid.' Voiceover: 'A mining pool is just an esusu for luck.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: ORE is a flagship Solana-native mechanism, and this is the consumer mobile client it never got. It uses non-custodial automation and 250 ms slots, and it frames expected value honestly instead of as yield. Mert: heavy real-time use of Board and Round account streams via Helius (LaserStream / Parsed Streams) and event-driven pushes. Chase: a network-effect loop (crews recruit crews) aimed at a base of only ~150-165 active miners per round, so the growth is measurable. Akshay and Beeman: Seeker-only seats with SGT verified inside a program (no official example exists), Live Updates, a QS tile and a widget, and genuine daily use that lifts Activity Tracking honestly. Ethelsec: ORE's deploy-or-return invariant, per-member vault PDAs instead of pooled custody, rigorous foreign-account validation (owner check plus PDA re-derivation, the exact missing-account-check class behind ORE's June stake exploit), and an executor fee capped on-chain.
ideas.closest_existing: The official ORE web app and PWA (Aug 20, 2026) with Automation Lite/Pro. The official ORE dApp Store app, stale since October 2025. refinORE Autominer (SKR→ORE swap, Jan 2026). Minemore/Orestack and Oreminer (bot-style autominers). Evore (a managed-miner program). Radiants' own lodestar-cli. ore-pool: v1/v2-era hashing pools existed, but nothing pools the v3 grid. Tramplin (a MONOLITH winner, random-winner staking). 'ORE crews / squads' is an obvious idea, so other Clock In teams may build squad mining. The differences here are an enforceable on-chain pact that reads ORE Miner accounts, coordinated tile coverage through a DiscretionaryBps executor, follow-the-sun shifts across the international Seeker base, and lock-screen Live Update mining.
ideas.technical_depth: A Rust program that CPIs into ORE (automate, top-up, claim) and deserializes ORE Miner, Round and Board accounts via ore-api types. A Rust executor service that schedules tile masks per round against ORE's Entropy timing. LiteSVM tests against the mainnet-dumped ORE binary and Surfpool fork tests. A Kotlin/Compose app (or Expo with custom Kotlin modules) for the Live Update, QS tile and Glance widget. THREAT_MODEL.md showing that the maximum loss from a compromised executor is bad tile choices plus ≤1% fees.
key_risks: Unverified whether ORE accepts a PDA as Miner/Automation authority for every needed instruction. The fallback is a bond-enforced 'handshake pact', but an SKR bond cannot cover a 300 ORE Motherlode defection.
Gambling optics: mining is currently -EV (production cost ~$104 vs price ~$85). Toly, the security judges and dApp Store review may react badly unless it is framed honestly.
ORE upgrades (v4 changes are still landing) could break CPIs or account layouts mid-judging.
The executor is a hot-key backend. Its worst case is bounded, but it is an operational and uptime risk.
Other Clock In teams are likely building ORE crews, and the ORE prize goes to only one top-10 project.
Tile coordination reduces variance but does not raise EV. Overclaiming it would be caught.
The active ORE miner base is small (~150-165 per round), and ORE's milestone payouts depend on sustained usage metrics.

ideas.name: Ajo
ideas.one_liner: The alajo that can't run away: SGT-verified savings circles where audited on-chain allowances pull contributions, a weekly auction lets whoever needs the pot first pay the others interest, and every completed circle builds a portable credit record tied to your Seeker.
ideas.core_concept: Around a billion people run rotating savings circles: ajo and esusu (Nigeria), chama (Kenya), tanda (Mexico), gye (Korea), tanomoshi-ko (Japan), hui (China), chit funds (India), caixinha and consórcio (Brazil). These are the same markets the Seeker's Upbit listing, Japanese hub and 57 preorder countries point to. Circles fail in two ways: the collector disappears with the money (the alajo who ran away), or a member takes an early pot and stops paying. Ajo fixes the first with code. Members grant the circle a capped, expiring, recurring pull through the Solana Foundation's audited Subscriptions & Allowances program, and a permissionless crank collects each period, so the collector is a program nobody can abscond with. It fixes the second with market design taken from Chinese hui and Indian chit funds. Each round's pot is auctioned by sealed bid. The member who needs money most accepts the largest discount, and that discount is paid as a dividend to everyone still waiting, so savers become lenders at a rate the auction discovers. Early winners post collateral that shrinks as their on-chain Ajo record grows. That record is keyed by SGT mint, so escaping a default means buying a new ~$450 phone. It becomes a sybil-resistant credit history on Solana that any program can read. Crypto-native Seekers get what DeFi never offered: undercollateralised credit from people they trust, priced by auction. Why now: the Allowances program (mainnet since June, audited) finally makes safe pull payments possible, Seeker provides one-device identity, and the dApp Store has zero savings-circle apps.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: the morning jar widget shows '7/8 dropped today · pot $392 · auction Sunday 20:00', plus a gentle nudge if you haven't dropped yet. Action: an optional one-tap 'drop early' with a double-tap before the automatic pull runs. Manual on-time drops earn credit points faster than auto-pulls, so the auto-pull works as a streak freeze, not a replacement. Variable reward: who paid, weekly auction outcomes, your dividend ('+$4.10 because tunde.skr needed rent early') and your credit limit rising. Investment: your Ajo record (circles completed, on-time rate) lowers future collateral and unlocks bigger circles, plus the social obligation of a circle you joined in person. Weekly spike: the live Sunday sealed-bid auction. Without any airdrop, the product is disciplined saving plus access to lump sums and credit.
mobile_native_surfaces: Seed Vault double-tap as the joining ritual (grants the capped allowance) and to seal bids
NFC tap-to-join at in-person meetups, with a fallback to the Google code scanner QR (no camera permission), since NFC on Seeker is unconfirmed
Glance 'jar' widget showing the pot and members' .skr avatars with today's paid status
Ongoing notification during the live auction window; push reminders before pulls (Helius webhooks → FCM)
Haptic sequence on bid reveal
SGT verified on-chain for seats; the credit record is keyed by SGT mint
Circle invites via .skr names and solanadappstore:// deep links
App Shortcut 'Drop early'
ideas.solana_integration: Subscriptions & Allowances program: each member grants the Circle vault PDA a recurring capped pull (amount, period, expiry = circle end). No member has to pre-deposit every contribution, and the audited program enforces the caps. Ajo program (Anchor or Pinocchio) accounts: Circle PDA [circle, creator, nonce] (USDC, period, size, schedule); Seat PDA [seat, circle, sgt_mint] (SGT verified in-program); Round PDA holding sealed bids hash(discount_bps, salt), a reveal window and bid bonds; a per-winner Collateral vault (USDC, or SKR with a haircut); AjoRecord PDA [record, sgt_mint] (circles completed, volume, on-time bps, defaults), writable only by the program and readable by any program via CPI. Instructions: create_circle, join (with the allowance grant), crank_collect (permissionless pull; a failure sets a late flag, then a grace period, then collateral seizure), commit_bid, reveal_bid, settle_round (winner receives the pot minus the discount, and the discount is split pro-rata as dividends), post_collateral, close_circle (returns collateral and updates records). Tie-breaks use Blueshift ecVRF or slot hashes (Switchboard is dead). It has to be on-chain because the collector must be code, the auction must be verifiable by every member, and the credit record must be unforgeable and portable.
ideas.ore_detail: Deliberately none. Putting circle savings into a -EV jackpot mechanic would destroy the trust story that is the product.
ideas.skr_role: SKR as trust collateral. Early-pot winners can post SKR (with a haircut) against their remaining contributions. Every sealed bid carries a small SKR bid bond, forfeited to the circle if the bid is not revealed, which stops commit-and-vanish griefing. SKR becomes the asset that makes strangers creditworthy. It is not staking, not a reward and not checkout currency.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: Six Seekers on a table at a Superteam Nigeria meetup. Each one taps the host's phone (or scans), double-taps once for 'Allowance: $5/day · 8 weeks · capped', and six .skr avatars drop into a glowing jar widget. Cut to Sunday 20:00: sealed bids go in and the phones buzz in turn as bids are revealed. tunde.skr wins at a 6% discount, $392 lands in his wallet, and the other five phones light up with '+$4.70 dividend'. Voiceover: 'In 2009 my mother's alajo vanished with her market savings. This one is a program.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: the auction is a real market for credit, and undercollateralised lending anchored in device-bound identity is new on Solana. Mert: Helius webhooks and Parsed Streams for pull events and notifications. Chase: a real-world format moved on-chain (as TikTok and Tamagotchi were for past winners), with a built-in network effect because every circle recruits 5-20 people. Akshay: it speaks to the international base (gye, tanomoshi, tanda, ajo), gives SKR a collateral utility, and turns the SGT into a credit identity. Beeman: the first consumer mobile use of the Allowances program, plus SGT verified inside a program. Ethelsec: no admin keys, pull caps enforced by an audited program, commit-reveal with salts and bid bonds, checked collateral maths, and a tested default path.
ideas.closest_existing: Kin, a Clock In competitor repo, is very close on the basics: bonded rotating circles, an in-program SGT check, SPL-delegation autopay, a home-screen widget and a 'Kin Score'. Judges will likely see both. Others: a Cardano Catalyst reverse-auction ROSCA prototype, tanda clubs on Arbitrum and Base with defaulter insurance, a Hedera ROSCA, WeTrust (2017), Celo-era esusu/chama apps, and offline chit funds and hui. No Solana auction-ROSCA was found. The differences: auction-priced credit (Kin uses join order or random order), the audited Allowances program instead of raw delegation, collateral that scales with reputation, a CPI-readable credit record keyed by SGT mint as a public primitive, and daily-drip plus weekly-auction event cadence.
ideas.technical_depth: A program with about 14 instructions that CPIs into the Allowances program. Property tests for the auction, dividend and collateral maths. LiteSVM scenarios for late payment, default, collateral seizure and bid griefing. A permissionless crank service. A Kotlin/Expo app with the widget and NFC/QR join. Docs covering the credit-record specification so other apps can build on it.
key_risks: Kin is already in this hackathon with the same core, so judges may read Ajo as a near-duplicate unless the auction and credit record lead the pitch.
Weaker innovation ceiling: ROSCAs on-chain have been tried since 2017.
Sealed-bid auctions add cognitive load for mainstream users.
Regulatory risk: chit funds are regulated in India, and lending and deposit rules differ by country.
Airdrop-conditioned Seeker natives may not want savings circles, and every circle needs a real group to form (cold start).
Mobile SDK maturity of the Subscriptions & Allowances program is untested.
Defaults larger than posted collateral still hurt the other members.

ideas.name: Maigadi
ideas.one_liner: Every compound in Lagos has a gateman, and Maigadi is your wallet's: a Mobile Wallet Adapter firewall between any dApp and Seed Vault that explains every transaction in your own language, blocks drainer patterns and enforces your spending rules before the double-tap.
ideas.core_concept: Drains are the most-cited fear in r/SolanaSeeker, and the dApp Store has no dedicated pre-sign protection app. On Solana, 2026 was marked by Drift's $286M durable-nonce heist and ORE's missing-account-check exploit. Maigadi (Hausa for gateman) registers as an MWA wallet endpoint. You choose it in any dApp's wallet chooser, it opens its own MWA session to Seed Vault Wallet using the same Seed Vault account, and every authorize and sign request passes its checkpoint first. It decodes and simulates each transaction (Helius), and flags what balance-diff previews miss. That includes System Assign owner reassignment, Token SetAuthority, Approve and CloseAccount to foreign destinations, and durable-nonce advance instructions (transactions signed now, used later). It also catches programs upgraded within the last day, signMessage payloads that are really transactions, and dApp identities that fail Digital Asset Links. Users write their own policy: daily outflow caps, a 24-hour cooling-off period for new domains, 'no signing after midnight', a lockdown switch. Maigadi enforces it whichever dApp is asking. A community layer lets SGT-verified Seekers report domains, addresses and programs with an SKR bond. Reports confirmed by on-chain drain evidence pay the reporter, false ones are slashed, and the registry lives on-chain for any wallet to read. You can select any address or link in Telegram or X and get a verdict in two taps. A weekly checkup revokes stale delegations, closes dust accounts and reclaims the excess rent freed by SIMD-0437. Why now: Helius Parsed Streams went GA on Sept 25, 4 KB v1 transactions make blind signing harder to eyeball, Solana Mobile just launched a bug bounty, and two security researchers are judging.

ideas.judge_appeal: Ethelsec: this is their home turf. The threat model covers owner reassignment, durable nonces, identity spoofing and the proxy itself as a target (reproducible build, no key material, no network signing). Mert: Helius simulation, Parsed Streams and webhooks are the engine, and decoding and explanations stay local for privacy. Toly: durable-nonce defense after Drift, and a public on-chain threat registry as ecosystem infrastructure. Chase and Akshay: it attacks the #1 fear holding back Seeker usage and makes every other dApp in the store safer, which is ecosystem impact. A transaction decoder library with a fixture corpus of real Solana drainer transactions (owner reassignment, delegate, durable nonce). lens: HABIT ARCHITECT (Stickiness & PMF first): I started from rituals Seeker owners already have. They lose hours to doomscrolling at work and in bed, they are afraid of drains every time they connect a dApp, they play the office-pool game with friends, and they would like to earn from real demand rather than emissions. For each ritual I made the Seeker's hardware and Solana the load-bearing parts. Every idea passes the no-airdrop test: users spend their own capped money or earn from real counterparties, with no app emissions and no memo check-ins. Two ideas are ORE-core bids for the matched prize (Heads Down, Foreman). Two are ORE-free: Float is a security product with a real SKR mechanic, and Airtime builds on Payment Channels. I dropped a savings-circle idea after checking the competitor repo angelraph/kin. It already ships SKR/USDC bonds, autopay by delegation, on-chain SGT checks, a widget and a Kin Score, so it is a near-duplicate.

ideas.name: Heads Down
ideas.one_liner: Put your Seeker face-down and it mines ORE; pick it up to scroll and the rig stops. Proof of (actual) work.
ideas.core_concept: Heads Down is a focus-and-sleep ritual that turns the Seeker into an ORE rig that only runs while you are not using it. Clock in from the Quick Settings tile or just flip the phone face-down. That starts a Day Shift (deep work), or a Night Shift if the phone is on the charger at bedtime. A Live Update chip starts, and your own non-custodial ORE Automation account deploys each ~78 s round through the app's DiscretionaryBps executor; pick the phone up to scroll and the shift ends on the spot. The app pays no emissions and sends no memo check-ins. You spend your own capped weekly budget, signed once, and ORE's native variable reward is the payoff: tile wins, star solo tiles and the 1/500 Motherlode, each felt as a haptic 'pickaxe thunk' through the desk. The morning alarm is the clock-out, and it opens the overnight haul reveal, a daily variable-reward ritual like pulling up a crab trap. Focus Rooms borrow Forest's plant-together mechanic: friends clock in together, and in a strict room one pickup breaks the shift for everyone, so social pressure does the enforcing rather than the sensors. It targets two needs Seeker owners share with everyone (doomscrolling at work and in bed). It also gives a daily job to the many Seekers that sit in drawers as second phones; SeekerTracker's primary-wallet scan puts most .skr IDs in its dormant bucket, though it undercounts. Why now: ORE has no native app (PWA only), its 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker' card never shipped, and the pitch writes itself: ORE is proof-of-work, and this makes it proof of actual work. It is honest about the economics: with production cost at ~$104 against a ~$85 price, it shows the expected cost per focused hour and a 'buying is cheaper today' banner.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The morning alarm opens the Night Shift haul card (e.g. '312 rounds, 0.041 ORE, missed the Motherlode by one tile at 03:14'). The widget shows the rig's state, and Focus Room invites arrive by push ('ada.skr started a 50-min shift, join?'). ACTION: Usually zero taps: flip the phone face-down, or tap the QS tile once. One Seed Vault double-tap a week refuels the rig. VARIABLE REWARD: Every round resolves as a haptic. Winning tiles, star solo-tile wins and the Motherlode (1/500 per round, roughly two hits a day network-wide) are genuinely random, and the room either completes or breaks. INVESTMENT: A focus-hours ledger keyed to your SGT; a forgiving streak (two auto-applied freezes a month, the Duolingo rule); unrefined ORE earning its share of ORE's 10% refining fee, so holding pays; room history; and rig cosmetics that level up with hours, not spend. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: You have to work and sleep every day regardless, and this makes phone-down time feel productive. Remove ORE and what's left is Forest for crypto people, a weaker product but not a dead one, which is the test for a real habit.
mobile_native_surfaces: Sensor fusion (gravity/accelerometer + proximity + screen/charging state) with a tiny on-device TFLite classifier that tells a real pickup from a desk bump, so shifts don't break falsely

Every shift is an ORE mining session built on ORE's native Automation/executor model: Day Shift runs a live-EV tile strategy that avoids crowded tiles and chooses the split/solo mix, Night Shift runs the conditional Motherlode hunter, and the economics screen shows ORE's buy-and-bury, Reserve and refining yield. It revives at the app layer what ORE advertised and then removed: 'Proof of mobile' and the claim_seeker SGT check. Post-hackathon milestones map directly to ORE's own metrics: active rigs, SOL deployed per day, rounds covered and new miners (today ~150–165 per round). ORE stays the primary featured product in the name, demo and social posts.

SKR works as self-commitment collateral with no shared pool for farmers to game, and it is not staking, a reward or a checkout. Honest caveat: burn-on-fail resembles bozPledge's step pledges, so this is a secondary SKR use, not the headline.

ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: A clean mechanism with no new custody (ORE's own automation, gated by human behaviour) and a meme he will repeat ('proof of actual work'); it uses tx v1 batching and the faster slots. MERT: Helius LaserStream/webhooks power every haptic and widget frame, and every claim in the pitch (shifts, rounds, SOL deployed) is verifiable on-chain, not screenshots. CHASE: Stickiness comes from a universal daily need (focus and sleep) plus a morning variable reward, and it answers 'what does my Seeker do all day?' for dormant owners. It is also the builder's founder story: 'I clocked in 200+ build hours for Clock In with this app; my rig mined while I coded.' AKSHAY/BEEMAN: Nearly every native surface they ask for (Live Update, QS tile, Glance widget, sensors, haptics, alarm, the Seed Vault ritual, SGT verified in-program, .skr, deep links), built on the official MWA stack, and it gives Seeker-exclusive ORE mining a reason to exist. ETHELSEC: Non-custodial by construction (the executor can only deploy within caps or return funds), a session key that cannot move money, SGT verified on-chain rather than by the client, no durable nonces, executor key in KMS, and a written threat model covering the worst case of a compromised executor (a bounded, per-round, capped deploy of the user's own budget).
ideas.closest_existing: Forest (the focus timer with plant-together, one of the best-selling productivity apps) is the format source. Heads Down swaps the virtual tree for real ORE mining with real money at stake. ORE's own Lite/Pro autominer, refinORE, Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer and Radiants' lodestar-cli already automate the grid 24/7 as bots with no ritual; Heads Down is an autominer whose on/off switch is your behaviour. Sleepagotchi (4,269 reviews on Seeker) proves sleep rituals resonate, but it runs on emissions. Solarma (wake-up vault) and bozPledge (stake SKR on steps, burn on miss) share the commitment-penalty DNA of the SKR tax. Tramplin (a MONOLITH winner) proves ORE-like randomness wins with these judges. Brutal truth: strip the ritual away and it is 'an autominer with a timer'. If judges read it as a 'gambling timer', it loses.
ideas.technical_depth: Native Kotlin/Compose app, or Expo SDK 57 with custom Kotlin Expo Modules: ShiftForegroundService, SensorFusion plus a TFLite pickup classifier, Live Update/ProgressStyle notifications, Glance widget, TileService, AlarmClock, a haptic composer, and an MWA clientlib-ktx trampoline. Rust executor service: subscribes to board/round resets via Helius LaserStream and, for each round, builds batched v1 deploy transactions for rigs in an active shift. It includes idempotency per (rig, round), Jito tips, retry without durable nonces, and the key in a KMS/HSM. Pinocchio/Anchor program: in-program SGT verification, Rig/Room/ShiftLog PDAs, SKR commitment escrow with timeout paths, BuryVault plus a permissionless crank. A Codama-generated client from ORE's IDL (there is no official TS SDK). LiteSVM/bankrun tests for SGT spoof attempts (wrong group, wrong authority, zero balance, a moved SGT), escrow timeouts and executor-cap violations. The README carries a threat model and an economics disclosure. Hundreds of granular commits across the program, executor, app and native modules.
key_risks: Gambling optics and negative EV: production cost (~$104) is above price (~$85), so judges or dApp Store reviewers may see a 'gambling timer'; mitigate with budget caps, honest EV display and a 'buy instead' banner

Many Seekers are secondary phones: putting the Seeker face-down doesn't stop doomscrolling on the primary iPhone, so position it as the desk/nightstand rig and Pomodoro companion rather than a screen-time blocker

Executor liveness and cost: a deploy must land every ~78 s for every active rig; this needs tx v1 batching plus the ≤1% bps fee to stay economical, and ORE's frequent 2026 rule changes (V4 tweaks, fee changes) can break the strategy code

Android background limits: Doze, OEM battery killers and foreground-service type rules; the break-signal design helps, but it needs device testing on Seeker. Live Update depends on Seeker's Android 16 build (MR7 per one source; unconfirmed elsewhere)
Focus-app retention historically decays after the novelty wears off; rooms and the morning haul must carry it
The ORE matched prize is discretionary, milestone-paid and requires staying live, and it is only awarded if the app finishes in the Top 10
Sensor gating is spoofable. That is harmless economically (no reward pool, you only cheat yourself), but leaderboards must be spend-neutral or they invite gaming

ideas.name: Float
ideas.one_liner: Clock in with a float, not your vault: a Seeker wallet that holds only today's capped allowance, so a drainer can take $5, never your stack.
ideas.core_concept: Every drain story on r/SolanaSeeker starts the same way: the main Seed Vault wallet connected to a dApp. Float is an MWA wallet that sits between dApps and your vault. Each morning, or on the first dApp connect of the day, one Seed Vault double-tap clocks you in: it grants today's Float key a capped, expiring fixed delegation from your vault through the Solana Foundation's audited Subscriptions & Allowances program (e.g. 25 USDC + 0.2 wSOL, expiring 23:59 local). Float appears in the MWA wallet chooser. When a dApp asks for a signature, Float simulates it, shows a plain-English 'what leaves your wallet' card, and blocks structural drainer patterns (SetAuthority, owner changes, unlimited approvals, durable-nonce tricks). It then pulls just in time only what the transaction needs from the allowance and signs with the day key, with no Seed Vault prompt per transaction, so exploring is faster and safer at once. At night, or instantly from the Quick Settings 'Clock Out' tile, Float sweeps everything back to the vault and the allowance expires, so a stolen key is worth at most today's remaining cap. Herd immunity: when any Float user's simulator catches a malicious transaction, the program or domain is flagged for every Float user within seconds. Flags are one per SGT and backed by an SKR truth bond, which builds the unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' idea from the SKR whitepaper. The same float doubles as a degen's daily loss limit, since it caps what you can lose to a drainer or to yourself today. Why now: the store has zero pre-sign protection apps, drain fear is the community's loudest pain, the allowance program went live in June 2026, and two security researchers are judging.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: Internal and already daily: 'I'm about to do my quests or try a new dApp.' A dApp's MWA connect routes to Float, which asks 'Clock in?'. The widget shows 'Off the clock · vault sealed 63 days'. ACTION: One Seed Vault double-tap sets today's float; then zero per-transaction prompts inside the cap. VARIABLE REWARD: The evening Shift Report: what Float blocked for you today, how many drainers the community flagged, and whether your SKR-bonded flag was upheld. Friday Autopsy is a weekly teardown of the biggest drainer the community caught, with a hunter leaderboard. INVESTMENT: A 'vault sealed' streak (days your vault never touched a dApp); a personal allowlist and per-category float presets; hunter reputation keyed to your SGT mint; and history that makes the simulator smarter for you. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: It answers the fear every owner already has, at the exact moment they already open dApps.

MWA dApp-side call into Seed Vault Wallet for the once-a-day fingerprint + double-tap grant (Float composes with Seed Vault rather than replacing it)
Android Keystore (StrongBox if present) wrapping the day key, with user-auth binding for over-cap requests via BiometricPrompt

Glance widget: float remaining, shield state, 'vault sealed' streak, turning red on an anomaly (FCM pushes driven by Helius webhooks)
Ongoing notification while clocked in with inline 'Clock out' action (deliberately not a Live Update countdown, to stay within Google's rules)
ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT + share target: select any address, .skr name, link or Blink in X or Telegram → 'Check with Float'
Distinct haptic 'danger' pattern and full-screen red sheet when a transaction is blocked
On-device small LLM (LiteRT-LM, CPU) that rewrites simulation diffs into one plain sentence, so previews never go to a third-party AI
SGT verification for flags; .skr names shown in every preview instead of raw addresses
ideas.solana_integration: Subscriptions & Allowances program (De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44, Cantina/Spearbit-audited). A fixed delegation per mint from the vault's program-controlled Subscription Authority to today's Float key, with a cap and expiry; several mints are granted in one tx v1 behind one double-tap. It is SPL/Token-2022 only, so SOL for fees rides as wSOL and is unwrapped just in time. Float program (Pinocchio/Anchor): (1) a DayKey registry PDA [b"float", sgt_mint] binding vault ↔ current key ↔ expiry, so a key can be revoked or rotated and other wallets can recognize a leashed key; (2) ThreatFlag PDAs [b"flag", program_id | domain_hash] holding the reporter's SGT mint, an evidence hash (the simulated tx), an SKR bond escrow and status; (3) a 72 h challenge window: the flagged dApp can dispute by signing with its program upgrade authority or dApp Store publisher key, and unresolved cases go to a jury of top-reputation SGT holders, with bonds slashed or returned. SGT is verified in-program (group GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…, owner = signer). Helius provides simulateTransaction plus Parsed Events for previews, and Parsed Streams/webhooks on the day key and the vault's token accounts detect new delegates or authority changes, triggering an automatic clock-out and a push. Sweeps are day-key-signed transfers back to the vault, plus close-account rent reclaim. It must be on-chain because the leash (cap, expiry) is enforced by an audited program even if Float's own app is compromised, and a public, sybil-resistant flag registry is a public good that Seed Vault Wallet or Phantom could read.
ideas.ore_detail: Deliberately ORE-free. Bolting ORE onto a security product would dilute both the trust story and the 'ORE must be primary' rule.
ideas.skr_role: Truth bonds: to flag a program or domain as a drainer, a hunter posts an SKR bond with evidence. If the flag is upheld after the challenge window, the bond comes back along with a share of a sponsor-funded bounty pool and reputation. A false flag is slashed to the disputing dApp. This is SKR as skin in the game for security curation, a direct build of the whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators'. It is not staking (it is a claim-specific bond, never yield), not pay-with-SKR and not an emission. Avoid the word 'stake' everywhere.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0:00 Straight to camera on a real Seeker: 'I'm about to get drained. On purpose.' 0:03 Connect to a red-team 'free mint' dApp (the team's own mainnet contract, tiny amounts). Float's sheet turns red with a danger haptic: 'This gives 7xK… permanent control of your USDC.' Tap 'Sign anyway (demo).' 0:09 The float is gone: -$4.80. Split screen: the vault still shows $12,000, untouched. 0:13 Swipe down, tap the 'Clock out' tile; the sweep lands in under a second and the widget flips to 'Vault sealed'. 0:17 A second Seeker on the table buzzes: 'Flagged by ade.skr 6 s ago · bonded 5,000 SKR.' Line: 'Your Seeker should expect to get drained, and survive it.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: It uses brand-new, audited Foundation primitives for the thing that most blocks mainstream use (signing fear), and it limits the blast radius by construction rather than by detection. MERT: Helius simulation, Parsed Events and Parsed Streams are the backbone; the flag registry is exactly the kind of public-good data layer an RPC company likes to serve; privacy-respecting on-device explanations. CHASE: It solves the most-voiced pain on r/SolanaSeeker and makes the quest-and-explore crowd, the store's most active users, safer every day. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: A new 'sign once a day' pattern that respects MWA's no-background-signing rule, both wallet-side and dApp-side MWA work (Beeman maintains wallet-ui), SGT used as sybil resistance for curation, and it fits the upcoming 'Privacy & Security' dApp Spotlight theme. ETHELSEC: A hot key on an on-chain leash is a concrete threat model they can attack. It carries a README with attacker capabilities per compromised component, daily or weekly key rotation, no durable nonces, simulation plus structural blocks, and in-program SGT checks, and it is their home turf.
ideas.closest_existing: Phantom/Solflare/Backpack already warn on malicious dApps and simulate transactions (Phantom absorbed Blowfish). Float's edge is the structural cap, not better detection, and in a straight detection comparison Phantom wins. Seed Vault Wallet (the default MWA wallet) has no allowance leash. RugLens (token risk scanner, 340 reviews) and SIMGUARD (1 review) are the only security apps in the store. Clock In competitors nuntius/mandatum (capped, revocable recurring payments granted in Seed Vault) and Veto (spending mandates for agents) use the same primitive family for different jobs. Many owners already keep manual burner wallets; Float automates the burner, puts it on a leash and makes it social. Solana Mobile or Phantom could ship native spending limits and erase the gap.
ideas.technical_depth: The repo shows a full Kotlin MWA wallet (walletlib) and an MWA dApp client in one app, including an association and trust UI. It has Keystore-wrapped key management with rotation, and a simulation-and-explainer engine that turns Helius simulation into balance and authority diffs, with rule-based structural blocks and optional on-device LLM wording. It builds just-in-time funding transactions and a sweep/close-accounts engine. The Anchor/Pinocchio program has in-program SGT verification, the DayKey registry, a ThreatFlag registry with SKR bond escrow, a challenge/dispute state machine and jury resolution. The backend runs Helius webhooks → anomaly rules → FCM, plus the flag propagation service. A red-team drainer contract and test suite prove the cap holds (drain attempts beyond the allowance fail on-chain), alongside LiteSVM tests for the bond and dispute logic and fuzzing of the transaction parser. SECURITY.md sets out a per-component compromise analysis.
key_risks: Being a wallet is hard: users must pick Float in the chooser, and dApps key accounts by address, so rotating keys breaks game and DeFi continuity (use stable weekly identities; LP positions can't be swept)
Unverified allowance details: SOL needs wSOL wrapping, delegate self-revoke semantics and the exact fixed-delegation UX must be tested on mainnet
A compromised OS can still steal today's float and can phish an 'increase cap' prompt; users must be trained that Float never needs more than one double-tap a day
Flag governance is genuinely hard: SKR-holder collusion, griefing of legit dApps, possible defamation risk, and who pays bounties without it becoming an 'earn SKR' farm
Insurance-like value is felt only when something goes wrong, so the daily clock-in may feel like a chore; stickiness rests on the float also being the explorer's fastest signing path
Phantom, Solflare or Seed Vault Wallet could ship native spending limits or leashed sub-accounts
Heavy scope for a solo builder: wallet-side MWA plus a program plus threat intel

ideas.name: Foreman
ideas.one_liner: Follow-the-sun ORE crews: the rig only runs while someone is on shift, and whoever is on shift calls the dig for the whole crew.
ideas.core_concept: Foreman is a social ORE mining game for crews of 3–8 friends spread across time zones. Every member keeps their own non-custodial ORE Automation account with a fixed daily budget, and appoints the crew's executor so all the crew's rigs deploy together as one crew rig. The crew rig only runs while someone is clocked in as Foreman. The Foreman makes 'the call': they pick tiles on a live heatmap (crowded vs empty, split vs star solo tiles), set a Motherlode threshold and choose the pace, and every member's rig follows within that member's own caps. Shifts hand off around the world like a relay (Lagos → London → New York → Seoul): 'tunde.skr clocked out, +0.42 ORE on his watch. You're up.' Budgets are fixed per day, so more coverage does not mean more spend. Coverage only means more exposure to a Motherlode that hits at a random time, which turns '24/7 coverage' into a real team objective rather than a spending treadmill. Motherlode Watch alerts every member when the jackpot passes a crew-set level (e.g. 300 ORE) and the crew goes all hands. Friday Crew Wars ranks crews on ORE mined per SOL, a partly skill-based metric because avoiding crowded tiles matters; winners get an on-chain trophy, not a pot. The format is the office lottery pool, the fantasy-league commissioner and a relay team, applied to ORE's 78-second heartbeat. Today that heartbeat is played by ~150–165 miners a round and a handful of bots, with no social layer at all.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The handoff push from the previous foreman, plus the widget's 24-hour crew ring showing who is on, the live board with crew avatars on the called tiles, and the Motherlode meter. Motherlode Watch pushes are rare and urgent. ACTION: Clock in from the QS tile or widget, do one Seed Vault double-tap to sign today's call and top-up, then a 10-second call on the heatmap. VARIABLE REWARD: A haptic reveal every ~78 s, your call's hit rate against every other foreman, solo-tile wins, and Motherlode hits landing on your shift, plus the crew's reactions in the feed. INVESTMENT: The crew coverage streak, where a missed shift can be covered by any sub (a social streak freeze) and two free gaps a month; your foreman record (hit rate, ORE per SOL); crew banner and trophies; unrefined ORE earning refining share; and an auto-generated crew feed where every call and outcome becomes a post, Fomo-style, with no posting burden. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: Your crew is counting on you to take the next shift, and your call is on the record.
mobile_native_surfaces: Jetpack Glance widget: 24-hour crew ring (who's on, next handoff) plus a live 5x5 board with crew avatars, updated via FCM
Quick Settings tile 'Clock in as Foreman' launching the MWA trampoline Activity
Android 16 Live Update while on duty (user-initiated, ongoing, like a delivery): 'Foreman · 41 rounds · crew +0.18 ORE'
Notification actions: 'Cover shift' / 'Go all hands' straight from the Motherlode Watch push
Synchronized haptics on every crew member's phone at round reveal
Seed Vault fingerprint + double-tap as the daily 'sign the call' ritual
On-chain SGT seats (one device, one seat) and .skr names on the board
dApp Store deep-link crew invites (solanadappstore://details?id=…) plus QR join in person
App Shortcuts ('Make the call', 'Crew feed')
ideas.solana_integration: ORE program oreV3EG1…: each member has their own Automation account (executor = the crew executor, DiscretionaryBps ≤100 bps, per-tile and per-day caps set by that member), with deploys and partial claims. There is no pooled custody anywhere. Foreman program (Pinocchio/Anchor): a Crew PDA; Seat PDAs [b"seat", crew, sgt_mint] created after in-program SGT verification, holding each member's caps and a follow/veto flag; and a Call PDA per shift signed by the on-duty foreman (tile mask, per-round amount, Motherlode min, expiry). The executor may only deploy what matches the posted call, so anyone can diff the executor's deploys against the on-chain calls, which makes executor honesty publicly auditable. There is also a CoverageLog, and a Season PDA for Crew Wars scored from on-chain deploys and claims (indexed with Helius Parsed Events). SKR dues and tips route to a BuryVault, and a crank swaps them to ORE via Jupiter and buries them at ORE's grams address. The daily call plus top-up is one tx v1 behind one double-tap, and the executor batches every crew's deploys into 4 KB v1 transactions. Helius LaserStream on round resets fans out to FCM so four phones on four continents buzz within a second of each other. It must be on-chain because funds never leave members' own ORE accounts, calls are verifiable commitments, and seats are sybil-proof by SGT mint.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the game: every crew action is an ORE deploy, call or claim through ORE's native Automation/executor model, including its split/solo tiles, conditional Motherlode deployments and refining fee. It is the first social consumer layer for ORE and turns ORE's ~150–165 miners per round into crews that recruit crews. The usage metrics the matched prize's milestones will likely ask for (miners, SOL deployed, retention) are what a crew game grows by design. Seeker-only seats also deliver ORE's abandoned 'Proof of mobile' idea.
ideas.skr_role: SKR is the crew's social currency. Members tip the foreman in SKR when a call hits, paid to their .skr name. Crew Wars entry dues are paid in SKR, and 100% of them are swapped to ORE and buried, so the prize is status (an on-chain trophy), not a pot, and there is no wagering on top of mining. Honest: tips and dues are thin SKR uses that would not win the SKR prize on their own; this is a flavor layer.

You're up.' She double-taps (Seed Vault sheet visible) and taps four tiles on the heatmap. 0:08 Within a second, the other three widgets update with her avatar on those tiles. 0:12 The round resolves and all four phones thud in sync; one lands on a winning tile: 'Crew +0.21 ORE · minji.skr's call.' 0:16 The Lagos phone's widget ring fills to 24/24 covered hours. Line: 'The rig never sleeps. Your crew takes shifts.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: A consumer layer for ORE with zero new custody, and an elegant trick in making executor behaviour auditable against on-chain calls. MERT: Sub-second fan-out from LaserStream to phones across continents, and Crew Wars computed from Parsed Events: Helius visibly doing real work. CHASE: The strongest retention mechanic in consumer apps is someone waiting on you; crews invite crews, which is a credible first-10k-users path inside a fixed ~120k-owner base. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: Widget, QS tile, Live Update, synchronized haptics, SGT seats verified in-program, .skr names, deep-link invites, and the daily double-tap as a ritual. ETHELSEC: Members' funds only ever sit in their own ORE Automation accounts; the executor is bounded by per-member caps and by posted calls; SGT seats resist sybils; no key export; a documented executor threat model.
ideas.closest_existing: ORE's own app (solo, stale on Seeker since Oct 2025) and its PWA, plus the bot autominers refinORE, Minemore/Orestack and Oreminer, all solitary. Radiants' lodestar-cli already offers EV heatmaps for tile choice. Evore offers managed miners. Old ORE v1/v2 mining pools pooled hashpower, a mechanic made obsolete by the grid. Tramplin (a MONOLITH winner) proves social lottery mechanics win with these judges. Lottery syndicates and fantasy leagues are the Web2 formats. Brutal truth: 'ORE crews' is the most obvious ORE idea and appears in every research file, so other Clock In teams are probably building a version. The defensible parts are the relay/foreman ritual and the auditable calls, not 'crews' itself.
ideas.technical_depth: The repo contains a Rust executor (a LaserStream subscriber, per-round batched v1 deploys across crews, idempotency per (seat, round), call-conformance checks before signing, a KMS-held key, Jito tips, no durable nonces). It has a Pinocchio/Anchor program with in-program SGT verification, Crew/Seat/Call/CoverageLog/Season PDAs, cap enforcement and a bury crank; a Codama client from ORE's IDL; and a Kotlin app with a Glance widget, TileService, Live Update, synchronized-haptics scheduling and a feed. An indexer turns Parsed Events into the crew feed and Crew Wars scores. Tests cover the failure cases: a foreman exceeding a member's cap, a stale call, a moved or spoofed SGT, and an executor deploying off-call (detected and alerted).
key_risks: Crews need 3–8 friends who each own a Seeker, which is hard with ~9k scattered DAU. Allow non-Seeker Android guests (no SGT seat) or match strangers into crews, which weakens the social bond
Gambling-with-friends optics and negative EV. Fixed daily budgets and status-only Crew Wars mitigate, but judges may still frown
A crowded ORE lane: the matched prize goes to only one Top-10 ORE integration, and other teams will build crews
A bad foreman call wastes friends' budgets (within caps), a source of social friction that can break crews
Executor liveness and cost, plus ORE rule churn (V4 changes through 2026), as for any automation client
Stickiness depends on crew health; a crew that loses two members dies, so crew merging and matchmaking need to be built

ideas.name: Airtime
ideas.one_liner: Ten minutes a day talking to a verified Seeker in another country, paid by the second over Solana Payment Channels: Duolingo's habit, Cambly's humans, instant USDC payouts to 57 countries.
ideas.core_concept: Duolingo proved language practice is a daily habit (~52.7M DAU), and Cambly, Preply and HelloTalk proved people will pay to talk to real native speakers. Their tutors in Lagos, Manila or Hanoi, though, lose large platform cuts, wait for payout minimums, and in Nigeria can't even receive PayPal. Airtime is a 10-minutes-a-day voice practice app where every tutor is an SGT-verified Seeker owner (a real human on a real device: no bots, no catfish) and learners pay by the second. One Seed Vault double-tap a week grants a capped 'airtime' allowance to an in-app session wallet. That wallet opens a Payment Channel to each tutor as needed and, as the channel's authorized_signer, streams 50-byte Ed25519 vouchers every second of the call with no prompts. The tutor settles once, instantly, in USDC. In Tandem mode two learners teach each other (5 minutes each way) over two channels, so balanced exchanges cost close to nothing net. After every call, on-device Whisper transcribes and a small local LLM returns three corrections and five new words into a spaced-repetition deck, the Duolingo layer that brings you back tomorrow even without a call. For Seeker owners it is the first 'earn' app funded by real demand rather than emissions: teach Yoruba, Korean or Portuguese from your phone. Learners can join from any Android wallet, which widens demand beyond the ~120k Seekers. Why now: Payment Channels went live on mainnet on Sept 3, 2026, audited, and no consumer mobile app uses them yet.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: The widget reads '🔥 23-day streak · 4 Korean speakers online · 12 words to review'. There is a daily reminder at your chosen time, and on the tutor side a push: 'A learner wants 10 min of Yoruba now · $0.15/min' (full-screen incoming-call UI). ACTION: Tap a face on the widget and the call starts; no signature is needed because the weekly allowance and channel already exist. Or do a 2-minute review of the deck. VARIABLE REWARD: Who you meet (a verified human from another country), the corrections you get, a live earnings ticker for tutors, and occasional tips. INVESTMENT: The streak (with freezes), a personal vocabulary deck built from your own mistakes, favourite partners, tutor ratings and repeat learners (reputation keyed to SGT mint), and prepaid airtime. WITHOUT AN AIRDROP: Learners come back because they are getting better at a language they need. Tutors come back because a real person is paying them real USDC.
mobile_native_surfaces: Microphone + WebRTC voice in a foreground service (type microphone/phoneCall) with Android Telecom ConnectionService: native incoming-call UI and full-screen intent for tutors
Android 16 Live Update during the call (user-initiated ongoing call, an allowed category): 'minji.skr · 03:12 · $0.29' ticking on the lock screen and status bar
Glance widget: streak, who's online in your target language, review-deck count; one tap to call a favourite
Quick Settings tile 'Go online as tutor' (with availability subtitle)
On-device Whisper speech-to-text (react-native-executorch on Vulkan, or LiteRT on CPU) plus a small local LLM (Gemma-class via LiteRT-LM) for private post-call corrections
Seed Vault fingerprint + double-tap as the weekly 'top up your airtime' ritual
SGT verification for tutors (verified supply), .skr names as profiles, App Shortcuts to favourite partners, haptic on connect/settle
ideas.solana_integration: Payment Channels program CHNLxYvVA28MJP9PrFuDXccuoGXAx7jBacfLEkahyGsX (Cantina-audited). One channel per learner→tutor pair, opened lazily; the channel PDA is derived from payer, payee, mint (USDC), authorized_signer, salt and open_slot. The session key is the authorized_signer and signs cumulative-amount vouchers (magic, channel_id, cumulative_amount, expires_at) each second over the WebRTC data channel. The tutor's app verifies each voucher and keeps only the latest, then calls settle / settle_and_seal / distribute at hang-up or batched daily, returning the refund and reclaiming rent. request_close with a grace period handles a learner who vanishes. Subscriptions & Allowances program (De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44): the weekly fixed delegation from the Seed Vault wallet to the session wallet is the leash, so a compromised phone can lose at most this week's airtime cap. Airtime program (Pinocchio/Anchor): Speaker PDA [b"speaker", sgt_mint] after in-program SGT verification (languages, rate, reputation), and CallAttestation records co-signed by both session keys at settle, which build tamper-proof ratings and no-show evidence. Helius webhooks on settlements feed tutor earnings pushes. It must be on-chain because per-second billing with no minimums and instant cross-border payouts only works with off-chain vouchers backed by an on-chain escrow, and verified-human supply needs SGT checks the app can't fake.
ideas.ore_detail: Deliberately ORE-free. The value is USDC for human time; adding ORE would read as bolted on.
ideas.skr_role: Secondary. Tutors post a small SKR show-up bond to go online, slashed to the learner on a verified no-show or drop (both sides' co-signed call logs), and learners can tip in SKR after a great call. USDC stays the unit of account. Honest: this would not win the SKR prize by itself.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0:00 A Lagos kitchen at 07:00 on a real Seeker; the widget reads 'minji.skr (Seoul) online · Korean'. Tap. 0:04 The call connects with a haptic. Lock the phone: the lock-screen Live Update chip reads 'Minji · 00:41 · $0.06', ticking every second. 0:09 Cut to Minji's Seeker in Seoul: 'earning $0.09/min', ticking in sync. 0:13 Hang up: '612 payments. 1 transaction. Minji paid $0.92 in 0.4 s.' Solscan shows a single settle transaction. 0:17 The post-call card, transcribed on-device in airplane mode: three corrections, five new words, streak 🔥 24.
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: The first consumer product on the Foundation's new Payment Channels (plus Allowances), which puts the payments and per-second-settlement thesis in a human product rather than an agent demo. MERT: Settlement pushes and indexing through Helius; millions of off-chain payments backed by a handful of verifiable on-chain settles, and on-device AI that keeps voice data private. CHASE: A proven Web2 daily habit (Duolingo streaks plus human tutors), and an earn loop funded by demand, not SKR emissions, which is exactly what Solana Mobile's grants page says it wants. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: SGT-verified humans, .skr profiles, Telecom integration, Live Update, on-device ML, and it plays to the international Seeker base (57 countries, Korea/Japan/Brazil/Nigeria communities). ETHELSEC: authorized_signer session keys bounded by a weekly allowance, cumulative vouchers with expiry (no replay), grace-period closes, in-program SGT checks, and co-signed call attestations against fake ratings.
ideas.closest_existing: Cambly, Preply and italki (paid tutoring with platform cuts and payout minimums), HelloTalk and Tandem (free exchange, with well-known bot and catfish problems), Duolingo (AI, now AI video calls, but no humans), and Clarity.fm/Intro (pay-per-minute experts). In crypto: Cherry paid DMs (a message, not time), x402/MPP sessions (machine-to-machine, same channel primitive), and Streamflow/Zebec (streaming payroll, on-chain per stream, not per-second vouchers on mobile). None does per-second paid human calls on mobile. Brutal truth: this is a two-sided marketplace where crypto is the payout rail, and judges may ask 'why is this a Seeker app?'
ideas.technical_depth: The repo contains a Kotlin app with WebRTC (LiveKit or a self-hosted SFU), a Telecom ConnectionService, a foreground service, a voucher engine (a Kotlin port of the 50-byte Ed25519 voucher, since official clients are TS/Rust only), tutor-side verification and settlement batching, allowance and channel lifecycle management (lazy open, top-up, forced close), and an on-device ASR+LLM pipeline with a spaced-repetition scheduler. It has an Anchor/Pinocchio program with SGT verification, speaker profiles, co-signed attestations and an SKR bond. The backend handles matchmaking (language × timezone × availability), abuse reporting and moderation, and Helius settlement webhooks → FCM. Tests cover voucher replay and overspend, a learner vanishing mid-call (request_close path), and allowance-cap exhaustion.
key_risks: Two-sided liquidity: tutors must be online when learners want them, and ~9k Seeker DAU are scattered across time zones, so it needs scheduled 'office hours' and non-Seeker learners
Seeker-community resonance is uncertain: owners are crypto-native farmers, not language learners; the pitch must lead with 'earn from real demand'
Heavy scope: real-time voice, moderation and safety for strangers on voice calls, matching, payments and on-device AI, all for a solo builder
Channel economics for many small pairs (open cost, rent, settle frequency) need tuning; per-pair opens mean the session wallet does many on-chain opens
On-device Whisper/LLM speed on the Dimensity 7300 is unmeasured; a fallback of server ASR hurts the privacy story
Tax and regulatory questions for tutor income, and USDC off-ramp friction in some countries
Judges may classify it as a generic consumer app that happens to use crypto rather than a Seeker-native product

lens: PRIZE STACKER, ORE-CORE. In each idea ORE is the engine and the primary product featured, so each qualifies for the ORE matched prize. Each also gives SKR a distinct non-staking role and is built to compete for 1st overall on the 4x25% rubric. My conviction order is SHIFT, FOREMAN, STASH, MELT.

ideas.name: SHIFT: Proof of Work, literally
ideas.one_liner: Clock in on your Seeker and your focus becomes hashrate: an ORE rig that mines only while you are actually working, with your crew's SKR on the line if anyone breaks.
ideas.core_concept: SHIFT turns ORE's hard-hat miner identity into a daily work ritual: your Seeker mines only while you are working. You clock in from a Quick Settings tile with one Seed Vault double-tap. That signature funds a capped ORE Automation on your own account whose executor is SHIFT's on-chain program, and it registers a hardware-bound Android Keystore key for the session. While you stay focused (screen off, or only allow-listed apps open), the phone signs a tiny heartbeat every ~78-second ORE round. A permissionless cranker submits it, the program verifies it on-chain through the secp256r1 precompile, and only then deploys your SOL to the live board. Open TikTok and the rig stops. Crews of 2-8 Seekers run synchronized shifts with SKR bonds: break focus and your bond goes to the crewmates who held on. This is Forest's 'Plant Together' with real, hardware-verified stakes. Clock-out is the reveal: rounds mined, tile hits, ORE earned and Motherlode near-misses, and a Night Shift mode mines while the phone sleeps face-down on the charger. It is aimed at the crypto-native Seeker owner who doomscrolls charts all day, and it puts Solana Mobile's own Seeker Summer line, 'Less scrolling. More seeking.', into practice. Why now: DiscretionaryBps (Aug 2026) makes a program-controlled executor possible, 250 ms slots and 4 KB v1 transactions make per-round cranking cheap, Seeker's Android 16 build enables lock-screen Live Updates, and ORE advertised 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker' but removed claim_seeker without ever shipping it.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: a morning widget and notification ('Crew shift 09:00, 3/4 clocked in, Motherlode 312 ORE'), with the Clock In tile always one swipe away in the shade. ACTION: swipe down, tap 'Clock In', do one Seed Vault double-tap (the day's only signature), put the phone face-down. VARIABLE REWARD: rounds resolve silently on the lock-screen chip (split-tile hits, solo-tile wins, and the Motherlode possible in any round at 1/500). Clock-out animates every round's winning tile with haptics, and crewmates' forfeited SKR bonds sometimes pay you. INVESTMENT: an on-chain hours-mined ledger, a forgiving weekly streak (5 of 7 days with auto-freezes), crew rank, and unclaimed ORE that earns refining-fee share the longer you hold it ('overtime pay'), all tied to your SGT and hardware key. NO-AIRDROP TEST: remove every token and it is still Forest-with-friends, a focus timer with social stakes, which is a proven daily habit.
mobile_native_surfaces: Quick Settings tile 'Clock In / Clock Out' (TileService + startActivityAndCollapse into a translucent MWA trampoline Activity)

Android 16 Live Update (NotificationCompat.ProgressStyle, setRequestPromotedOngoing): shift time, rounds mined and crew status on the lock screen, always-on display and status-bar chip. It is user-initiated like a workout, so it follows Google's rules.

Seed Vault side-button double-tap + fingerprint via MWA (clientlib-ktx 2.0.3), exactly once per day
Auto Do-Not-Disturb during shifts (notification policy access)
Haptics: a soft tick per mined round, Android 16 envelope haptics for the clock-out reveal and Motherlode
App Shortcuts ('25-min shift', 'Night shift') and dApp Store deep-link crew invites
SGT verified on-chain + .skr names for crewmates
Optional NFC desk-tag clock-in via AAR, runtime-gated because Seeker NFC is unconfirmed
ideas.solana_integration: shift_rig program (Anchor). (1) register_seeker: verifies the SGT on-chain (Token-2022 mint, TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89nU4iWFkNXj1Bw6uYhJJWDRPpShHt4Bk8f99Te, mint authority GT2zuHVaZQYZSyQMgJPLzvkmyztfyXg2NJunqFp4p3A4, amount 1, holder == signer) and creates Seeker PDA [b'seeker', sgt_mint]. It rebinds when the SGT moves between the user's own wallets. This is the first public on-chain SGT verifier. (2) open_shift (the daily Seed Vault tx): sets the user's own ORE Automation (authority = user) to strategy DiscretionaryBps with executor = SHIFT's executor PDA (fee e.g. 50 bps; ORE enforces <=100) and caps amount, and creates Shift PDA [b'shift', seeker, id] holding the device P-256 pubkey, expiry, per-round cap, total budget and a monotonic counter. (3) crank: permissionless. The tx carries a secp256r1 precompile instruction over (program id, shift PDA, ORE round id, counter, focused=1). The program introspects the instructions sysvar (checks the offsets point inside that instruction and match the expected key and message), checks owners and addresses of the ORE Board/Round accounts and the current round, then invoke_signed calls ORE deploy with the executor PDA as signer. v1 txs batch several users per crank. (4) CrewShift PDA escrows SKR bonds (mint SKRbvo6Gf7GondiT3BbTfuRDPqLWei4j2Qy2NPGZhW3) and settles forfeits from recorded heartbeat coverage, with no admin key. SOL never enters SHIFT custody: it sits in the user's ORE Automation, ORE accrues to the user's ORE miner account, and the user can always close the automation through ORE's own path. Why on-chain: the rig must be provably non-custodial and gated by heartbeats, bond forfeits must be trustless, and one-device-one-seat must be enforced by a program, not a server.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is both the engine and the reward. Every focused round is a real deploy on the live 5x5 board: split and solo tiles, with the Motherlode at 1/500 (about two hits a day, ~312 ORE today). It uses Automation (one signature per session), DiscretionaryBps with SHIFT's executor PDA, conditions (min Motherlode for Night Shift, max production-cost EMA), reload of SOL winnings, partial claims, and refining-fee share for unclaimed ORE. It revives ORE's shelved 'Proof of mobile' card and the removed claim_seeker instruction as on-chain SGT verification plus hardware-attested phone keys. Crews can vote to swap forfeited bonds to ORE and send it to the grams bury address. The expected cost is shown before every shift: at ~$104 production cost vs ~$85 price, each $1 of SOL burned buys about $0.82 of ORE in expectation. Most deployed SOL comes back each round (89.1% on losing tiles, 99% on the winning tile), so a 50-minute shift at 0.002 SOL/round burns only ~0.008 SOL. Proposed matched-prize milestones: SGT-verified miners, shifts per day, and SOL deployed to the board.
ideas.skr_role: The SKR role is a crew focus bond: the stake in a hardware-verified commitment contest, which is the pattern that won MONOLITH's SKR prize for Seek. It is not used as a currency or reward. Crewmates escrow, say, 5,000 SKR each for a synchronized shift. The program settles from on-chain heartbeat coverage: members who held get their bond back plus a pro-rata share of forfeits, or the crew can vote to 'bury' forfeits (SKR to ORE, sent to the grams address). There is no staking, no pay-with-SKR and no earn-SKR leaderboard.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: 8:59am, a real Seeker on a desk. Swipe down, tap the 'Clock In' tile, Seed Vault sheet, side-button double-tap + fingerprint, screen off. 5-12s: the lock screen shows the Live Update chip ('On shift 00:00:14, Round 1, Crew 4/4') and a soft haptic tick as the first deploy lands, with a small explorer overlay. 12-17s: a crewmate's Seeker opens X; her screen flashes 'Leaving the mine? 5,000 SKR bond, 3 crewmates still underground' and she backs out. 17-20s: the clock-out reveal flips 38 tiles with haptics: '+0.047 ORE, 3 tile hits, Motherlode missed by one tile'. Title card: 'ORE brought back proof-of-work. We made it literal.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: a memorable meme ('proof of work, literally') backed by real mechanism design: hardware P-256 keys verified with the secp256r1 precompile, no hot wallet on the phone at all (the P-256 key can't even pay fees), and 250 ms slots plus 4 KB v1 transactions used in the crank.
