MERT: Helius LaserStream/Parsed Streams drive round events to FCM to the Live Update, and Sender lands cranks. It is also privacy-preserving: the chain learns one signed 'focused' bit per round, never which apps you use. CHASE: an open-source executor program and cranker other ORE and Seeker apps can reuse, with clean Anchor code and tests. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: about as Seeker-native as a loop gets: QS tile, Live Update, Glance widget, Seed Vault as a once-a-day ritual, SGT verified on-chain and keyed by mint, .skr crews, a correct MWA trampoline (passes AlignAI's connect/sign/rejection checks), and one natural value-moving tx per day instead of memo spam, echoing 'Less scrolling. More seeking.' ETHELSEC: funds stay in ORE's own Automation under user authority, and the executor PDA can only deploy within caps and never withdraw. Heartbeats are bound to program, round id and counter against replay, precompile offsets are validated, the SKR escrow has no admin key, and there's a written threat model, a verifiable build and a multisig+timelock upgrade authority.
ideas.closest_existing: Forest (Web2 focus app with 'Plant Together'); 'Forest Focus', a React Native Forest clone for Seeker with a SOL 'revive' fee and planned token rewards (forest-focus-web.lovable.app); Time Miner (focus minutes to virtual resources); Solarma (SOL-staked wake-up vault, devnet); stickK/Beeminder (commitment contracts); Moonwalk and bozPledge (stake-on-steps); Sleepagotchi (sleep-to-earn); the stale official ORE app and the Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer and refinORE autominers, which automate deploys with no human loop. SHIFT differs because the reward is real ORE mining on the live board, gated round by round on-chain by a hardware-bound heartbeat (not an app-side timer or a revive fee), and crew SKR bonds settle trustlessly. Weak spot: at a glance it can read as 'Forest + crypto', so the demo must open with the lock-screen mining chip and the on-chain heartbeat.
ideas.technical_depth: (1) shift_rig Anchor program: Token-2022 SGT extension parsing, Seeker/Shift/CrewShift PDAs, executor-PDA CPI into ORE deploy via the ore-api crate, secp256r1 instruction-sysvar introspection, and SKR bond escrow and settlement. Tested with LiteSVM/Mollusk unit tests, Surfpool mainnet-fork integration tests against the real ORE program, and Trident fuzzing of settlement math. (2) Rust cranker: Helius LaserStream for round resets, batched v1 txs via Helius Sender. It is open source so anyone can crank, and its fee-payer key holds only fee SOL and can neither move user funds nor choose tiles (the program derives the mask). (3) Kotlin/Compose app: clientlib-ktx MWA with a Keystore-encrypted auth-token cache and assetlinks identity, TileService, Glance, Live Updates, foreground focus service, Keystore key generation + attestation, haptics. An optional on-device LiteRT-LM 'shift coach' summarises focus patterns locally, which hedges the Align 'AI' criterion. (4) Small backend: SIWS single-use nonces, attestation-chain verification, FCM fan-out. Docs: threat model, invariants, Squads multisig + timelock upgrade authority, solana-verify reproducible build. Many granular commits across program, app and cranker.
key_risks: Using a PDA as the DiscretionaryBps executor via CPI is unproven. deploy.rs only checks that executor == signer, but any first-deploy costs the signer pays must work from a system-owned PDA. Prove it on a mainnet fork in week 1, or fall back to a scoped hot executor key with tiny caps.
Focus detection can be spoofed on rooted or modded devices. Keystore attestation raises the bar but is not TEEPIN-grade, so keep bonds small and flag attestation failures.
Mining is negative-EV today (production cost ~$104 > price ~$85) and carries jackpot optics. Show the expected cost before every shift and never call it yield.

Android background limits: a foreground service signing every ~78 s for hours (Night Shift) costs battery and runs into FGS-type rules. Live Updates depend on Seeker's Android 16 build (check at runtime).
ORE is upgradeable and changed monthly in 2026, so a program change can break the CPI. Pin ore-api and run nightly fork tests.
Crank economics for tiny deploys: 5,000-lamport fees against a <=1% fee on 0.002 SOL, so many users must be batched per v1 tx.
A Forest clone already exists on Seeker, and judges may pattern-match unless the ORE mechanic leads the demo.
secp256r1 precompile activation on mainnet and StrongBox availability on Seeker must be verified on-device.

ideas.name: FOREMAN: mining co-ops where luck is shared and skill is scored
ideas.one_liner: Seeker crews pool into one ORE rig that covers the board, so they collect ORE nearly every round and share every Motherlode. Each member clocks in for a daily 5-minute foreman shift, steering it live with no wallet pop-ups and scored on skill, not luck.
ideas.core_concept: Solo ORE mining with small amounts of SOL is a lottery; mining pools exist because pooling turns variance into a steady wage. FOREMAN is a Seeker-only mining co-op: 5-50 SGT-verified members deposit SOL into a program-owned, share-accounted co-op vault. The vault's ORE rig spreads across most or all 25 tiles, so ORE drips in almost every round and every Motherlode hit (about two a day) is split pro-rata among members. The social core is the rotating foreman shift. Each member gets a daily 5-minute slot to steer the co-op live on a 120 Hz board, tilting allocation toward under-deployed tiles in the final seconds of a round, which is the real EV edge in ORE's split/solo design. Every tap is signed by a hardware Keystore key and lands on-chain in about a second without a wallet prompt. The program computes each foreman's 'EV alpha' against a uniform baseline from ORE's own round data, a skill score that luck can't move. Co-ops challenge each other to weekly SKR skill duels settled on EV alpha, not on who got lucky, and when the Motherlode hits the co-op every member's phone quakes at once. It serves ORE's existing ~150 miners, who want less variance, and Seeker friend groups who want a social game that isn't a casino. Why now: DiscretionaryBps executors (Aug 2026), 250 ms slots that make last-second human calls feasible, and 4 KB v1 transactions that fit a verified call plus a 25-tile deploy.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: a push 20 minutes before your slot ('Your shift: 18:40 UTC, crew is +3.1% EV alpha this week'), the widget's 'ORE in 47 of the last 50 rounds' counter, and Motherlode alerts. ACTION: tap the notification or 'Take my shift' tile and run ~4 rounds of live calls (hardware-key taps, gasless) while a Live Update chip counts your shift. Non-foremen cast a one-tap strategy vote (coverage, Motherlode threshold) or top up. VARIABLE REWARD: tile reveals with haptics synced across the crew's phones, your EV-alpha grade, the crew's standing in the weekly duel, and shared Motherlode hits, which a full-board co-op is guaranteed to catch. INVESTMENT: co-op shares, an on-chain foreman rating history, crew rank and the Nations table, and an attendance streak. NO-AIRDROP TEST: it is a daily multiplayer 'take your turn at the helm' game with friends, closer to Twitch Plays or a fantasy-league captaincy than to a slot machine.
mobile_native_surfaces: 120 Hz Compose Canvas live board with an EV heatmap fed by Helius LaserStream at 250 ms slots
Android Keystore P-256 session key (StrongBox/TEE) for gasless, pop-up-free live taps, verified on-chain via the secp256r1 precompile
Haptics synced across crew phones via high-priority FCM data messages (tile reveal, Motherlode 'quake' with Android 16 envelope haptics)
Live Update during your user-started foreman shift (time left, calls made, running EV alpha)
Glance widget: rounds-with-ORE counter, co-op ORE today, your next slot, Motherlode size
Quick Settings tile 'Take my shift' and notification actions; MWA trampoline Activity for deposits
Seed Vault double-tap reserved for money movement only (deposit, withdraw, duel stake)
SGT one-seat-per-device verified on-chain; .skr names on the board; dApp Store deep-link invites
Optional NFC/QR tap to join a co-op at IRL meetups
ideas.solana_integration: (1) foreman_coop program. CoopVault PDA [b'coop', id] is the authority of one ORE miner and Automation (executor = the program's executor PDA, DiscretionaryBps, <=1% fee enforced by ORE). Member PDA [b'member', coop, sgt_mint] holds shares with ERC-4626-style accounting: virtual-share offset against inflation attacks, minimum deposit, and a deposit/withdraw queue that settles at round boundaries. Session PDA registers a member's P-256 key with slot window, per-round tilt limits and expiry. (2) crank(): permissionless. It derives the deploy mask and amount from the co-op's default strategy plus the foreman's latest signed call (secp256r1 verify instruction + instructions-sysvar introspection + round-id binding), then invoke_signed calls ORE deploy. The cranker cannot choose tiles. (3) score_round(): reads the ORE Round PDA's per-tile totals after the round and computes the foreman's EV alpha on-chain. (4) A weekly 'payday' batches partial claims to limit refining-fee churn. (5) duel program: two co-ops escrow SKR, and it settles after 7 days from the recorded EV-alpha sums, with no oracle and no admin. Why on-chain: the pooled vault must be trustless (it removes the 'syndicate organiser ran off' problem), and skill scores and duel settlement must be verifiable from public ORE data.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the whole game board: FOREMAN is a multiplayer front-end to ORE's live grid. It uses split and solo tiles, the Motherlode (1/500, ~312 ORE today), Automation with a program executor (DiscretionaryBps), conditions (production-cost EMA, min/max Motherlode, split/solo tile counts), reload, partial claims and the refining fee (payday batching keeps co-op ORE unclaimed and earning refining share). A share of executor fees can buy ORE and send it to the grams bury address. Pooling recruits Seekers who would never mine solo, which grows ORE's ~150-165 miners per round, and co-op SOL is sticky, recurring deployed volume, exactly the usage metrics ORE's milestones ask for. It revives 'Proof of mobile' as Seeker-only co-ops with seats keyed by SGT mint. The app states plainly that pooling does not change expected value (production cost ~$104 vs price ~$85); it only removes variance, and the only edge shown is measured skill.
ideas.skr_role: SKR stakes weekly co-op skill duels settled on EV alpha, a skill score computed on-chain from ORE round data that luck can't move. Nobody wagers SKR on the Motherlode or a tile outcome, only on whose foremen read the board better. SKR is the stake in a verifiable skill contest (the Seek-style pattern), with no staking, checkout, lootbox or earn-leaderboard.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: six Seekers on a table in one crew room, 'Foreman: ade.skr, 04:12 left'. 5-12s: in the last 3 seconds of a round the foreman drags weight onto two under-deployed tiles. Each tap lands on-chain in under a second with no wallet prompt (explorer overlay), and the heatmap shifts. 12-16s: '3-2-1', all six phones buzz in sync: 'ORE in 47 of last 50 rounds, EV alpha +4.2%'. 16-20s: a real Motherlode hit recorded during testing (a full-board co-op shares every hit, so this footage is guaranteed within about a day); every phone quakes and member shares tick up next to .skr names. Title card: 'Luck is shared. Skill is scored.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: mechanism design he'll enjoy: variance pooling, an on-chain skill metric that luck can't move, and human-speed live play that only works with 250 ms slots and 4 KB v1 transactions. MERT: a real-time board driven by LaserStream and synced pushes; it separates skill from gambling openly instead of hiding the jackpot. CHASE: an open, reusable co-op vault and executor program for the ORE ecosystem, with rigorous tests. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: multiplayer Seeker-only seats (SGT keyed by mint, one per device), .skr on the board, hardware-key gasless taps with MWA reserved for money movement, Live Update shifts, a widget, and a social reason for friends to open the app daily. ETHELSEC: the vault is the obvious target and the README says so. Share-inflation defences target the exact class of ORE's June 2026 stake exploit (a missing account check in deposit), every account owner and PDA is checked, there is no admin withdraw, the upgrade authority is a Squads multisig with a timelock, Trident fuzzing checks the assets = shares x price invariant, and foreman keys are bounded by tilt caps so they can neither drain nor redirect funds.
ideas.closest_existing: Bitcoin mining pools and historical ORE v1/v2 pools; Evore managed-miner program (Kriptikz); refinORE/Minemore/Oreminer autominers; Radiants' own lodestar-cli (zero-fee terminal autominer with EV heatmaps); Tramplin (pooled prize staking, MONOLITH winner); UK lottery syndicates; Twitch Plays. 'ORE Crews' is the most obvious ORE-prize idea (it appears as a seed across the research, and SolanaFloor publicized the prize), so expect several Clock In teams to ship some kind of squad ORE app. FOREMAN differs through real pooled variance (full-board coverage) rather than cosmetic squads, a rotating human foreman making gasless hardware-key live calls, on-chain EV-alpha scoring, and SKR duels on skill rather than luck.
ideas.technical_depth: Three Anchor programs (co-op vault + executor, session keys with secp256r1 introspection, SKR duel escrow), a shared SGT-verifier crate, an on-chain EV-alpha calculator over ORE Round accounts, and a batched cranker (LaserStream + Sender, v1 txs). Tests: LiteSVM unit tests, Surfpool mainnet-fork integration against the live ORE program, Trident fuzzing of share math, and explicit property tests for inflated-share, first-depositor and rounding attacks. Kotlin/Compose client with a custom 120 Hz Canvas board, Keystore session-key management, FCM-synced haptics, Glance widget and Live Updates. An 'Autoforeman' fallback fills empty slots and explains calls, which hedges the Align 'AI' criterion. Backend: FCM fan-out, SIWS auth. This is the heaviest security surface of the four, deliberately owned and documented (threat model, invariants, verifiable build).
key_risks: Pooled custody is the highest-risk code in this portfolio. A single bug is fatal with Ethelsec judging and ORE's June exploit fresh, so it needs a narrow scope and heavy testing.
Legal optics: pooled funds plus a jackpot can look like a collective investment scheme or lottery syndicate in some countries.
Full-board coverage needs meaningful pooled SOL; small co-ops only partly smooth variance and dilute the 'always on the winning tile' promise.
Foreman griefing or poor play needs bounded tilt caps, reputation and an autopilot fallback.
Crowded concept: several ORE 'crew' entries are likely, so the win depends on execution quality and the skill-scoring twist.
The 10% refining fee on exits complicates fair share accounting and withdrawal UX.
Same PDA-executor CPI and ORE-upgrade dependency risks as SHIFT; secp256r1 precompile availability to verify.

ideas.name: STASH: the hard-money ajo
ideas.one_liner: One tap a day stacks ORE the cheapest way available: it mines when the board beats the market and buys when it doesn't, your circle watches your streak, and SKR gifts arrive already mining.
ideas.core_concept: STASH is a daily savings ritual in the mould of Jar's daily gold savings, PiggyVest's autosave and UK Premium Bonds, with ORE as the asset and the route chosen for best execution. Each morning you tap 'Save today', and one Seed Vault signature does both halves in a single v1 transaction. It tops up your own ORE Automation, set to mine only while the effective mining cost (SOL burned divided by 1 + Motherlode/500) is below Jupiter's price, and it swaps the rest into ORE at market. That makes it the one ORE app that tells you when not to mine, and a big Motherlode visibly makes mining cheaper. Your stash stays in your own ORE miner account and wallet: unclaimed ORE earns a share of everyone else's 10% refining fee, and bought ORE can go into stORE. A morning 'dig report' widget shows what the rig mined overnight in ORE and in local currency (NGN, KRW, BRL, INR, PHP). Circles of 3-12 SGT-verified friends or family see each other's daily saves, with amounts optionally hidden. 'Gift a Miner' turns SKR into a live, SGT-locked ORE rig for any .skr name, for red envelopes, Eid gifts or Nigerian owambe 'spraying'. The pitch writes itself for a West African founder: the neighbourhood esusu collector (alajo) sometimes vanishes with everyone's savings, and STASH has no collector at all.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: a 7am widget refresh ('Overnight: +0.021 ORE, Motherlode 312, mining is 14% cheaper than buying right now'), a notification with an inline 'Save N1,500' action, and circle pressure ('5/6 saved today'). ACTION: tap the widget, tile or notification, go through the trampoline, one Seed Vault double-tap; the whole ritual takes about 5 seconds. VARIABLE REWARD: the overnight dig report (tile hits, solo wins, Motherlode near-misses), the daily mine-or-buy verdict, rare Motherlode shares, and incoming Gift-a-Miner envelopes. INVESTMENT: a growing unclaimed-ORE balance that earns refining-fee share (claiming costs 10%, which teaches holding), circle streaks with auto-freezes, a savings goal ('1 ORE by December'), and a 'hard money vs naira' chart that means more the longer you stay. NO-AIRDROP TEST: it remains a daily savings habit with social accountability, the loop PiggyVest proved.
mobile_native_surfaces: Glance home-screen widget: jar fill, overnight dig report, value in local currency, Motherlode size, circle status (FCM-refreshed)
Quick Settings tile and notification inline action 'Save today' leading to a translucent MWA trampoline
Seed Vault double-tap as the daily save ritual: one real value-moving tx per day, the 'natural wallet use' that Solana Mobile's Aug 20 re-weighting rewards
Haptic 'coin clink' on save; tile-reveal haptics in the morning report
Share sheet / QR / optional NFC tap for Gift-a-Miner 'spray mode' at parties
ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT: select any .skr name in Telegram or X and choose 'Gift a miner'
App Shortcuts ('Save now', 'Gift')
Locale-aware currency (NGN, KRW, BRL, INR, PHP) and a biometric-gated balance view
SGT verification + .skr names for circles and gifts
ideas.solana_integration: The core path uses no custom custody. The daily save is a single v1 (4 KB) tx the user signs through MWA. It tops up the user's own ORE Automation (authority = user) using ORE's permissionless executor (~7,000 lamports/round) with a Preferred/Random strategy, conditions max_production_cost and min_motherlode set to the day's thresholds, and reload on. The same tx includes a Jupiter SOL/USDC to ORE swap for the buy portion and a circle instruction that reads the user's Automation account after the top-up in that tx to record a streak backed by real value, not a memo. Optional autopilot uses the Subscriptions & Allowances program (a capped USDC pull, e.g. <=$2/day with a 90-day expiry) into a per-user stash PDA whose only exits are ORE deploy CPIs or the owner's wallet. The gift program: the sender's tx swaps SKR to SOL on Jupiter and deposits into escrow PDA [b'gift', recipient_sgt_mint, nonce]. Only the current holder of that SGT, verified on-chain, can claim, which creates their funded ORE Automation via CPI; unclaimed gifts refund after 30 days. Helius Parsed Streams feed the dig report and circle feed. Why on-chain: savings must stay self-custodied, the mine-or-buy gating uses ORE's on-chain production-cost EMA and Motherlode, and gifts must be trustlessly bound to a real Seeker.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the savings asset, the mining engine and the unit the app reports in. It uses Automation with the max_production_cost and min/max Motherlode conditions (shipped Aug 2026) for execution-aware mining, plus reload, partial claims and refining-fee share for unclaimed balances ('interest paid by people who withdraw'). Bought ORE can go to ORE's stake program or stORE; that is ORE staking, not SKR staking. The app shows ORE Reserve and buy-and-bury stats, and optional round-ups go to the grams bury address. Being the ORE app that tells users when not to mine is the honest answer to production cost (~$104) sitting above price (~$85), and it still routes every save into ORE. For the ORE team it adds steady, habitual SOL deployed and new miners from an audience that would never run a bot.
ideas.skr_role: The SKR role is Gift a Miner: SKR becomes the gifting and onboarding currency for ORE. Send SKR to any .skr name; it is atomically swapped to SOL and escrowed against the recipient's SGT mint, so only a real Seeker can claim it, and it arrives as a pre-funded ORE rig that is already digging, a red envelope with a Motherlode ticket inside. It includes a party 'spray mode' and 30-day refunds. This gives idle airdropped SKR a social, peer-to-peer use without staking, checkout or leaderboards. Honest overlap: Seeker Envelope already does SKR red envelopes; the difference is the SGT-bound claim and the live miner inside.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-4s: Lagos, 7:02am, a real Seeker home screen; the STASH widget reads 'Overnight dig: +0.021 ORE, 41-day streak, Circle 6/6'. 4-10s: tap 'Save N1,500', Seed Vault double-tap + fingerprint, coin-clink haptic; a banner reads 'Mining is 14% cheaper than buying right now, sent to your rig'. 10-16s: the live 5x5 board lights where the deploy landed, a round compressed to 3 seconds, the winning tile flips with a haptic. 16-20s: founder voiceover over a paper esusu card (use a true personal or community story): 'Where I'm from, the savings collector sometimes disappears. STASH has no collector.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: market microstructure in a consumer app. It compares effective mining cost (including Motherlode EV) with the DEX price, bundles automate plus swap in one 4 KB v1 transaction, and brings internet capital markets to a daily habit in emerging markets. MERT: openly anti-casino ('we tell you when not to mine'), with Helius Parsed Streams for the dig report and hidden amounts in circles. CHASE: a real emerging-market founder story that uses the Foundation's audited Allowances primitive for autopilot. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: one meaningful value-moving tx per day, a widget + QS tile + Seed Vault ritual, SGT-bound gifts that farmers can't multiply, the .skr social graph, and a target in the under-supplied Earn category. ETHELSEC: the core path has zero custom custody (ORE Automation + the user's wallet); the gift escrow is minimal, SGT-verified on-chain and refundable with no admin key; the allowance is capped and expiring; signing prompts are human-readable.
ideas.closest_existing: Web2: Jar (daily digital-gold saving), PiggyVest (autosave), UK Premium Bonds (prize-linked savings), Acorns round-ups. Solana: the official ORE app (stale since Oct 2025) and ORE's web Lite/Pro autominer; Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer and refinORE autominers (refinORE already does SKR-to-mine swaps); the Seed Vault Wallet USDC Earn vault; Kin (github.com/angelraph/kin), a Clock In competitor running SKR/USDC-bonded rotating savings circles with optional SGT gating but no ORE; Seeker Envelope (SKR red envelopes); Tramplin (no-loss prize staking). STASH differs as a savings-first daily ritual where ORE is acquired by best execution (mine only when cheaper, else buy), self-custodied, with SGT-bound miner gifts. Honest weakness: under the hood it is a smart autominer plus DCA, so the ritual, the honesty and the UX must carry it.
ideas.technical_depth: Programs: the gift escrow (SGT verifier, claim that creates the recipient's ORE Automation via CPI, refund path, no admin), a circle registry (SGT-keyed membership, save attestations backed by real value that read Automation state in the same tx), and an optional stash PDA for Allowances autopilot (exit invariants: ORE deploy CPI or the owner's wallet only). Off-chain: an execution engine that computes effective mining cost from on-chain Round/Treasury state and api.ore.com against a Jupiter quote and sets the day's conditions; Helius Parsed Streams to FCM for the dig report; SIWS auth. An on-device plain-language 'why mine vs buy today' explainer hedges the Align 'AI' criterion. App: Kotlin/Compose + Glance + TileService + clientlib-ktx, localized currencies. Tests: Surfpool mainnet-fork tests combining ORE automate and a Jupiter swap in one v1 tx; escrow fuzzing.
key_risks: Volatility: ORE is ~66% below its Nov 2025 high (~$249 to ~$85). Marketing a volatile token as 'savings' to users in inflation-hit economies is a real ethical and reputational risk; it needs clear 'hard-money sleeve' framing and drawdown disclosure.
Regulatory: 'savings' language plus jackpot mechanics may look like an unlicensed deposit or prize-linked product in some jurisdictions.
Innovation may read as 'another autominer + DCA'; existing autominers and refinORE blunt the novelty.
If production cost stays above market, the mine-when-cheaper window is rare and most saves become plain swaps, weakening the mining story.
Kin (circles) and Seeker Envelope (SKR gifts) overlap on two sub-features.
Whether a third party can top up someone else's ORE Automation is unverified; Allowances autopilot may force a program-owned authority, which means custody.
Bundling a Jupiter swap with ORE automate in one v1 tx depends on the shipping Seed Vault Wallet supporting v1 (SDK support landed Sep 26); test on device.

ideas.name: MELT: get paid in hard money to prove fiat is melting
ideas.one_liner: Every day the whole Seeker world prices one item (rice, petrol, a gigabyte), and each verified price tag earns an ORE mining shift. Together they build the first phone-sourced, sybil-resistant street-price index on Solana, quoted in local currency and in ORE.
ideas.core_concept: Crypto's founding story is fiat debasement, and much of the Seeker base lives it (Nigeria, Argentina, Turkey, Brazil, the Philippines). MELT is GasBuddy for the whole economy: each day one item drops for everyone, and Seekers photograph its price on their commute. On the phone, ML Kit OCR reads the tag, faces are blurred and location is coarsened to an H3 cell. The capture digest is signed by an attested Keystore key and committed on-chain, one report per SGT per day. At 20:00 UTC the reports reveal. Commit-reveal stops copying and creates a Wordle-style shared moment: medians are computed per city and the global map lights up ('rice in Lagos N2,450/kg, +38% YoY; in ORE, -12%'). Accepted reports are paid as ORE mining shifts: the MELT treasury runs rounds on the live board in each reporter's name. The reporter risks nothing, and because returned SOL recycles to the treasury, $1 of sponsor money funds roughly $9.50 of deploys. People who can't capture that day play 'Guess the Global Median' (a Price Is Right mode), and flagged outliers go to SKR-bonded validators. The index is a public on-chain feed that programs, prediction markets and agents can read, and data buyers pay per query over Solana Payment Channels, which refills the wage treasury. Why now: ~121k SGT-verified devices make crowd data sybil-resistant for the first time, ORE provides a jackpot-flavoured wage, Payment Channels (Sep 3) make per-query data sales cheap, and the Foundation's stablecoin and ICM push needs real-world price data.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: an 08:00 local notification and widget ('Today: 1 L petrol, 214 reports in 31 countries, your city: 3 so far'). ACTION: open the camera from the widget or App Shortcut, point, auto-OCR, confirm: about 10 seconds, gasless via a fee relayer, with Seed Vault used only for claims and validator bonds. VARIABLE REWARD: the 20:00 UTC global reveal (your city's rank, how far your median guess was off), then wage rounds mining on the live board under a Live Update chip, with tile hits and a Motherlode chance at zero money at risk. INVESTMENT: reporter reputation (a quality-weighted wage multiplier), city coverage badges, a streak with freezes, a personal 'melt chart' of your own basket, and a Sunday city CPI you helped build. NO-AIRDROP TEST: it is still a GasBuddy/Numbeo-style utility plus a daily shared-object game (Wordle's reveal, Price Is Right's guess).
mobile_native_surfaces: CameraX + on-device ML Kit Text Recognition v2 (Latin, Korean, Devanagari, Chinese, Japanese scripts) with on-device face/person blur before anything leaves the phone
Android Keystore P-256 capture-signing key with Key Attestation (package + signing cert), so reports provably come from the genuine app on real hardware
Coarse location (H3 cell); precise GPS is never stored
Glance widget: today's item, your city vs the world, report count so far, your wage-rig status
Live Update while your user-triggered wage shift is mining
Notifications for the daily drop and the 20:00 UTC reveal; App Shortcut 'Price it'
Spoiler-free Wordle-style share card via the share sheet to X/Telegram
SGT verified on-chain (one report per device per day) + .skr reporter identity
Seed Vault double-tap for claims, cash-out and validator bonds
Haptics on OCR lock and on the reveal
ideas.solana_integration: melt program (Anchor). Report PDA [b'report', day, item, sgt_mint] stores a commitment hash (price, currency, H3 cell, capture digest, salt) whose P-256 signature is verified via secp256r1 precompile introspection. reveal() runs after the cutoff, and aggregate() computes bounded, deterministic per-cell and per-country medians and writes an IndexFeed PDA any program can read. Wages: WageRig PDA [b'wage', sgt_mint] is the authority of an ORE Automation funded from the Treasury PDA. Accepted reports credit wage rounds; the program's executor PDA CPIs ORE deploys (DiscretionaryBps); mined ORE is claimable only to the current SGT holder's wallet; leftover SOL sweeps back to the treasury. Validators: an SKR bond escrow and a Schelling-point vote on flagged reports, with the minority slashed. Sponsors deposit to the Treasury, tagged by item or region. Data buyers pay per query through the Payment Channels program (CHNLxYvVA28MJP9PrFuDXccuoGXAx7jBacfLEkahyGsX, x402 'upto'); settled revenue refills the treasury and a slice buys ORE for the grams address. A Kora fee relayer means reporters need no SOL. Why on-chain: the index must be tamper-evident and composable, commit-reveal needs a neutral clock, wages must be trustless, and sybil resistance (SGT keyed by mint) must be enforced by the program.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the wage and the unit of account. Every accepted report becomes rounds on the live ORE board in the reporter's name (Automation, executor PDA, DiscretionaryBps, conditions such as min Motherlode for weekend 'bonus shifts'), so each reporter becomes a new ORE miner without ever buying SOL. Every price in the index is also quoted in ORE ('rice in Lagos costs 0.019 ORE'), which positions ORE as the hard-money yardstick against melting fiat, exactly ORE's store-of-value narrative. Part of data revenue buys ORE and sends it to the grams bury address. Proposed matched-prize milestone: the ORE match itself funds the first reporter wages. Economics: sponsors lose ~10.5% of deployed SOL per round; reporters receive about $0.82 of ORE per $1 burned in expectation, plus Motherlode upside; the burn funds ORE's buy-and-bury.
ideas.skr_role: The SKR role is validator bonds, a working version of the SKR whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' idea applied to real-world data. Seekers bond SKR to adjudicate flagged or outlier reports (photo + OCR + location cell) in a Schelling-point vote. Validators who side with the majority earn a share of wage rounds and the minority's slashed SKR, and anyone who approves a fake loses their bond. SKR becomes the collateral that makes the data trustworthy, with no staking program, no checkout and no earn leaderboard.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-6s: a Lagos market stall; a real Seeker points at a hand-written price card, the OCR box locks on 'N2,450' with a haptic, and faces in frame auto-blur. 6-10s: tap Commit, and 'Report sealed, 1 per Seeker per day' appears. 10-15s: jump to 20:00 UTC; the global map fills with that day's real tester reports and a card reads 'Rice: Lagos +38% YoY in naira, -12% in ORE'. 15-20s: 'You earned 12 wage rounds'; the lock-screen chip shows the rig mining on the live ORE board as a tile hit flips. Title card: 'Fiat melts. ORE doesn't. Get paid to prove it.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: an on-chain oracle sourced from ~121k verified phones that feeds the internet-capital-markets thesis (CPI-settled markets, remittance pricing), plus commit-reveal done right. MERT: a data product with real privacy engineering (on-device blur, coarse cells, only commitments on-chain until reveal), Helius streams for the reveal fan-out, and Payment Channels for data sales. CHASE: a public good with an ecosystem API that puts the Foundation's newest payments primitive into a consumer app. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: camera, on-device ML, Keystore attestation, SGT sybil resistance, a daily shared moment, and a story built for Seeker's international base. ETHELSEC: commit-reveal against copying, attested keys, a Schelling game with slashing, reporters who hold nothing that can lose money, and a treasury whose only exits are ORE deploys, reporter claims or sponsor refunds.
ideas.closest_existing: GasBuddy (crowd-reported gas prices rewarded with prize draws, the closest Web2 analogue and evidence that lottery-style incentives drive price reporting), Numbeo (crowd cost-of-living data), MIT's Billion Prices Project/PriceStats and Truflation (inflation indexes from scraped or aggregated data, not phones), Kled (sell photos/data for AI), Hivemapper (useful-work DePIN). On Seeker: Seek (photo-verified hunts, MONOLITH SKR winner), Legwork (paid real-world missions), Candor and SeekerLens (camera hashing, non-winners), TokenRun and LootGO (GPS). A web search found no crowdsourced, phone-verified street-price index on Solana. MELT differs through on-chain SGT sybil resistance, a commit-reveal daily shared object, ORE-denominated prices, and wages paid as live ORE mining.
ideas.technical_depth: melt Anchor program: commit-reveal, on-chain medians over bounded sets, an IndexFeed PDA for CPI consumers, WageRig executor CPI into ORE, treasury accounting, and SKR validator escrow with Schelling settlement. Also: Payment Channels integration for per-query data sales (pay-kit Kotlin/TS clients) and a Kora fee relayer. Kotlin app: CameraX + ML Kit OCR pipeline, a price parser (currency symbols, decimal conventions, per-kg/per-litre normalisation), on-device blur, Keystore attestation, Glance widget. The on-device ML is a genuine hedge for the Align 'AI' criterion. Backend: attestation verification, encrypted, expiring image storage for validators, reveal fan-out via Helius. Adversarial test suite: copied prices, duplicate SGTs, replayed signatures, and coordinated median manipulation within a cell.
key_risks: ORE fit: the ORE team may see ORE as 'the payout token' rather than the product, which weakens the matched-prize case against mining-centric entries. Mitigate by making ORE the unit of account and running every wage visibly on the live board.
Demand for the data is unproven, and sponsors and data buyers won't exist by judging, so early wages are subsidised (possibly by the ORE milestones).
Data quality and fraud: printed fake tags, staged photos, colluding reporters in thin cells. SGT caps sybils but not collusion.
Safety and privacy: photographing inside shops is sensitive in some countries; on-device blur and clear opt-outs are required.
Stickiness leans on wages, which invites airdrop-farming behaviour; the reveal and guess game must carry retention (lowest stickiness of the four).
OCR accuracy across scripts, handwritten tags and unit normalisation.
On-chain medians are compute-bound, so sample caps or off-chain aggregation with on-chain verification may be needed.

lens: Judge whisperer / frontier primitives. Each idea uses a mainnet primitive only weeks or months old (Payment Channels, Subscriptions & Allowances, secp256r1 with Android Keystore keys, tx v1 4 KB transactions, SIMD-0437 rent reclaim, Helius Parsed Streams/LaserStream/Sender, 250 ms slots, durable nonces used defensively) to make a consumer UX that was not possible last quarter. Each idea is also aimed at specific panelists: Toly (payments, latency, meme charm), Mert (Helius infra doing real work, no fake metrics, privacy), Chase (PMF and a first-10k wedge), Akshay and Beeman (Seeker-only hardware and OS surfaces, SGT verified on-chain, wallet-ui) and the Ethelsec pair (bounded blast radius, reuse of audited programs, published threat models). Novelty checks changed the set. Totem Wallet (a Clock In entry: a Kotlin pre-sign-receipt wallet with 291 commits) and U$ER (SagaDAO's SGT-gated paid app testing) already exist, so a pure pre-sign scanner and a paid-testing marketplace were dropped or reshaped. The web search budget and the GitHub rate limit ran out partway through, so the novelty checks for Punch, Pulse and Parachute are partial.

ideas.name: Punch
ideas.one_liner: Punch in on your Seeker and get paid by the second: every second you work is already an escrowed, signed voucher in your pocket, and your live paycheck shows on the lock screen.
ideas.core_concept: Punch is a time clock that pays. A client (any Solana wallet; no Seeker needed) funds a Solana Payment Channel once, with the worker as payee and a weekly cap as the deposit. While the worker is punched in, an authorized session key streams cumulative Ed25519 vouchers every few seconds, and the worker's phone checks each one against the on-chain escrow. So the number on the lock screen is not a promise. The worker can settle it on-chain at any second, with or without Punch's servers, which cuts non-payment risk to the last few seconds and caps the client's risk at the escrow. After punching out, the worker can cash out at once (earned-wage access in one settle on 250 ms slots) or let the week build up and settle once. Long contracts refill themselves through a Subscriptions & Allowances recurring delegation, so a client sets a weekly budget once and never signs again. Each settle writes an hours attestation to a worker profile keyed by the Seeker Genesis Token mint and verified inside Punch's own program. That gives Seeker owners a portable work history that farms cannot fake. The first users are crypto contractors already in the Seeker base (moderators, community managers, designers, devs, QA and content people across 57 countries), who are paid in USDC by invoice, late, and sometimes never. The founder story comes from Lagos, where 30- to 60-day payment delays on crypto gigs are normal. Why now: Payment Channels reached mainnet on Sept 3 and no consumer mobile app uses them yet, Seeker's Android 16 build enables Live Updates, and the dApp Store has zero clock-in, shift or attendance apps, in a hackathon literally named Clock In.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: the home-screen widget shows today's contracts and this week's verified hours. A morning nudge fires at your usual start time, and the Quick Settings tile is one swipe away. Action: swipe down, tap 'Punch in' and touch the fingerprint sensor. A Keystore key signs the punch, so no wallet popup appears. Variable reward: the paycheck visibly climbs on the lock screen with a soft haptic at each dollar. Clients can add bonuses or tips at punch-out, and the end-of-day paystub shows verified hours with a one-tap 'cash out now'. Investment: an on-chain verified-hours record and ratings tied to your SGT, recurring contracts that refill themselves, and a weekly Payday ritual where one Seed Vault double-tap settles everything. With every token incentive removed it is still your wage, so the loop does not depend on airdrops.
mobile_native_surfaces: Android 16 Live Update (NotificationCompat.ProgressStyle, promoted ongoing, status-bar chip plus lock screen): a shift timer the user starts, counting up (not a countdown), with earnings as the subtitle. It doubles as the required notification of the heartbeat foreground service.
Quick Settings tile 'Punch in/out' (TileService with requestAddTileService, and startActivityAndCollapse into a translucent trampoline activity)
Jetpack Glance widget whose RemoteViews Chronometer ticks live without app updates, plus FCM pushes from Helius webhooks when settles land
Android Keystore P-256 heartbeat key (StrongBox if present) bound to BiometricPrompt, so punching needs no MWA session
Seed Vault double-tap reserved for the 'Payday' ritual (channel open, settle, cash-out)
Geofence punch, plus an NFC-sticker or rotating-QR punch for on-site shifts (NFC gated behind a runtime check)
Haptics per dollar earned, share-sheet invoice links, and .skr names for clients and workers
ideas.solana_integration: Payment Channels program (CHNLxYvVA28MJP9PrFuDXccuoGXAx7jBacfLEkahyGsX, audited by Cantina). The client calls open to deposit the escrow and set authorized_signer and payee, and can top_up later. Vouchers are off-chain 50-byte cumulative messages with an expiry. The worker calls settle or settle_and_seal. Exits use request_close (which starts a grace period), then seal or withdraw_payer, and distribute sends a committed split to a platform or agency fee recipient. A Subscriptions & Allowances RecurringDelegation (De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44) lets a Punch PDA refill the channel weekly from the client's USDC within a cap. A small Punch program (Anchor or Pinocchio) stores contracts at [b"contract", client, sgt_mint]. It verifies the worker's SGT on-chain: TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89..., mint authority == GT2zuH..., token account owner == signer, and amount == 1. It records an hours attestation on each settle. Helius webhooks and Parsed Streams watch every channel, so when a client calls request_close the worker gets a high-priority push to settle before the grace period ends. Why this must be on-chain: the escrow proves the money exists before work starts, vouchers can be redeemed without Punch's cooperation (credible neutrality), and the work history is sybil-resistant and portable.
ideas.ore_detail: Not an ORE product; forcing ORE in would fail the 'primary product' rule. At most an unpitched option to send x% of each payday to ORE via distribute.
ideas.skr_role: Optional and minor. Clients who want to hire from the SGT-verified worker directory post an SKR 'good-payer bond' in Punch's program. If a client force-closes a channel mid-shift and the dispute window rules for the worker, the worker can claim part of that bond. It is a bond held by Punch's program, not SKR staking, and not the main SKR-prize play.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-3s: a real Seeker lies locked on a desk. Voiceover: 'They named this hackathon Clock In. So we built the clock.' 3-8s: swipe down, tap the Punch tile and touch the fingerprint sensor. A status-bar chip appears and the lock screen reads 'On the clock - 0:00:04 - $0.01', ticking up with a soft haptic. 8-14s: open the voucher inspector: 'voucher #412 - cumulative 3.41 USDC - Ed25519 verified - escrow 200 USDC on mainnet'. Switch on airplane mode and the earned amount still verifies offline. 14-20s: punch out, tap 'Cash out now' and double-tap Seed Vault. Solscan shows the settle confirmed in under a second, with the USDC in the wallet.
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: payments is his number-two narrative and the Foundation just hired a payments GM. This is the first consumer mobile app on Payment Channels plus Allowances, cash-out rides 250 ms slots, it frames labor as an internet capital market, and 'we built the clock' is the meme. Mert: every on-chain event is a real payment for real hours, with no emissions and no fake metrics. Helius webhooks and Parsed Streams do real work (the forced-close watch), and per-second earnings stay off-chain in vouchers instead of being broadcast. Chase: the problem is validated and painful (freelancer non-payment, and a multi-billion-dollar earned-wage-access category), crypto contractors are an obvious first-10k wedge, and a small fee taken via distribute is a clear business model. Akshay and Beeman: a Live Update, QS tile, widget, Keystore key and Seed Vault payday ritual are all native, the identity is keyed by SGT mint and verified on-chain, it is built on wallet-ui, and it makes Seeker 'the phone you get paid on'. Ethelsec: it reuses an audited escrow instead of writing custody code. The session key can only pay the named worker, up to the deposit. Cumulative, expiring vouchers cannot be replayed, forced close is monitored, and the README ships a threat model.
ideas.closest_existing: Zebec, Streamflow and Sablier stream tokens on a fixed on-chain schedule: pausing needs a transaction and nothing ties the stream to attendance or a phone. Upwork Hourly offers escrow and a Work Diary, but it bills weekly, pays out 1-2 weeks later and takes about 10%. DailyPay and Payactiv offer earned-wage access only through employer integrations, and they charge fees. Deel and Rise run monthly crypto payroll. Superteam Earn pays per bounty, not per hour. Among Clock In competitors, nuntius does recurring payment authority (subscriptions, not metered time), ChainWitness proves presence without paying anyone, ClockLend is P2P lending, and TapWifSol is tap-to-pay. Punch differs in three ways: pay is metered per second off-chain and can be redeemed on-chain at any moment through audited channels, the Seeker itself is the time clock, and the worker's history is bound to a device through the SGT.
ideas.technical_depth: Expo SDK 57 with @wallet-ui/react-native-kit (Beeman's library), plus custom Kotlin Expo modules for the Live Update foreground service, TileService, Glance widget and Keystore. Pure Kotlin/Compose with clientlib-ktx is the alternative. The channel program ships only TypeScript and Rust clients, so the app needs its own Kotlin port of the 50-byte Borsh/Ed25519 voucher layout. The repo would include: a Rust metering signer with per-channel session keys in KMS, a rate limit driven by Keystore-signed heartbeats, and pause and dispute handling. It also includes the Punch program, the first public example of on-chain SGT verification, with contract and attestation PDAs, checked math, and bankrun and Surfpool mainnet-fork tests covering forced-close races. Rounding it out: a Helius webhook-to-FCM pipeline, MWA flows that pass the AlignAI fixtures (connect, session, signing completion, rejection recovery), and an optional on-device LiteRT-LM Gemma model that drafts the weekly timesheet summary locally, covering the possible AI score without the work data leaving the phone.
key_risks: Two-sided cold start: Punch needs clients as well as workers. Judges may read it as a B2B productivity tool rather than a Seeker-community habit unless the demo shows real crypto teams paying real Seeker owners.
The voucher-signing session key is a hot key on Punch's server. Its reach is limited to the named worker and the escrow, but Ethelsec will probe it, and moving the signer to the client hurts UX.
Being present is not proof of work on remote jobs. The rate limit is enforced off-chain by the signer, not by the channel program, so disputes need a clear policy.

There is no Kotlin client for the channel program. The voucher layout, grace-period behavior and whether a third party may call top_up must be checked against the program source before relying on auto-refill.
Live Update promotion and a long-running specialUse foreground service (Doze, battery) must be tested on a real Seeker running Android 16.
Payroll, earned-wage-access and labor rules vary by jurisdiction. Punch must be positioned as a payment tool between two parties, not as an employer of record.

ideas.name: Pickaxe
ideas.one_liner: Acorns for hard money: the spare change from every swap and payment on your Seeker goes onto ORE's board automatically, and each morning a shift report tells you what it mined.
ideas.core_concept: Pickaxe is the consumer ORE app that ORE never shipped: a native Seeker miner funded by a habit instead of a lump sum. Setup is one Seed Vault double-tap on a single tx v1 transaction that does three things. It creates a vault PDA for the user. It grants that PDA a capped Subscriptions & Allowances recurring delegation over the user's USDC (for example up to $3 a day for 90 days). And it opens an ORE Automation account whose authority is the vault, configured with the user's strategy: split/solo tile mix, a minimum Motherlode size and a maximum production cost. Helius Parsed Streams watches the user's wallet. Every decoded Jupiter swap, transfer or Solana Pay payment produces a round-up. Pickaxe's program pulls it into the vault, swaps it to SOL and tops up the automation, which ORE's permissionless executor (or Pickaxe's own DiscretionaryBps executor) then deploys round after round. A weekly 'Sweep' packs a whole wallet cleanup into one 4 KB transaction: it reclaims the excess rent freed by SIMD-0437, closes empty token accounts, swaps dust and sends it all to the board. The economics are stated honestly. When ORE's production cost (about $104) is above its price (about $85), Smart Pickaxe only mines up to a premium the user sets and buys ORE otherwise, so the user always sees what the Motherlode ticket costs. Why now: the official ORE app has not been updated since Oct 2025, mobile ORE today means bot autominers, only about 150-165 miners play each round, and allowances, Parsed Streams and tx v1 only just made a signature-free, stream-triggered habit possible. For a Nigerian founder, saving spare change in a hard asset because the naira lost most of its value is lived experience, not a pitch.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: a 7am 'Shift Report' notification and a widget jar ('Overnight: 318 rounds, 41 wins, +0.0062 ORE, refining yield +0.0003'). Motherlode hits (about 1 in 500 rounds, roughly twice a day) send a push with a strike haptic, plus a near-miss line when you were one tile away. Action: nothing is required, because round-ups happen as a side effect of normal wallet use. You can tap to adjust strategy, to refine (claim), or to run the weekly Sweep with one double-tap. Variable reward: winning tiles, solo-tile wins, the rare Motherlode, and SOL found in your own wallet's rent. Investment: a growing ORE stack whose unclaimed balance earns refining fees from other miners, streaks of funded days, a tuned strategy, and a .skr crew comparing 'ORE stacked from spare change' (never PnL). With rewards removed, the core value is still an automatic savings habit into a hard asset.
mobile_native_surfaces: Jetpack Glance widget showing the ORE jar, a Motherlode meter and the last round's result, refreshed by Helius webhook to FCM data pushes
Android 16 Live Update for a 'mining shift' the user starts, such as a Sweep or boost (ProgressStyle showing rounds done out of total)
Quick Settings tile 'Sweep', which opens a trampoline activity, builds one tx v1 transaction and asks for one Seed Vault double-tap
Morning digest notification with inline 'Refine' and 'Pause' actions
Android 16 envelope haptics for the tile strike and Motherlode reveal, and a 120 Hz board animation
SGT 'Proof of Mobile' badge and .skr crews; the shift-report card can be shared through the share sheet
Seed Vault used only for setup, Sweep and refine, never once per round
ideas.solana_integration: ORE mining program (oreV3EG1i9BEgiAJ8b177Z2S2rMarzak4NMv1kULvWv): an Automation account with the vault PDA as authority, holding strategy, tile mask, split/solo counts, minimum and maximum Motherlode, maximum production cost and auto-reload. Rounds are deployed by ORE's permissionless executor (about 7,000 lamports per round) or by a Pickaxe DiscretionaryBps executor (fee at most 1%). Claiming and refining go through the vault, with optional stORE staking of refined ORE on the stake program that replaced the one exploited in June. Subscriptions & Allowances (De1egAFMkMWZSN5rYXRj9CAdheBamobVNubTsi9avR44): a RecurringDelegation whose delegate is a Pickaxe PDA, so pulls only happen through program CPI and can only land in the user's own vault. The Pickaxe program (Pinocchio or Anchor) implements pull_roundup (amount no more than the remaining cap for the period, deduplicated by source transaction signature), a Jupiter CPI swap (tx v1 removes the need for address lookup tables), automation top-up, and withdraw-to-owner as the only way out. It has no admin withdrawal path and verifies the SGT on-chain to mark Seeker miners. The tx v1 (4 KB) Sweep combines WithdrawExcessLamports rent reclaim, CloseAccount, dust swaps and the deposit under one signature. Helius Parsed Streams is what triggers each round-up. Why on-chain: mining is on-chain by definition, the cap and the destination are enforced by the delegation and the program rather than a server, and every round-up is a real payment anyone can verify.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the whole product. Every routed dollar lands on ORE's 5x5 board through native Automation accounts, the main screen is the live board and Motherlode, and claiming, refining and stORE are first-class features. It delivers, at the app layer, the 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker' that ORE advertised but never shipped (its claim_seeker instruction was removed in Nov 2025). It adds hundreds to thousands of small, habitual miners to a board that sees about 150-165 per round, which is exactly the usage metric the milestone-paid ORE match asks for. An optional 'bury share' sends part of the fees to the grams burn address, in line with ORE's hard-money story.
ideas.skr_role: Minor: users can pick SKR as a round-up source, for example so Seeker Season payouts drip onto the board. This is close to refinORE's existing SKR mining, so it is not an SKR-prize play.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: on a real Seeker, pay a friend 4.63 USDC through a Solana Pay QR code and double-tap as usual. 5-10s: with no second prompt, the widget buzzes '+0.37 round-up to ORE board, round #412,331' and the 5x5 board animates the deposit. 10-15s: the round resolves, a strike haptic fires ('Tile 9 hit, +0.0004 ORE') and Solscan shows the delegated pull, the swap and the executor's deploy. 15-20s: swipe down, tap the 'Sweep' tile and double-tap once. A single tx v1 transaction with 23 instructions lands: 'Recovered 0.041 SOL rent + 7 dust tokens, now mining.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: a payments-native habit built on three brand-new primitives (allowances, tx v1, rent reclaim), sub-second feedback on 250 ms slots, ORE (the Renaissance Grand Champion), and a 'hard money from spare change' meme. Mert: Parsed Streams is the trigger the product depends on, not a logo on a slide. There are no fake metrics, because every round-up is a real delegated payment, and the expected-value disclosure is honest. Chase: a proven Web2 format (Acorns, 10M+ customers) with a clear first-10k wedge in the 32k ORE holders plus active Seeker owners. Akshay and Beeman: widget, QS tile, haptics and SGT Proof of Mobile, with Seed Vault kept for meaningful actions and no signature spam, so usage reads as natural wallet activity under the Aug 20 re-weighting. Ethelsec: the delegate is code, not a key; the cap is per period and enforced on-chain; the destination is fixed to the user's own vault; withdrawals go only to the owner; there is no admin key; and custody is per user, never pooled. The ORE team gets the native Seeker app it never built.
ideas.closest_existing: Acorns, Stash and Revolut round up fiat purchases into ETFs. Gather is a web-first devnet demo that rounds up into tokenized stocks. refinORE Autominer lets users mine ORE with SKR through a swap on the web. Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer and RefinORE AutoMiner are autominer bots. The official ORE Seeker app has not been updated since Oct 2025, and ore.com has only offered a PWA since Aug 2026. Other lenses will likely pitch ORE crews or squads. Pickaxe differs in three ways: its funding habit (stream-triggered round-ups pulled through audited allowances with no user signature), the tx v1 rent and dust Sweep, and its Seeker-native surfaces. It is also the only one that routes honestly between mining and buying.
ideas.technical_depth: The Pickaxe program makes CPIs into three external programs (Subscriptions delegated transfer, Jupiter swap, ORE automate and claim) under strict invariants: per-user PDAs, owner-only withdrawal, deduplication by source signature and checked math. It is covered by property and fuzz tests and by Surfpool mainnet-fork tests against the live ORE program. A TypeScript and Kotlin ORE client is generated with Codama from api/idl.json (none exists on npm) and contributed back. A Rust crank consumes Helius Parsed Streams with idempotent round-up accounting. A tx v1 builder assembles the Sweep, with a v0 fallback. The rest: Glance widget, FCM and Live Update modules, on-chain SGT verification, MWA flows that pass the AlignAI fixtures, and a small 'strategy explainer' that turns a user's settings into an expected cost per ORE (covering the possible AI score).
key_risks: Economics: with production cost (about $104) above price (about $85), mining loses money compared with buying. Toly and the security judges may read it as a lottery, so the premium must be disclosed honestly and the dApp Store framing handled carefully.

Pickaxe's vault program holds user funds, one vault per user. After ORE's June exploit through a missing account check, any bug would sink the pitch, so the program must stay tiny and be tested exhaustively.

CPI compatibility is unverified: whether an ORE Automation authority can be a PDA signing through invoke_signed, whether the Jupiter CPI fits within compute and size limits, and whether the Subscriptions transfer works with a PDA delegate.

The crank chooses the round-up amount within the cap, because the triggering transaction cannot be proven on-chain. Its blast radius (at most the daily cap, moved into the user's own vault) has to be explained clearly.
Passive apps tend to have weaker daily active use; stickiness depends on notifications, the widget and Motherlode drama.
The ORE match is a single prize that ORE awards at its sole discretion and pays by milestone, and other entrants will pitch ORE too.
Production Seed Vault Wallet support for tx v1 (the SDK added it on Sep 26) must be confirmed on a device.

ideas.name: Pulse
ideas.one_liner: One question a day, answered only by real Seekers: tap your answer on the home screen, guess how the other 120,000 will vote, and see the truth at 9pm. It is the only poll in crypto that bots can't vote in.
ideas.core_concept: Crypto Twitter's polls and engagement numbers are farmed by bots, and the Seeker is the only large population of hardware-verified crypto users (about 121k Seeker Genesis Tokens). Pulse turns that population into a daily shared object like Wordle and a skill game like Family Feud's 'survey says'. You answer today's question, predict the crowd's split, and score on how well you read the room when every result is revealed at the same moment. Voting needs no wallet popup. At setup, one Seed Vault signature binds a non-exportable P-256 key from the Seeker's Android Keystore to the user's SGT mint in Pulse's program. After that, each vote is signed by the hardware key behind a fingerprint, verified on-chain through the secp256r1 precompile and relayed gas-free by a Kora fee relayer. Votes are first committed as hashes and then revealed automatically from the device at close, which prevents herding and front-running. One vote per device is enforced with a bitmap indexed by the SGT's TokenGroupMember number, so anyone can recount. Questions come from two sources. The community proposes them with an SKR bond and verified Seekers upvote them. Sponsors (dApps, funds, media and Solana Mobile itself) pay to hear from verified crypto users, and that money goes to the people who answered. Opt-in cohorts built with Helius Parsed Events ('among Seekers who actually swapped this week, 64% said...') make Pulse the most credible sentiment dataset in crypto. Why now: secp256r1 plus Keystore finally lets a phone's secure hardware act on-chain without the wallet, and nobody has published an example of verifying SGTs on-chain.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: at 9am local time the widget changes to 'Pulse #217' with the day's question, and one notification offers inline answers. Action: tap an answer on the widget or in the notification shade, confirm with a fingerprint, then slide to guess the split. It takes about 5 seconds and no wallet. Variable reward: the synchronized 9pm reveal shows the often-surprising result, your room-reading accuracy, how your .skr friends voted, on-chain-verified cohort splits and sponsor bonuses for the best readers. Investment: a streak with automatic freezes, an 'Oracle rank', your proposed questions climbing the queue, and a weekly 'State of the Seekers' report worth sharing. The core value (curiosity, social comparison and a verified community voice) holds up with every token removed.
mobile_native_surfaces: Interactive Glance widget whose answer buttons go through a translucent BiometricPrompt activity (no MWA)
Notification inline actions for answering from the shade, plus an automatic reveal at close via WorkManager
Android Keystore/StrongBox P-256 key with setUserAuthenticationRequired, with Android Key Attestation checked at registration
Seed Vault double-tap used only for one-time registration and SKR bonds
Haptic drumroll and a 120 Hz reveal animation; a spoiler-free emoji-grid share card through the share sheet
SGT as one-device identity, a .skr friends graph, and an App Shortcut 'Propose a question'
ideas.solana_integration: The Pulse program has six parts. (1) register_device verifies the SGT on-chain (Token-2022 TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89..., mint authority == GT2zuH..., holder == signer) and binds a P-256 public key to PDA [b"voter", sgt_mint]. (2) commit_vote checks, via the instructions sysvar, that a Secp256r1SigVerify1111111111111111111111111 precompile instruction signed (question_id, commitment, nonce); it records one commit per SGT memberNumber in a per-question bitmap, so no per-vote accounts are needed. (3) reveal and finalize compute the tally and scores on-chain. (4) A question market: propose with an SKR bond, one upvote per SGT per day; a selected question gets its bond back plus a reward, and spam flagged by N verified devices loses its bond. (5) Sponsor escrows pay out pro-rata to respondents, with claims authorized by the Keystore key and sent only to the bound wallet. (6) Kora relays the fees. Helius Parsed Events and DAS power the opt-in cohort segmentation, and rent reduction plus bitmaps keep the daily cost to cents. Why on-chain: anyone can verify that each answer came from a distinct real Seeker, sponsors can audit the sample size, and the results are a public good other programs can read.
ideas.ore_detail: Deliberately none: bolting ORE on would dilute the daily-question product and fail ORE's 'primary product' test.
ideas.skr_role: SKR becomes the price of verified human attention. (1) Proposing a question requires an SKR bond, and the queue is curated by one-device-one-vote upvotes, which builds the SKR whitepaper's still-unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curator' idea. (2) Sponsors pay SKR to ask the verified-Seeker panel. (3) That SKR goes to the Seekers who answered, so it is funded by real demand rather than emissions. No staking is involved. This is the strongest SKR-prize candidate in this set.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: 9:00 on a real Seeker. The phone buzzes and the widget reads 'Pulse #217: Would you sell your Seeker for 2 SOL today?' 5-10s: tap 'No' on the widget and touch the fingerprint sensor (no wallet sheet), then slide to 'I think 70% say No'. 10-14s: Solscan shows the vote transaction carrying a secp256r1 precompile instruction and 'voter: SGT #48,211'. 14-17s: a laptop script moves the same SGT to another wallet and tries to vote again, and the program rejects it: 'one Seeker, one voice'. 17-20s: jump to 21:00. A haptic drumroll reveals '73% No - you read the room within 3 points', and the share card posts to X.
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: every Seeker owner becomes part of the product, a shared daily object for all 121k devices (his 'first 10k users' line made literal). The secp256r1 votes and in-program SGT checks are frontier work, and the daily questions can be meme-aware. Mert: the premise is anti-bot and anti-fake-metrics, it runs on real infrastructure (Parsed Events, DAS, relayed transactions), and it has a privacy roadmap (private tallying via MagicBlock's private TEE rollup or Arcium). Chase: sentiment research from verified crypto users is scarce and polluted by bots, sponsors pay from day one, and the Wordle-style share loop gives free distribution. Akshay and Beeman: nothing is more Seeker-native (SGT, .skr, widget, Keystore). It wakes dormant owners with a 5-second daily habit, and Solana Mobile can run its own community consultations on it. Ethelsec: one vote per device is enforced on-chain, not by a server. Keys are hardware-bound, votes use commit-reveal with replay protection per question, the relayer cannot forge votes, and keys are attested.
ideas.closest_existing: X and Telegram polls are full of bots. Wordle has the daily shared object but no verified identity. Family Feud's 'survey says' and Keynesian beauty contests supply the game mechanic. Pollfish and Prolific sell paid research panels. World App polls use Orb-verified humans. Snapshot is token-weighted. Foresee (a MONOLITH winner) runs social prediction markets with SKR and accuracy reputation. U$ER (SagaDAO) is SGT-gated paid app testing, and clockin-canvas is daily check-in pixels. Pulse differs because it is not a prediction market (players have no external event, odds or positions), voting needs no wallet thanks to the hardware key, anyone can verify on-chain that each device voted once, and SKR prices verified attention.
ideas.technical_depth: The repo shows the first public on-chain SGT verification, secp256r1 instruction introspection (including low-S normalization of Keystore DER signatures), commit-reveal with an on-chain tally over a memberNumber bitmap, SKR bond, slashing and sponsor-escrow logic, and Kora relayer integration. On the client and server side: an Android Key Attestation verifier service, an interactive Glance widget with a BiometricPrompt trampoline, automatic reveal through WorkManager, and a Parsed Events cohort pipeline with opt-in consent. Fuzz tests cover double votes, moved SGTs and replays. An optional on-device model groups free-text 'why' answers into the daily results card, covering the possible AI score.
key_risks: Content is the product: bland questions will kill it (the BeReal lesson), so it needs a question pipeline and editorial taste every single day.
Sponsor demand is unproven. Without sponsors, rewards are points only, which worked for Wordle but is weaker for an airdrop-conditioned audience.
Revealed votes are public on-chain and linked to an SGT pseudonym, which may discourage honest answers; private tallying is a stretch goal.
Activation of the secp256r1 precompile, StrongBox availability on Seeker, and the relayer's spam economics all need checking. Key attestation is verified off-chain, not on-chain.
If the game design is not clearly distinct, judges could lump 'predict the crowd' in with the saturated prediction-market category or with daily check-in apps.
SGTs can move between a user's own accounts, so re-binding must be clean. Farms holding many real Seekers remain a residual sybil risk.

ideas.name: Parachute
ideas.one_liner: A wallet guardian that fights back: when a drainer moves on your Seeker, Parachute fires a rescue you pre-signed with one double-tap and pulls everything into your own vault, locked for 72 hours, in one atomic transaction. One tap on the locked screen does the same under duress.
ideas.core_concept: Pre-sign scanners (Solflare's simulation, and Totem in this hackathon) warn you before you sign. But the drains Seeker owners describe on Reddit are 'smart trigger' drainers that use a delegate or authority granted earlier. Parachute covers what happens after the signature. Once a week the user 'packs' a parachute: one Seed Vault double-tap signs a durable-nonce tx v1 rescue transaction. It moves the full balance of every listed token account, and all SOL except fees, into the user's own Squads v4 vault, which has a 72-hour timelock that the user's guardians can cancel. The signed transaction is stored encrypted on the phone and with Parachute's guardian service. A Helius LaserStream/Parsed Streams watcher applies detection rules to the wallet: a new Approve to a delegate not on the allowlist, a SetAuthority, outflows the user didn't start, or contact with a drainer another Seeker has already flagged. When a rule fires, the service broadcasts the rescue through Helius Sender with a Jito tip, trying to land a slot before the drainer's pull. The signed rescue can only move your assets into your own vault, so if it leaks, nothing is lost. The pre-signed durable nonce, the tool behind Drift's $286M loss, becomes the defense. A lock-screen Quick Settings tile, 'Pull the cord', fires the same rescue without unlocking the phone or opening Seed Vault. A thief or a wrench attacker finds a timelock instead of a balance, and if the phone is taken, the owner can pull the cord from any browser using a passkey. Two things give it a daily layer. A rent-back and hygiene card handles SIMD-0437 rent reclaim, closing empty accounts and revoking stale approvals. A 'herd immunity' feed spreads every flagged drainer to all Seekers, so one rescue anywhere protects everyone. The goal is to make Seeker the safest crypto phone, not just the one with a secure element.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: the widget shield ('Armed - covers 97% of $1,240 - packed 2d ago'), a push when a new asset arrives uncovered ('Repack: 1 tap'), and a morning herd feed ('3 Parachutes fired overnight; 1 new drainer flagged; you have 0 approvals to it'). Action: one tap clears today's hygiene card (reclaim rent, close empty accounts or revoke a stale delegate), or one double-tap repacks. Variable reward: real SOL recovered as rent reduction rolls out, a rising safety score, and occasionally a rescue that literally saves your money. Investment: a vault with guardians, a packed parachute, and reports that protect other Seekers. Honest note: this habit is insurance-shaped, weekly more than daily.
mobile_native_surfaces: Quick Settings tile 'Pull the cord' that works from the lock screen (it broadcasts an already-signed transaction, so no unlock or Seed Vault is needed)
Android 16 Live Update while a rescue runs ('Rescue: 5/6 assets secured to Vault, unlocks in 72h')
Glance shield widget (coverage %, last pack, threats) updated through Helius to FCM pushes
Seed Vault double-tap as the weekly 'pack your parachute' ritual (sign-only)
Signed rescue stored encrypted with a Keystore AES-GCM key, and a passkey-triggered remote cord from a second device
ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT 'Check with Parachute' on any address selected in X or Telegram, plus high-priority full-screen alerts with strong haptics
ideas.solana_integration: The rescue is a tx v1 (4 KB) transaction using a durable nonce account whose nonce authority is the user; the larger size fits dozens of token accounts atomically without address lookup tables. A tiny stateless Pinocchio 'sweep_all' program transfers each passed account's entire balance to the vault's token accounts. It skips frozen or closed accounts so one failure doesn't abort the rescue, and it holds nothing. Custody reuses the audited Squads v4 (time lock, spending limits for small instant withdrawals, guardians added by .skr name), so no new custody code is written. Detection runs on Helius LaserStream and Parsed Streams; broadcast uses Helius Sender plus a Jito bundle, and 250 ms slots decide the race. A separate tx v1 hygiene batch runs WithdrawExcessLamports rent reclaim, CloseAccount and Revoke. A herd-immunity registry program lets SGT-verified devices flag addresses, one flag per SGT, verified on-chain. The subscription business model is itself a Subscriptions & Allowances merchant Plan ($2.99 a month in USDC, capped and revocable), so the product uses the same safe pull pattern it recommends. Why on-chain: the rescue has to win an on-chain race, and the vault's timelock is what makes coercion pointless.
ideas.ore_detail: Not an ORE product.
ideas.skr_role: none (deliberately: gamifying a security product invites fake reports, so SKR is not forced in)
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-4s: split screen. On the left, a laptop runs a 'free airdrop' dApp's drainer that holds a delegate approval; on the right, a locked Seeker. 4-9s: the drainer starts its transferFrom. The Seeker buzzes and a Live Update chip reads 'Parachute deployed'. 9-14s: Solscan shows Parachute's rescue landing one slot earlier and the drainer's transaction failing with insufficient funds; the assets sit in the Squads vault, 'unlocks in 72h'. 14-20s: a hand grabs the phone. The owner taps 'Pull the cord' on the lock screen, with no unlock and no wallet, and the remaining balance moves to the vault. 'A wrench can't open a timelock.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Ethelsec (two of the seven judges): it turns the Drift attack tool (pre-signed durable nonces) into a defense whose effect is provably bounded. It reuses audited custody (Squads v4), no server key can move funds anywhere except the user's own vault, and it ships a threat model plus race tests; this is the security-first product they are on the panel to find. Mert: Helius LaserStream, Parsed Streams and Sender are the engine, detection runs only on the user's own addresses, and the shared threat intelligence respects privacy and has no fake metrics. Toly: latency is literally the product, since 250 ms slots decide who wins the race, and safe phones are a prerequisite for internet capital markets on mobile. Akshay and Beeman: security is Seeker's core pitch, and the lock-screen tile, Live Update and widget are native surfaces no PWA can reach. It fills the store's documented gap of zero drainer-protection apps and answers the drain stories on Reddit. Chase: fear of drains is the community's loudest pain, and users should pay for protection much as they pay for insurance, through an on-chain subscription.
ideas.closest_existing: Totem Wallet, a visible Clock In competitor (Kotlin, about 291 commits), is a full Seeker wallet with pre-sign receipts and risk scoring. Solflare, which designed Seed Vault Wallet, has simulation, scam warnings and delegation alerts. Blowfish (now part of Phantom) and Blockaid scan transactions before signing. Revoke.cash-style approval managers and Sol-Incinerator/Step close accounts. On EVM, whitehats use Flashbots 'rescue bundles' to save compromised keys by hand. Squads v4 already offers time locks, and Argent pioneered guardians. Parachute differs because it acts after the signature: an automated, pre-authorized counter-transaction that races drains, a duress cord on the lock screen or from another device, and shared protection across SGT-verified devices. It complements pre-sign scanners rather than duplicating them.
ideas.technical_depth: A Kotlin/Compose app (more credible for a security product) using clientlib-ktx sign-only MWA, a durable-nonce lifecycle manager, a tx v1 builder that packs 40-60 accounts, and Keystore-wrapped storage of the signed rescue. A Rust guardian service on LaserStream/Parsed Streams with a detection-rule engine, a replayable test corpus and Sender/Jito broadcast, plus Surfpool mainnet-fork race tests in which a scripted drainer competes with the rescue. The Pinocchio sweep_all program and the SGT-verified herd registry are fuzz-tested. The app also integrates the Squads v4 SDK, the QS tile, Live Update and widget, and a passkey web cord. An on-device LLM explains each threat in plain English (covering the possible AI score). The README ships a full threat model covering a leaked rescue transaction, a key thief advancing the nonce, false positives and a compromised relayer.
key_risks: Stickiness is the weak criterion: insurance-shaped products get opened weekly, not daily, and the rent-back card and herd feed may not sustain daily engagement.
MWA's sign-only path (solana:signTransactions) is deprecated. If Seed Vault Wallet does not support it, the durable-nonce design fails and needs a Swig or Squads guardian-role fallback.
Durable-nonce support inside tx v1, and production tx v1 support in Seed Vault Wallet, must be verified on a device.
A drainer bundling in the same slot can win the race, and a thief who has the key can advance the nonce to disarm the parachute, so the pitch must not over-promise.
False positives lock funds for 72 hours. A guardian or allowance fast-unlock is needed that does not reopen the duress hole.
Coverage gaps: NFTs and compressed NFTs, stake accounts, and LP and perp positions are not swept by a simple transfer.
Direct competition from Totem in this same hackathon and from Solflare's built-in features; judges may see the category as already covered.

lens: FUSION / WILDCARD. Each idea fuses two or three unrelated mechanics (a proven Web2 ritual, a physical or hardware behaviour on the phone, and a real on-chain engine) into one sentence a judge can retell. Each also reads 'Clock In' sideways rather than as a check-in button: (1) Heads Down: you clock in by putting the phone down; (2) Whistle: a mine's shift whistle, blown BeReal-style; (3) Clocked: slang for spotting a scam; (4) Foreman: managers clock into shifts on your rig while you're away. Three are ORE-core because ORE's DiscretionaryBps executor (Aug 17, 2026) is the only way to run ~78 s rounds under MWA's foreground-only signing without custody. I checked the ORE source: one Automation per authority; the executor picks the amount (capped) and the tiles bitmask; the fee is ≤100 bps of deployed value, charged once per round; and the executor can only deploy or return funds. One idea is deliberately ORE-free for diversity. Novelty check (read-only): no public GitHub repos turned up for ORE+focus/sleep, ORE social/pool apps on mobile, or scam-sweep bounty apps.

ideas.name: Heads Down
ideas.one_liner: Put your Seeker face-down and it starts mining ORE; pick it up and the rig goes cold. It's the crypto phone that pays off when you stop using it.
ideas.core_concept: Heads Down fuses Forest's focus timer (leave the app and your tree dies), Pokemon Sleep's bedtime ritual and the dinner-table 'phone stack' game (the first to touch their phone pays), all running on ORE's native Automation account. You clock in from a Quick Settings tile placed next to Android's Do Not Disturb. One Seed Vault double-tap funds that session's budget into your own ORE Automation, with Heads Down's DiscretionaryBps executor as executor. While the phone lies face-down with the screen off (checked by accelerometer, proximity and screen-state broadcasts in a foreground service), the executor deploys your per-round amount into each ~78 s round. When you unlock, a signed 'break' goes out; after a 10 s grace period the rig stops, and the rest of the budget stays in an automation only you can withdraw. There are three modes. Focus covers deep-work blocks. Night Shift arms at bedtime on the charger and reveals the haul at alarm time; doomscrolling at 2am cools the rig. Stack is for friends, in the same room or remote: each posts an SKR bond and the first to flinch forfeits to the others.
