The core value survives with token rewards removed: it is a focus and sleep ritual with social accountability, and ORE is the variable reward and the hard money you accumulate. The app is honest that marginal mining is currently -EV (production cost ~$104 vs ~$85 price). It shows a live EV meter and by default mines only when the Motherlode is large enough to push rounds near break-even (Motherlode EV per round = Motherlode/500 ORE). Why now: Solana Mobile's own Seeker Summer tagline was 'Less scrolling. More seeking.'; ORE on mobile is only a PWA plus bot autominers; and DiscretionaryBps executors make hands-free, non-custodial mining possible.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: (a) Morning: the Night Shift exact alarm opens on a lock-screen haul reveal: rounds mined, hits, ORE earned, and whether you were on the tile when a Motherlode landed (or 'the Motherlode was too lean, your SOL stayed put'). (b) Workday: the Heads Down tile and the widget's 'rig heat' prompt a focus block. (c) Evening: a friend's Stack invite. ACTION: one swipe plus one double-tap to fund, then the real action, which is not touching the phone. VARIABLE REWARD: a single haptic reveal of tile hits when the session ends, rare Motherlode catches (about 2.2 Motherlode events per day across ORE), Stack wins and losses, and friends' rigs going cold in the crew view. INVESTMENT: unclaimed ORE (which earns ORE's 10% refining-fee redistribution while held), a lifetime 'proof of focus' profile keyed to your SGT mint, rig heat built over consecutive days (2 automatic freezes per week), and standing focus rooms with your crew. With no airdrop at all, people return because they want the focus block and the sleep, and the morning reveal is a Wordle-sized curiosity hit.
mobile_native_surfaces: Quick Settings tile 'Heads Down' (TileService; startActivityAndCollapse into a translucent trampoline Activity that runs the MWA session; sits next to the system DND tile)

Android 16 Live Update (NotificationCompat.ProgressStyle + setRequestPromotedOngoing) for a user-initiated focus or sleep session: status-bar chip 'Heads down 18:40, rig hot', lock screen and AOD; degrades to an ongoing notification on older builds
Jetpack Glance home-screen widget: today's haul, rig heat, crew rigs; an embedded Chronometer ticks without update calls; refreshed by Helius webhook -> FCM

Foreground service sensor fusion: accelerometer face-down detection, proximity sensor, ACTION_SCREEN_ON/ACTION_USER_PRESENT broadcasts, optional UsageStatsManager allow-list (calls/maps don't break a session)
Exact alarm (USE_EXACT_ALARM, acceptable on dApp Store distribution) with full-screen intent for the Night Shift reveal
Seed Vault double-tap + fingerprint as the literal clock-in ritual via MWA (@wallet-ui/react-native-kit or clientlib-ktx)
Android Keystore P-256 key with Key Attestation for signed heartbeats in Stack mode
Nearby Connections / BLE so phones at the same table see each other in an in-person Stack
Android 16 envelope haptics for the end-of-session and morning reveal
Battery-optimization exemption prompt (dApp Store build) so stationary sessions survive Doze
SGT gating and .skr names for crews and Stack tables
ideas.solana_integration: ORE program (oreV3EG1...): the user signs `automate` once per session or top-up. It deposits the budget, sets executor = the Heads Down executor, strategy = DiscretionaryBps (e.g. 50 bps, cap 100), a per-tile amount cap, and native conditions (min Motherlode, max production cost). The executor deploys only while the device's focus state is valid. The source confirms an executor can only deploy (amount capped, tiles by bitmask) or return funds to the authority, never withdraw to itself, so there is no custody. Users claim ORE and SOL themselves. Heads Down program (Anchor or Pinocchio): (1) Seat PDA [b"seat", sgt_mint], created only after on-chain SGT verification: the Token-2022 account is owned by the signer with amount 1, the mint's TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89nU4iWFkNXj1Bw6uYhJJWDRPpShHt4Bk8f99Te, and mint authority == GT2zuHVaZQYZSyQMgJPLzvkmyztfyXg2NJunqFp4p3A4. The seat stores the attested Keystore P-256 pubkey plus focus-hours and streak counters (one Seeker, one seat; SGT moves between the user's own wallets are handled by re-checking the current holder). (2) StackTable PDA with an SKR vault PDA, participant seats and start/end slots. Settlement is permissionless: each participant's last heartbeat {table, slot, state=down} is verified with the secp256r1 precompile (instruction introspection); the earliest last-heartbeat before end_slot is the flincher; bonds are redistributed; timeout refunds apply if no one settles. Executor: a Rust service on Helius LaserStream/websocket for board and round accounts. It deploys late in the round with crowd-aware tile placement and batches member deploys into Transaction v1 (4 KB). Each deploy adds only 3 member-unique accounts (authority, automation, miner) to a shared set, so roughly 20 members fit per transaction, subject to compute limits. That cranks cheaper than ORE's 7,000-lamport permissionless executor. What must be on-chain and why: non-custodial mining (ORE Automation); bonds between people settled without trusting the team (secp256r1-verified heartbeats); and one-device-one-seat fairness plus a public focus record (SGT-keyed PDAs).
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the engine and the thing users accumulate: every focus minute is a real deploy on the ORE board, every morning reveal is real ORE mined. The app delivers ORE's own abandoned 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker' promise (claim_seeker was shipped and removed in 2025) as a consumer product, and adds new, human, non-bot miners to a board that sees only ~150-165 miners per round. It is built for the matched prize: live on mainnet, ORE-branded in the demo, and milestones pitched as ORE miners added, SOL deployed and weekly active focus-miners.
ideas.skr_role: Stack mode stake: friends (in the same room or remote) each escrow SKR in a StackTable. The first phone to flinch, proven by secp256r1-verified hardware heartbeats, forfeits its bond to the others. SKR is the stake in a hardware-verified self-control contest, the same pattern that won MONOLITH's SKR prize for Seek. It is not staking, not checkout and not an emissions reward.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0:00 Night, on a real Seeker. The founder pulls down the shade and taps 'Heads Down' beside Do Not Disturb. Seed Vault bottom sheet, side-button double-tap, fingerprint: 'Rig armed'. 0:05 He lays the phone face-down; a soft haptic thud. A screen capture shows the status-bar chip 'rig hot', and a laptop beside him shows the live ORE board with his .skr name landing on tiles each round. 0:10 He picks the phone up; the chip flashes 'Rig cooling... 10'. He sets it back down: 'hot'. 0:14 Hard cut to 7:00am: the alarm opens on the lock-screen haul reveal counting up '212 rounds, 9 hits, +0.41 ORE', with haptic thumps. Caption: 'My phone mines when I'm not using it.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: ORE-style proof of work turned into a human habit; an honest EV meter instead of yield hype; a trust-minimized settlement that is one of the few consumer uses of the secp256r1 precompile. 'Put the phone down and it mines' is a meme he will repeat. MERT: the executor runs on Helius LaserStream, the haul history on Parsed Events, and widget freshness on webhook -> FCM; everything can be checked on-chain. CHASE: a proven consumer format (Forest, Pokemon Sleep, phone-stack) with a clear first-10k-users wedge (focus and sleep, not trading), and a daily reveal that drives word of mouth. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: the app is only possible on a Seeker. It uses the QS tile, Live Update, Glance, sensors, the Seed Vault ritual, on-chain SGT and .skr, and MWA wired properly with wallet-ui. It is great PR for Solana Mobile's 'less scrolling' message while still producing organic daily on-chain activity rather than synthetic memo check-ins. ETHELSEC: users never give up custody (executor powers are deploy-or-return only), and the blast radius of a compromised executor key is bounded. Keystore attestation, SIWS single-use nonces, SGT uniqueness by mint, pull-based bond claims and a threat model in the README give them something substantial to review.
ideas.closest_existing: Forest and Flora (Flora already takes real-money focus stakes) and 'Hold' (rewards students for phone-free time): Web2, no chain, no mining. Sleepagotchi on Seeker (sleep-to-earn, 4,269 reviews): emission-funded, not ORE, not hardware-gated. ORE autominers (Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer, refinORE, Radiants' lodestar-cli): 24/7 bots with no ritual or behaviour gate. Solarma (SOL-staked alarm, devnet), bozPledge and Moonwalk (stake on steps): commitment stakes on a different verified behaviour, with no ORE. Kinlog: a camera exercise habit. The difference: nobody gates a real, non-custodial ORE rig on the physical state of the phone, and nobody turns phone-stack self-control into a settled SKR contest. Honest caveat: the brief itself lists 'focus x ORE' as an example, so other entrants may reach the same headline. The phone-down, sleep and stack framing, the secp256r1 heartbeats and the executor design are what have to set it apart.
ideas.technical_depth: Repo shows: (1) a Kotlin/Compose app, or Expo SDK 57 with custom Kotlin Expo Modules, covering the foreground-service sensor state machine, TileService, Glance widget, ProgressStyle Live Update, exact alarms, Keystore P-256 key generation with an attestation chain, and Nearby/BLE table discovery; (2) an Anchor program for SGT verification on-chain (Token-2022 extension parsing), Seat/StackTable PDAs, an SKR escrow vault, secp256r1-precompile heartbeat verification via instruction introspection, and timeout refunds, with LiteSVM/bankrun tests plus fuzzing of the settlement ordering; (3) a Rust executor with a LaserStream subscription, crowd-aware late placement, v1 batch builder, Jito tips, liveness monitoring and a kill switch; (4) a Codama-generated client from ORE's api/idl.json (ORE has no official TS SDK); (5) SIWS with server nonces, auth tokens in encrypted storage, and assetlinks.json dapp identity; (6) a README threat model covering executor compromise, heartbeat spoofing and Doze. An optional AI-rubric hedge: an on-device LiteRT-LM model (Gemma 3 1B on CPU) writes the morning haul narrative and explains the EV. Target: steady granular commits across the month plus a mainnet dApp Store build.
key_risks: Economics: marginal ORE mining is currently -EV (production cost ~$104 vs ~$85 price, losing tiles return 89.1%), so users partly 'pay to focus'. The EV meter, Motherlode-threshold defaults and tiny budgets mitigate but don't remove this.
Focus detection is spoofable (rooted phone, modified APK, a second phone). That's harmless in solo mode, but Stack bonds rely on Key Attestation and must stay small.

Doze and OEM battery management may suspend heartbeats on stationary unplugged phones. The design needs the battery-optimization exemption plus a 'report on break' model; Seeker behaviour is untested.
Ideological friction: an app that wants you off the phone could read as anti-engagement to a device maker, even though it still generates daily sessions and real on-chain activity.

The executor is a team-run hot key. If compromised it can bleed users' budgets at about -11% per round, up to their caps, until they revoke. Liveness is on the team, because DiscretionaryBps automations can't fall back to ORE's permissionless executor.
Dependencies are unverified on Seeker: secp256r1 precompile activation on mainnet, Keystore attestation quality, Live Updates on the MR7 Android 16 build, and FCM/Play Services availability.
ORE program changes (V4 already changed payouts in Aug 2026) can break the executor. The ORE match also requires long-term support and usage milestones.
Gambling optics around the Motherlode, and possible dApp Store or regional regulatory scrutiny.
Headline overlap: 'focus mines ORE' is an obvious fusion that other Clock In teams may also build.

ideas.name: Whistle (the Seeker Swarm)
ideas.one_liner: Once a day the mine whistle blows at a random moment, and verified Seekers everywhere have three minutes to clock into the same ORE shift, spread across the whole board so that when a big Motherlode lands, the Swarm is on it.
ideas.core_concept: Whistle fuses BeReal's random daily notification (a short window, everyone at once), Pokemon GO's community events and a mining pool, and it avoids the custody problem mining pools usually have. Every SGT-verified Seeker holds exactly one seat and keeps their own ORE Automation, with the Whistle executor as the DiscretionaryBps executor; no funds are pooled. At an unannounced moment in each region's daytime the whistle blows. Members have 3 minutes to clock in with one double-tap that tops up that Rush's budget and records attendance on-chain. For ~15 rounds the executor then places every member's stake across the board with a water-filling allocation against the live board, so the Swarm covers all 25 tiles without members diluting each other. (Stacking a crowd on one tile would be sharply -EV, because a tile can pay out at most 1 ORE.) Between Rushes, a 'Standing Swarm' of opted-in members mines only when the Motherlode is large (e.g. at least 200 ORE, where rounds approach break-even). So whenever a big Motherlode hits, Swarm members are on the winning tile, their .skr names light up, and every clocked-in phone buzzes at once. ORE currently sees only ~150-165 miners and ~9-11.5 SOL per round, so 1,000 Seekers at 0.002 SOL per round would be roughly a sixth of the board. The 'Seeker Swarm' would become a visible force on a top Solana protocol and deliver the Seeker mining that ORE advertised and never shipped. Without token rewards, it is a live, synchronized event with your people plus real ORE. Honest caveat: individual variance is not pooled, so the Swarm always 'wins' something each round but you personally win only when your tiles hit.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: the whistle (once per region per day, random time, heads-up plus full-screen). There are also Motherlode alarms when the jackpot crosses a threshold, and crewmates who have already clocked in. ACTION: tap the notification, then a trampoline Activity, then one double-tap within 3 minutes (the top-up and the attendance record in a single transaction). After that, just glance at the Live Update chip. VARIABLE REWARD: which rounds your tiles hit, the unison buzz as each round resolves, the rare Motherlode caught by named Swarm members (maybe you), regional pride (Asia vs EMEA vs Americas shift leaderboards) and the Captain's banner. INVESTMENT: a shift streak with automatic freezes, seat-seniority badges, crew standing inside the Swarm, and unclaimed ORE earning refining-fee redistribution. It brings people back with no airdrop because missing the whistle means missing the moment. That is BeReal's pull, backed by real stakes and a persistent community goal: the Swarm's share of ORE.
mobile_native_surfaces: High-priority FCM whistle notification (heads-up plus full-screen intent) with a 'Clock in' action into a translucent trampoline Activity for MWA

Android 16 Live Update for the user-initiated shift: ProgressStyle segments = rounds ('Swarm Rush, 1,204 Seekers, round 9/15'), status-bar chip, lock screen and AOD; no price ticker or pre-event countdown, per Google's rules
Synchronized haptics (Android 16 envelope haptics) on round resolution: the 'stadium buzz' across every clocked-in phone
Glance widget: live Swarm size, the Swarm's share of the ORE board, the last Motherlode catch with .skr names, your streak
Quick Settings tile 'Clock In' (join the next Rush or toggle Standing Swarm)
Seed Vault double-tap + fingerprint as the punch clock
Share sheet: an auto-generated, spoiler-style shift card for X and Telegram ('Rush #88: 1,204 Seekers, 15/15 rounds hit, Motherlode caught 212 ORE')
SGT seat and .skr names rendered on the live 5x5 board
ideas.solana_integration: ORE: one Automation per member (confirmed one per authority), with executor = the Whistle executor, strategy DiscretionaryBps (≤100 bps, charged once per round on total deployed), native conditions (min/max Motherlode for the Standing Swarm), and per-tile amount caps. The executor chooses each member's squares bitmask and amount within the cap, and can only deploy or return funds, so the Swarm is a mining pool with zero custody. Whistle program: Seat PDA [b"seat", sgt_mint], created after on-chain SGT verification (TokenGroupMember.group == GT22s89..., mint authority == GT2zuH..., the signer's Token-2022 account holds 1). Shift PDA: id, start slot, round range, captain, flavor, member count. ClockIn PDA [shift, seat], created in the same transaction as the Automation top-up, which makes attendance public and auditable. Captain's Chair: an SKR bid escrow with a highest-bid-wins close 5 minutes before the Rush, and proceeds claimable pro-rata by that shift's ClockIn seats (pull-based, no loops). Executor: a Rust service on Helius LaserStream reading the board, round and treasury. It computes a water-filling allocation against other miners' live deployments, deploys late in the round (250 ms slots leave room) and batches ~20 member deploys per Transaction v1. Each ORE deploy adds only authority, automation and miner as member-specific accounts to a shared board/config/round/treasury/entropy set. Why it must be on-chain: one-human-one-seat has to be publicly verifiable, custody has to stay with each member, and attendance plus SKR splits have to be auditable by anyone, including the ORE team checking usage milestones.
ideas.ore_detail: The product is a coordinated community of ORE miners. Every Rush and every standing deploy is ORE mining, and the headline metric is the Seeker Swarm's share of ORE's board (miners and SOL per round). It gives ORE a native Seeker experience, turns scattered Seeker owners into a durable miner base (ORE sees ~150-165 miners per round today), and generates exactly the usage metrics the milestone-paid match asks for. A co-branded 'Seeker Swarm' leaderboard on ore.com would be a natural ask.
ideas.skr_role: Captain's Chair auction: each Rush's captaincy is auctioned in SKR. The captain's .skr name and banner appear on every member's Live Update chip and widget ('Captain alice.skr has the shift'), with a bounded choice of flavour: split/solo mix and the Motherlode threshold, never custody or anything that changes EV materially. 100% of the winning SKR bid is split among the seats that clocked in. SKR becomes a status and attention currency inside a sybil-proof crowd, funded by users rather than emissions. It is not staking, checkout, a spin wheel or an earn leaderboard.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0:00 Three Seekers on a table next to a laptop showing a world map of seats. All three phones scream at once: WHISTLE. 0:04 Three thumbs, three side-button double-taps, three fingerprints; each status bar fills with 'Swarm Rush, 214 Seekers'. 0:09 On the laptop the live ORE board shows Swarm stakes spread across all 25 tiles, labelled with .skr names. 0:13 The round resolves: all three phones buzz in perfect unison and tile 17 lights up with names. 0:16 Cut to a real test clip: 'MOTHERLODE: caught by 6 Seekers, 212 ORE' and a tester's reaction. Caption: 'Clock in together.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: mechanism design. It is a mining pool without custody, one human per seat via SGT, and an honest water-filling allocation that shows the team understands ORE's economics (with the one-tile trap explicitly avoided). 250 ms slots and Transaction v1 are used for something real. MERT: the executor and the live board run on LaserStream and Parsed Events, and the Swarm's share of the board can be checked by any indexer. CHASE: BeReal's appointment plus Pokemon GO's community event plus real stakes gives the FOMO trigger that consumer apps crave, and the unison-buzz moment is inherently shareable. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: it turns ~121K scattered Seekers into one visible force on a top Solana protocol, includes the first public example of verifying the SGT inside a program, is Seeker-only by construction, and is ready-made for Seeker Season quests. ETHELSEC: per-member automations (no pooled vault), executor powers limited to deploy-or-return, pull-based SKR claims, SGT uniqueness by mint and bounded captain powers.
ideas.closest_existing: ORE's own permissionless autominer and third-party autominers (Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer, refinORE, lodestar-cli) are individual bots with no social layer. Evore's managed-miner program has custody-style pooling. Tramplin (a MONOLITH winner) runs random-winner staking every 10 minutes: similar 'frequent shared draw' energy but a different product and not ORE. BeReal (random daily prompt), Pokemon GO Community Day and Bitcoin mining pools are the source mechanics. The difference: nobody has built a synchronized, SGT-seated, non-custodial social layer on ORE for mobile. The closest idea is the 'ORE Crews' research seed, which is crew-scale; Whistle is community-scale and event-driven.
ideas.technical_depth: (1) Anchor program: on-chain SGT verification; Seat/Shift/ClockIn PDAs; SKR auction escrow with pull claims; exhaustive account, owner and signer checks; LiteSVM tests plus property tests on the auction. (2) Rust executor: LaserStream ingestion, water-filling allocation against live board state, late-round deploy timing, a Transaction v1 batch builder with compute budgeting, retry and Jito logic, and a load test simulating 1,000 automations per ~78 s round under contention on the shared writable board and round accounts. (3) Notification fan-out with per-region random scheduling, FCM data messages and delivery telemetry. (4) Native Android modules: Live Update ProgressStyle, Glance widget, TileService, synchronized haptic patterns, trampoline Activity for MWA. (5) A Codama client from ORE's IDL. (6) A public dashboard of the Swarm's share of ORE, verifiable against Helius data. A README threat model covers executor compromise, liveness and auction griefing.
key_risks: Cold start: the spectacle needs hundreds of seats, and with 30 testers the Rush looks small. The demo should show share of the ORE board rather than raw headcount.
Economics: mining is -EV except in high-Motherlode regimes. Random whistle times are not timed to EV, so Rush budgets must stay tiny, and the honest message is 'a cheap ticket to a shared event'.
Individual variance is not pooled (no custody), so 'the Swarm won' is not the same as 'you won'. Users may misread it; the UI must separate the two.
Executor capacity: ~1,000 deploys per ~78 s round contend on shared writable ORE accounts. ORE's compute per deploy is unknown, so the batch size (~20 per transaction) needs benchmarking.
Gambling optics: a 'synchronized jackpot' is exactly what regulators and some judges will frown at. Framing it as mining, showing EV and keeping the design non-custodial all matter.
Notification reliability and FCM/Play Services availability on Seeker are unconfirmed; random whistles across time zones may frustrate some users.
The Captain's Chair could read as frivolous or pay-to-win; captain powers have to stay cosmetic or bounded.
ORE program updates can break the executor, and the ORE match requires ongoing milestones and support.

ideas.name: Clocked
ideas.one_liner: Scammers airdrop junk into every Seeker. Clocked turns each piece into rent money for you and a bounty for the verified Seekers who 'clock' the scam, and one daily 'would you sign this?' puzzle trains you never to get drained.
ideas.core_concept: Clocked fuses Wordle (one shared daily puzzle with a spoiler-free share grid), inbox-zero spam cleaning and bug-bounty hunting, aimed at Seeker owners' most documented fear: wallet drains. It also fills a dApp Store category with zero apps. Every morning a Helius-webhook digest lists what landed overnight: spam SPL tokens, phishing NFTs, new delegations. One double-tap sends a batched Transaction v1 that burns junk, closes the accounts, revokes stale delegations and reclaims rent. As each SIMD-0437 rent-reduction step lands, it also withdraws excess lamports from kept accounts via WithdrawExcessLamports. The scammer paid that rent: you keep 95%, and 5% funds the hunter pool, so the scammers fund the hunters. Unknown mints, programs or domains can be 'clocked': an SGT-verified hunter posts a small SKR bond, and flags confirmed optimistically (≥3 independent seats, no successful challenge within 72 h) earn from the pool, while wrong flags forfeit the bond to the challenger. The resulting Seeker Shield is an on-chain public registry any wallet or dApp can read. The same registry powers X-ray: select any address, URL or .skr in any app (ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT), share a link or Blink, or scan a Solana Pay QR, and Clocked simulates it and explains in plain English what signing would do. The daily Clocked puzzle renders one real transaction from yesterday (a drainer or a decoy) exactly as a Seed Vault approval sheet, and asks what happens if you sign: three guesses, then a share grid. Why now: the dApp Store has zero pre-sign security apps; r/SolanaSeeker is full of drain stories; rent-reduction steps pay out through late 2026; Helius Parsed Events went GA on Sept 25; Transaction v1 makes big cleanups a single signature; and two security researchers are on the panel.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: an 8am push ('3 junk airdrops landed overnight, +0.006 SOL to sweep'), the daily puzzle number (like a Wordle #), and real-time heads-up alerts when a new delegation or approval appears on your wallet. ACTION: a 30-second puzzle, then one double-tap to sweep, then optionally clock an unknown token or domain with a small bond. VARIABLE REWARD: the puzzle result and streak, how much rent came back, whether yesterday's flags were confirmed (bounty) or challenged, and the occasional 'you were targeted by a known drainer; blocked' save. INVESTMENT: a 'days unclocked' streak (days without a risky signature), a hunter reputation tied to your seat's confirmed flags, personal allow and block lists, and a friends leaderboard. Without any airdrop, people return because the fear is real, the found money is real, and the puzzle is a 30-second habit. It is also the one app that pays you when you get spammed.
mobile_native_surfaces: ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT: a 'Clock it' entry in every app's text-selection menu (addresses, URLs, .skr names in X, Telegram, Chrome)
Share-sheet target for links and Blinks; ML Kit code scanner (no camera permission) for Solana Pay QR X-ray before paying
Helius webhook -> FCM digest and real-time heads-up alerts on new delegations
Quick Settings tile 'Panic': revoke all delegations and sweep, via trampoline and one double-tap, reachable from the lock screen with unlockAndRun()
Glance widget: 'days unclocked' streak, junk waiting, today's puzzle status
Seed Vault double-tap for one batched Transaction v1 sweep (fallback: multiple legacy transactions in one MWA request)
Haptics on 'clocked!' detections and the sweep cascade

Optional experimental Guard mode: Clocked registers as an MWA wallet endpoint (walletlib), simulates the incoming request, then forwards it to Seed Vault Wallet through clientlib: an opt-in transaction firewall
On-device plain-English explanations (LiteRT-LM small model on CPU, with a deterministic template fallback)
SGT seat and .skr hunter handles
ideas.solana_integration: Token and Token-2022 programs: burn + close_account for junk accounts, WithdrawExcessLamports for excess rent on kept accounts as rent-reduction steps land, and revoke for delegations. Each close adds about one to two accounts, so a 4 KB Transaction v1 can batch dozens of closes behind a single Seed Vault signature (e.g. 47 accounts x 0.00203928 SOL ≈ 0.096 SOL back). The 5% pool fee moves in the same transaction. Clocked program (Anchor): Seat PDA [b"seat", sgt_mint] with on-chain SGT verification; Flag PDA [b"flag", target, seat] holding an SKR bond in a vault PDA; Target PDA [b"target", address] aggregating flags and status (Pending -> Confirmed/Rejected); a challenge instruction with a counter-bond; permissionless finalize after the window with ≥3 independent seats; disputes escalate to a Squads security multisig behind a timelock; Bounty pool PDA with pull-based claims. The confirmed registry is readable by any wallet or dApp via RPC or CPI, making it an ecosystem public good. Helius: webhooks on the user's wallet, Parsed Events/Streams to decode instructions, DAS for token metadata (phishing URLs live there), getTransactionsForAddress, and simulateTransaction for X-ray diffs. Why it must be on-chain: the blocklist has to be sybil-proof, bonded and owned by no single company, and the money flows (rent, bounties, bonds) are real value, not memo check-ins.
ideas.ore_detail: Deliberately ORE-free, to give the set a non-ORE contender. An optional 'sweep dust into ORE' destination is trivial to add, but it would not qualify as 'ORE as the primary product', and I don't recommend pitching it for the ORE match.
ideas.skr_role: Hunter bonds: SGT-verified hunters bond SKR on each flag. Confirmed flags earn from the bounty pool (funded by 5% of swept scam rent plus sponsors); false flags forfeit the bond to the successful challenger. SKR becomes skin in the game for sybil-proof security curation, applying the SKR whitepaper's still-unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' idea to safety. It is not staking, checkout or emissions.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0:00 A real Seeker wallet screen stuffed with 60+ junk tokens ('CLAIM 5000 USDC AIRDROP - visit...'). The founder: 'Every Seeker looks like this.' 0:04 He taps 'Clock them all': Seed Vault sheet, double-tap, fingerprint. 0:08 A satisfying cascade animation as 47 accounts burn in ONE transaction; the counter lands on '+0.096 SOL back, 12 scams added to the Seeker Shield', with an explorer link. 0:13 He switches to Telegram, long-presses a pasted address, and taps 'Clock it' in the system text menu. A red sheet slides up: 'Signing this moves all your SOL and delegates your USDC. Known drainer, clocked by 9 Seekers.' Caption: 'Scammers pay rent. We collect it.'
ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: clean mechanism design (the attacker's own rent funds the defenders), a public-good registry, and fresh chain features (Transaction v1, rent reduction) used for direct user value. MERT: Helius-native end to end (webhooks, Parsed Events GA, DAS, simulation), security and privacy aligned, and a registry Helius itself could consume. CHASE: an obvious consumer hook ('your wallet's spam folder pays you') plus a Wordle-style shareable daily puzzle. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: it fills a zero-app category on the dApp Store, addresses owners' number-one fear, uses Seeker-native entry points (PROCESS_TEXT, QS tile, widget, Seed Vault ritual), and could plug into Seed Vault Wallet later. ETHELSEC: this is their home turf. It has an explicit threat model, bond and challenge game theory, conservative burn rules with simulation diffs, and an optional MWA firewall they will want to break. Inviting them to sit on the dispute council is a natural story.
ideas.closest_existing: Sol Incinerator and similar web rent-reclaimers are web tools that take a fee and offer no protection or registry. Phantom has built-in spam filtering and Blowfish-powered transaction scanning, Solflare has simulation, and Seed Vault Wallet (designed by Solflare) may already warn on some transactions. Web3 Antivirus, Wallet Guard and Pocket Universe are EVM-first browser extensions. ScamSniffer and Chainabuse are off-chain databases. RugLens (token risk scanner, 340 reviews) and SIMGUARD (1 review) are the only Seeker-store neighbours. The difference: mobile-native pre-sign entry points, a sybil-proof bonded on-chain registry, scammers funding the bounty, and a daily training puzzle. Honest caveat: each component exists somewhere; the fusion and the Seeker-native delivery are what's new.
ideas.technical_depth: (1) Anchor program: flags, challenges, bond escrow, optimistic finalize, multisig escalation, pull claims, full signer/owner/PDA checks, LiteSVM plus adversarial tests (collusion, griefing, double-claims). (2) A sweep builder with hard safety rules: never burn tokens with liquidity or a price, never close accounts holding value, a pre/post balance diff via simulateTransaction shown before signing, user confirmation per category. (3) A Helius pipeline (webhooks, Parsed Events, DAS) with an incident-to-puzzle generator. (4) Native Android modules: PROCESS_TEXT and share intents, QS tile with unlockAndRun, Glance widget, ML Kit scanner. (5) The optional MWA proxy wallet using mobile-wallet-adapter walletlib plus clientlib. (6) On-device LLM explanations with a deterministic fallback, which also hedges the Align AI criterion. (7) A published threat model and security README.
key_risks: The security judges will attack Clocked itself. A burn or close bug that destroys value would be fatal, so conservative rules and simulation diffs are non-negotiable.
The found-money hook decays: rent reduction cuts per-account rent ~90% for new spam, and much spam is compressed NFTs with no rent to reclaim. The first-run windfall is largely one-time.

Optimistic resolution can be gamed by colluding seats or used to grief legitimate projects, and the multisig backstop is a centralization point. Labelling addresses or domains as scams also carries defamation risk.
Incumbents (Phantom/Blowfish, Solflare/Seed Vault Wallet) can ship similar features. Guard mode may confuse users or be declined, because the wallet sees Clocked's identity instead of the dApp's.
Stickiness depends on spam volume and puzzle novelty; security tends to be an 'insurance' category with weaker daily pull than games or money apps.
No ORE match; the SKR prize is uncertain.

ideas.name: Foreman
ideas.one_liner: Idle Miner Tycoon where the ore is real and the managers are real Seekers: hire a verified strategist to run your ORE rig overnight, and a Solana program makes it impossible for them to break the rules they advertised.
ideas.core_concept: Foreman fuses the idle-tycoon genre (Idle Miner Tycoon's core loop is literally 'hire managers to automate your shafts, come back to collect') with a creator marketplace and ORE's DiscretionaryBps executor model. The mapping is exact: in ORE, the third-party executor on your Automation is your manager, and its ≤1% fee is the manager's salary. You own a mine: your single ORE Automation (one per wallet, confirmed from the source). You hire managers for shifts, such as a night-shift grinder or a Motherlode hunter. Managers are SGT-verified Seekers who publish declarative strategies: deploy only when the Motherlode is at least X, cap the per-round amount, tile mask bounds, split/solo preference, time windows, max rounds per day, and late crowd-aware placement. Your Automation's executor is the Foreman Guard PDA. A manager (or the hosted runner executing their strategy) calls Guard, which enforces the declared constraints on-chain, CPIs ORE's deploy via invoke_signed and splits the fee between manager and protocol. A manager cannot deviate from what they advertised, cannot touch principal, and can be fired with one double-tap. The idle-game shell makes ORE's hard-to-follow mechanics readable: shafts = shifts, elevator = claims, refinery = the refining-fee decision, vault = stORE, tailings = buy-and-bury, and the offline-earnings screen is the real on-chain haul. Managers compete on a leaderboard of verifiable ORE-per-SOL over thousands of rounds, so the best strategists earn from many mines, which creates a creator class for ORE. Why now: DiscretionaryBps shipped Aug 17, 2026, ORE has no native mobile consumer app, and idle games are the most proven 'come back tomorrow' format there is.
ideas.daily_loop: TRIGGER: a morning shift-report push and widget ('Night shift by alice.skr: 186 rounds, +0.31 ORE, 2 Motherlode near-misses'). ACTION: open, 'collect' (claim, or leave ORE unrefined to earn refining-fee redistribution), review managers, hire or fire, and top up with one double-tap. VARIABLE REWARD: haul size, Motherlode catches, a manager climbing or falling in the ranks, new strategies to try, level-ups of your mine diorama (cosmetic, earned only from real lifetime deploys). INVESTMENT: your mine's level and history, relationships with managers, and unclaimed ORE. On the other side, managers are the daily power users: they tune strategies, post shift notes and grow a following, because fee income depends on verified performance. It works with no airdrop because it's a game loop over real hard-money accumulation, and for managers it's income.
mobile_native_surfaces: Jetpack Glance widget: a live mine diorama showing the current shift manager and tonight's haul, with a Chronometer for shift time; refreshed by Helius webhook -> FCM
Morning shift-report notification with a rich full-screen art card
Android 16 Live Update when the user starts a 'supervised shift' (watch mode): ProgressStyle rounds, user-initiated
Quick Settings tile 'Pause mine' plus an app shortcut 'Fire all managers' (kill switch via trampoline and double-tap)
120 Hz Compose/Skia animations and haptics on collect and level-up
Seed Vault double-tap for hire, fire and top-up (one automate + Guard contract transaction each)
SGT-verified manager seats; .skr names on manager profiles; share-sheet manager cards for X and Telegram
ideas.solana_integration: ORE: the user's Automation sets executor = the Foreman Guard PDA, strategy = DiscretionaryBps. Native ORE conditions (min/max Motherlode, max production cost) are set in the Automation itself, and ORE enforces that the executor can only deploy (amount capped, tiles by bitmask) or return funds. Foreman Guard program: Manager PDA [b"manager", sgt_mint] with on-chain SGT verification (group GT22s89..., mint authority GT2zuH...). A Strategy PDA holds an immutable, versioned set of declared constraints. A Contract PDA [mine_authority, shift_id] records the hired manager, the time window and the fee split. `execute` checks that the caller is the contracted manager (or a runner acting for them), that the time window and per-day round cap hold, and that the requested squares and amount lie within the declared mask and caps. It reads ORE board, round and treasury state for Motherlode-conditioned rules, then CPIs ORE deploy with the Guard PDA as signer via invoke_signed. Fees land in the Guard PDA and are credited on-chain to manager and protocol earnings PDAs with pull withdrawals. Per-contract counters (SOL deployed, rounds, ORE attributed via miner-account deltas) plus Helius Parsed Events give verifiable track records. Managers with many mines batch executes in Transaction v1. Why it must be on-chain: a marketplace where strangers manage other people's money only works if the rules are enforced by code and track records are verifiable, and SGT stops one strategist from posing as fifty.
ideas.ore_detail: The entire economy is ORE mining. Every mine is an ORE Automation, every shift is ORE deploys, and every manager is an ORE strategist earning ORE's own executor fee. It gives ORE a mobile consumer front door plus a new creator class of strategists, and it maps cleanly to milestone metrics: active automations, SOL deployed per round, and ORE miners added.
ideas.skr_role: Minor, deliberately. An optional SKR listing bond is required to publish a strategy publicly: it deters spam and is slashable to affected mines for impersonation or off-chain misrepresentation, since on-chain misbehaviour is already made impossible by Guard. I would not pitch Foreman for the SKR prize. Keeping the economy ORE/SOL-denominated protects the 'ORE as primary product' requirement.

The founder: 'This mine is real.' 0:05 In the app he opens the manager board and taps Hire on 'alice.skr, Motherlode Hunter: only mines when the Motherlode is at least 250 ORE, verified over 12,000 rounds'. ideas.judge_appeal: TOLY: mechanism design. Least-privilege delegated execution enforced on-chain, and a strategist market on top of ORE's executor primitive. MERT: verifiable manager performance from Helius Parsed Events and indexable contracts, with no leaderboards that rely on trusting the team. CHASE: a massively proven Web2 genre (idle tycoon) with a creator economy on the supply side, which gives both a daily collect loop and a reason for power users to evangelize. AKSHAY/BEEMAN: a widget-first game with a real on-chain economy, SGT-verified creators, and the Seed Vault ritual used for the moments that matter (hire, fire, top-up).
