It is exactly the kind of code they like to review, and exactly where they'll look for bugs.
ideas.closest_existing: Idle Miner Tycoon (Kolibri/Ubisoft), one of the most-downloaded idle games, has no real value. ORE third-party autominers (refinORE, Minemore/Orestack, Oreminer) are single-operator bots with no marketplace and no enforced strategy. Evore's managed-miner program is custody-style. FOMO and other copy-trading apps are social strategy-following for trading, with no on-chain enforcement of declared rules. The 'Strategy Market' research seed is the closest concept. The difference: on-chain enforcement of a manager's declared strategy through a CPI guard, SGT-verified strategist creators, and an idle-game UX that makes ORE understandable.
ideas.technical_depth: (1) Guard program: invoke_signed CPI into ORE deploy, strategy validation against ORE account state, fee accounting and pull withdrawals, versioned immutable strategies, exhaustive account checks, and LiteSVM/bankrun suites including fuzzed malicious managers. (2) A hosted strategy runner in Rust on LaserStream, plus a small SDK so technical managers can self-host executors. (3) A performance indexer with daily Merkle-anchored stats. (4) The game client: Compose/Skia animations, Glance widget, Live Update, QS tile, shortcuts, trampoline MWA flows. (5) A Codama client from ORE's IDL. (6) An optional on-device LLM strategy explainer to hedge the Align AI criterion. (7) A threat-model README covering malicious managers, runner compromise and ORE upgrades.
key_risks: CPI compatibility is unverified: ORE's deploy requires a writable signer and may assume a system-account executor or funding behaviour a PDA can't satisfy. ORE upgrades could also break Guard. This needs a mainnet test first.

The '-EV tycoon' contradiction: the genre sells getting rich, but ORE mining currently loses SOL on average. Honest framing, plus Motherlode-conditioned strategies, is essential, and manager 'skill' is mostly noise over short windows.
Two-sided cold start: a marketplace needs good managers, and the team will be the first one. Manager income is capped at 1% of deployed SOL, which is thin until volume grows.
One Automation per wallet limits 'multiple shafts' to time-sliced shifts, which is less rich than the game metaphor suggests.
Art and production burden for a solo builder; the risk of judges seeing 'a skin over an autominer' if the Guard story isn't front and centre.
Gambling optics and dApp Store policy uncertainty; ORE match milestones require sustained support.
Shares its executor stack with Heads Down and Whistle. The orchestrator may prefer to fold its manager market into one of them rather than build it standalone.

lens: SEEKER-NATIVE X-FACTOR: experiences that are impossible on a web app, where the phone's own hardware, OS surfaces and Seeker identity are the product and still form a daily habit. Checked against the live dApp Store catalog (SeekerTracker mirror, 2026-09-29) and GitHub; web search budget was exhausted, so novelty checks relied on those two sources.

ideas.name: Face Down
ideas.one_liner: Put your Seeker face-down and it becomes an ORE rig: every minute you're not scrolling, it mines; pick it up and the rig stops.
ideas.core_concept: Face Down is a digital-wellbeing app whose reward engine is ORE mining. It turns Seeker Summer's own tagline ('Less scrolling. More seeking.') and ORE's never-shipped 'Proof of mobile: mine ORE on Seeker' promise into a product. Once a week the owner 'clocks in' with one Seed Vault double-tap. That funds an ORE Automation account they alone control, with Face Down's executor set as its executor. After that the phone's sensors are the controls. When the phone is face-down, screen-off, or on the charger in the night window, the rig deploys every ~78-second round. Picking the phone up pauses the rig after a 10-second grace. The core value is a Forest/Opal-style focus and sleep habit with friends, which works with no token at all. ORE simply turns offline time into slowly accumulating hard money, with an honest live 'cost per dark hour' read from on-chain production cost. Crews of 3-8 Seekers are enforced on-chain as one seat per Seeker Genesis Token mint. Everyone in a crew mines the same tiles, so strikes are shared moments, and the crew widget shows who is 'dark' right now. Why now: the official ORE app has been stale since Oct 2025, mobile ORE is bot autominers, ORE's Automation/DiscretionaryBps executors (Aug 2026) make hands-free non-custodial mining possible, and Android 16 Live Updates on Seeker give the rig a lock-screen presence no crypto app uses yet.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: bedtime, a meeting or gym block, or the crew widget showing '3 of 5 crew dark', a social pull that inverts social media's online dot. Action: zero taps. Flip the phone over, or tap the 'Go Dark' Quick Settings tile. A weekly double-tap refills the rig. Variable reward: the morning Rig Report. It shows rounds mined, split-tile strikes, rare solo-tile wins, crew strikes, and Motherlode events that happened while you slept ('it hit tile 17; your crew was on 17'). Haptic strike pulses also arrive while the phone lies face-down. Investment: unrefined ORE that earns a share of the 10% refining fee from other miners' claims (holding pays); a dark-hours streak with automatic freezes; your crew seat and rank; and a rig that levels up cosmetically. Why you open it with no airdrop: it is your sleep and focus accountability app with friends, and the ORE is savings rather than points.
mobile_native_surfaces: Sensor fusion in a foreground service the user starts: gravity vector (face-down), proximity (covered), screen state, charging and night window. Phone posture is the mining switch

Android 16 Live Update (NotificationCompat.ProgressStyle + setRequestPromotedOngoing): a status-bar chip plus lock-screen/AOD card reading 'Rig running 1h12m · 55 rounds · +0.0021 ORE'. It is a user-started session, like a workout, not a price ticker
Quick Settings tile 'Go Dark' whose subtitle shows today's dark hours, plus an App Shortcut 'Night shift'
Glance home-screen widget: a live 5x5 board with the crew's tiles, a Motherlode meter and crew presence, updated by FCM pushes fed from Helius streams
Live wallpaper (WallpaperService) that renders your rig's cave glowing with last night's strikes
Custom haptic language: a strike pulse, a crew-strike pulse, and a global 'Motherlode heartbeat' that fires on every rig at the same moment
Seed Vault double-tap as the weekly 'clock in' ritual that funds and refills the rig, reached from the tile or widget through a trampoline MWA activity
Stack mode over Nearby Connections (BLE): friends at dinner link rigs face-down together, and the first to pick up drops SKR into the crew jar
Seeker Genesis Token verified on-chain, .skr names on the crew board, and dApp Store deep-link invites ('join my crew')
ideas.solana_integration: ORE program (oreV3EG1…): the user signs once via MWA to create and fund an Automation account. The account's authority is the user and its executor is Face Down's executor, configured with a DiscretionaryBps fee of at most 1%, a crew tile mask, auto-reload of winnings, and conditions for maximum production cost and minimum Motherlode. ORE's program lets the executor only deploy the SOL to the board or return it to the owner. That makes the app non-custodial by construction; a leaked executor key can at worst deploy within the per-round cap. The executor deploys only for rigs whose device holds an active shift. Shift start and stop are signed by a device-bound Android Keystore P-256 key, and a pre-signed night window keeps overnight sessions alive through Doze. The owner can close the automation and withdraw at any time, or switch to ORE's permissionless executor. Face Down's own Pinocchio program, 'facedown', does four things. (1) init_rig verifies the SGT in-program: the token account owner is the signer, the amount is 1, the mint is owned by Token-2022, TokenGroupMember.group is GT22s89…, and the mint authority is GT2zuH…. It then creates the Rig PDA [b'rig', sgt_mint], and a rebind instruction handles permissioned SGT moves between the user's own wallets. (2) Crew PDAs allow one seat per SGT mint. (3) record_day stores the device-signed count of dark minutes, verified through the secp256r1 precompile with instruction introspection, so one device cannot pose as ten. (4) The crew 'Proof of Mobile' leaderboard reads ORE Miner accounts, so ORE mined per Seeker is verifiable rather than self-reported. Transaction v1 (4 KB) lets the executor batch several rigs' deploys into one transaction, cutting fee drag on small rigs. Helius Parsed Streams on the Round, Miner and Treasury accounts drive the widget and Live Update pushes. Why on-chain: the mining itself is the product, custody has to be impossible, and crew seats cannot be botted.
ideas.ore_detail: ORE is the only reward asset and the primary featured product. Every dark minute is an ORE deployment through the user's own Automation account, run by Face Down's DiscretionaryBps executor with ORE's permissionless 7,000-lamport executor as fallback. The app revives ORE's removed claim_seeker and 'Proof of mobile' ideas at the app layer, as SGT-verified rigs and crews. Honest economics are shown in-app. Rigs recycle their SOL every round: losing tiles return 89.1% of the SOL deployed and winning tiles 99%. The net cost is roughly the round fees minus the ORE received; production cost is about $104 per ORE against a ~$85 price. So a hobby-sized rig costs cents per night in expectation, and the figure is displayed live. 'Motherlode hunter' mode concentrates deploys into rounds where the Motherlode is above a threshold. Candidate milestones for the ORE match: active rigs, dark hours, SOL deployed, and first-time miners who never used ore.com.
ideas.skr_role: Secondary and non-staking: the 'Doomscroll Jar'. If you declare a shift and break it early, a small SKR amount you chose drops into the crew jar; in Stack mode the same happens to whoever picks up first. Each week the jar is swapped to ORE through Jupiter and sent to ORE's grams address, which buries it automatically ('your doomscrolling buries ORE'). Alternatively, the crew can vote to split the jar among members who kept their shifts. SKR works here as a commitment currency that feeds ORE scarcity, not a reward drop. Keep it optional, because it resembles stake-on-habit apps (bozPledge).
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: a lit Seeker on a dark desk. The founder flips it face-down; it buzzes once, and the always-on display shows the Live Update chip 'Rig running'. 5-12s: time-lapse. The face-down phone double-pulses twice ('strike'), while a second Seeker beside it shows the Glance widget lighting tile 14 with '+0.0008 ORE' and the crew row switching to '4/5 dark'. 12-17s: he picks the phone up; the chip turns amber with 'Rig paused, put me down', and his avatar on the crew widget leaves the dark. 17-20s: title card: 'The only proof-of-work that pays you for not working your phone.' Then a cut back to the single double-tap clock-in that funded it all.
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: one fingerprint, then fully automated and non-custodial mining driven by the phone's own sensors, a crisp answer to 'why a crypto phone', plus a proof-of-work joke. Mert: live widget and lock-screen state run on Helius Parsed Streams (GA Sept 25), a visible, real use of his infrastructure. Chase: crews spread through dApp Store deep links, a first-10k-users loop with no token emissions. Akshay and Beeman: it productizes Seeker Summer's 'Less scrolling. More seeking.', uses widgets, Quick Settings tiles, Live Updates and the Seed Vault ritual correctly, and finally ships ORE's abandoned 'mine ORE on Seeker' promise. Voynich and A2nkF (Ethelsec): custody is impossible by ORE's program design; the app's own program is small, with rigorous Token-2022 SGT checks and PDAs keyed by SGT mint; secp256r1 verification uses proper instruction introspection; and the README bounds exactly what a compromised executor can do. ORE team: the first native, consumer, Seeker-exclusive ORE app, bringing in new miners rather than bots.
ideas.closest_existing: RefinORE AutoMiner (91 reviews), Orestack/Minemore (38) and Oreminer (296) are 24/7 expected-value autominers that use burner wallets or email logins. They have no behavioural gating and no social layer, and they are bots by design; Face Down mines only while you are away and adds crews without custody. The official ORE app (2,198 reviews) has been stale since Oct 2025, and ore.com is a PWA. DeepWork on Seeker (31 reviews) is a strict focus timer at 1 USDC a month with no mining. ScreenLytics (370) and EdgeVault Lite (97) are screen-time trackers only. Sleepagotchi (4,269 reviews) proves Seeker owners install 'earn while you sleep' apps, but it is an off-chain points game. Solarma is a staked alarm. Forest and Opal (Web2) validate the wellbeing loop without hard-money accumulation. Hashish.fun ('Seeker is the new GPU', 50 reviews) is a separate proof-of-work token with a Seeker pool, not ORE and not tied to behaviour. What is new: phone posture as the mining switch, crews seated by SGT, and a Live Update rig.
ideas.technical_depth: The Kotlin/Compose app (or Expo with custom Kotlin modules) includes: a sensor-fusion foreground service (specialUse type, a state machine with hysteresis and grace period, Doze-safe night windows); a Live Update built with ProgressStyle on androidx.core 1.19; a Glance widget with a Chronometer RemoteView; a TileService using startActivityAndCollapse; a WallpaperService; Stack mode over Nearby Connections; and a trampoline MWA activity on clientlib-ktx with an encrypted auth-token cache and rejection recovery, which covers the AlignAI lint categories. The Pinocchio program implements SGT verification (Token-2022 TLV extension parsing), secp256r1 precompile introspection and crew/seat logic, with Mollusk/LiteSVM tests, fuzzing and Codama-generated clients. A Rust executor on the ore-api crate subscribes to Board and Round, schedules active rigs, and builds batched tx v1 deploys with Jito tips, retries and DiscretionaryBps fee accounting. The backend covers a single-use SIWS nonce service, Helius Parsed Streams fanned out to FCM, and crew aggregation. A threat-model README explains what the executor can and cannot do, builds are reproducible, and the commit history spans program, executor and Android surfaces.
key_risks: Optics: a wellbeing app that looks like gambling while you sleep. It has to be framed and shown as mining and savings with honest expected value. Production cost (~$104) is above the ORE price (~$85), so users lose a little on average. Hobby-sized rewards are small, and Motherlode shares are proportional to stake, so the thrill has to come from crew moments and haptics, not jackpots

Face-down detection is trivially spoofable. That doesn't matter for personal mining, since it is your own SOL, but dark-hour leaderboards must stay social-only or be anchored on verifiable ORE metrics

Overnight reliability: Android Doze, OEM battery killers and foreground-service limits can break sessions. Mitigate with the server-side executor plus pre-signed night windows, and test on a real Seeker early
Fee drag on tiny rigs (executor fees and transaction fees) can dominate returns. This needs minimum deploy sizes, Motherlode-threshold rounds and tx v1 batching

ORE prize conditions: ORE must stay the primary product, the integration must stay live, and milestone payments depend on post-hackathon usage metrics. ORE's June 2026 exploit history means the integration's correctness will be scrutinized
Live Update eligibility: Google may not accept a mining session. Fall back to a standard ongoing notification, and verify Android 16 behaviour on a Seeker
Audience split: hardcore miners may prefer 24/7 autominers. The app has to win the wellbeing crowd first, with ORE as the delightful engine
Name collision risk with AFK.FUN and generic 'grass' branding; a trademark check is needed

ideas.name: Tripwire
ideas.one_liner: Truecaller for your Seeker wallet: every transaction, address and link is identified by verified Seekers, and drainers are stopped before your double-tap.
ideas.core_concept: Tripwire is a Seeker-native security layer that sits somewhere no Solana security tool has sat: inside the on-device Mobile Wallet Adapter signing path. In Guard mode (the default), Tripwire registers as an MWA wallet endpoint. When any dApp asks for a signature, Tripwire first simulates the transaction with Helius and renders a plain-English diff of balances, authorities and delegates. It then checks policy rules: SetAuthority and Approve instructions, mints with permanent-delegate or transfer-hook extensions, durable-nonce advances (the root cause of the Drift hack), lookalike recipients and unknown programs. Only then does it relay the unmodified transaction to Seed Vault Wallet for the double-tap, or block it. In Pocket mode, risky apps connect to a device-bound Pocket key with a spending cap, refilled daily from the Seed Vault account through the audited Subscriptions & Allowances program, so a malicious mint site can take at most today's allowance. A Truecaller-style 'Caller ID' runs Helius streams on the user's wallets. It flags address-poisoning dust and spam NFTs the moment they land ('lookalike of your contact bob.skr') and hides them. Selecting any address, contract address, .skr name or transaction hash in X or Telegram offers 'Check with Tripwire'. Labels come from an on-chain threat registry that allows one report per Seeker Genesis Token, so attackers cannot mass-vote their drainer as safe. Why now: the dApp Store has zero pre-sign protection apps, owners post drain stories constantly, 2026 was a bad security year on Solana (Drift $286M, Avici, ORE's June exploit), and two of the judges are security researchers.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: external and daily by nature. Attackers send poisoning dust and scam NFTs every day, and every dApp transaction the user already makes passes through Tripwire (73% of Seeker signers make more than 5 transactions a day). Action: glance at the verdict sheet and double-tap, or read a Caller ID push ('3 spam transfers hidden'). Variable reward: 'blocked' moments; rent SOL reclaimed by burning and closing spam accounts in one tap; your threat reports confirmed by other Seekers; and a morning 'wallet weather' card. Investment: a .skr contact graph that powers lookalike detection, custom policies, Pocket settings, and Sentinel reputation. With no airdrop, it is pure utility, like antivirus or Truecaller: it earns the daily open by catching things.
mobile_native_surfaces: MWA wallet endpoint (walletlib) that appears in the system wallet chooser, combined with an MWA client that relays to Seed Vault Wallet: a firewall inside the on-device signing path
Seed Vault double-tap reserved for vetted transactions, allowance changes and Lockdown
ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT: 'Check with Tripwire' in the text-selection menu of every app (addresses, contract addresses, .skr names, transaction hashes, X handles)
Share-sheet target for URLs and Blinks, plus a 'Safe Scan' Quick Settings tile that uses the ML Kit code scanner (no camera permission) for physical-world Solana Pay and Blink QR codes
'Lockdown' Quick Settings tile: one double-tap revokes all delegations, the Pocket allowance and risky approvals in a single tx v1 transaction
Glance 'wallet weather' widget: green/amber/red status, threats blocked today, and Pocket balance against its cap
High-priority Caller ID notifications from Helius Parsed Streams via FCM, plus an ongoing notification while a large vault transfer is pending
Device-bound Android Keystore keys: the Pocket Ed25519 key (hardware Curve25519 if Seeker's KeyMint supports it, otherwise Keystore-wrapped) and a P-256 device key
On-device LLM (LiteRT-LM, Gemma 3 1B on CPU) that narrates the simulation diff offline, so the transaction never leaves the phone for the explanation
Optional Android Contacts integration: .skr friends appear in the native Contacts app with a 'Send on Solana' action
ideas.solana_integration: Three layers. (1) Pocket: a Subscriptions & Allowances program delegation (audited, on mainnet since June) from the Seed Vault account to the Pocket key, capped per day, expiring, and revocable with one double-tap. The Pocket signs risky dApp transactions directly, so the vault never touches untrusted apps. (2) Sentinel Registry, Tripwire's own Pinocchio program: Report PDAs [b'report', target, sgt_mint] can be created only after the program verifies the reporter's SGT (Token-2022 owner, amount, TokenGroupMember group GT22s89…, mint authority GT2zuH…). Reports carry a label, an evidence hash and a timestamp. SKR bonds sit in the program's escrow with dispute windows, and aggregate labels are readable by any wallet or dApp over RPC, or via CPI as a public good. (3) Analysis: Helius simulateTransaction, Parsed Events and the Wallet API produce the diffs; DAS detects spam NFTs; getTokenAccountsByOwnerV2 checks the SGT. Tripwire fully parses v0 and v1 (4 KB) transactions, including detection of the durable-nonce AdvanceNonceAccount instruction. Lockdown and 'clean wallet' batch revoke, close and burn instructions plus rent reclaim (WithdrawExcessLamports after SIMD-0437) into one signature. Why on-chain: the Pocket cap has to be enforced by a program, because no server can undo a phished signature, and the threat registry has to be public, sybil-resistant through the SGT, and uncensorable so other wallets can consume it.
ideas.ore_detail: None. A later option is a 'safe mining' Pocket preset that whitelists the ORE program. This is not an ORE-prize play.
ideas.skr_role: Sentinel bonds. To publish a weighted threat label, or to dispute one, a Seeker locks a small SKR bond in the registry's own escrow for a dispute window; this is not the SKR staking program. If a quorum of SGT holders overturns a label, the bond is slashed to the disputers. Early reporters of drainers that are later confirmed earn from an SKR bounty pool funded by optional Tripwire Pro fees paid in SKR and by ecosystem security sponsors. This implements the SKR whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators' idea for security, with SKR as skin in the game rather than a reward drop. Avoid any wording that sounds like staking.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-4s: 'I'm going to get drained on camera.' On a real Seeker he opens a fake 'Seeker Season 3 airdrop' site and taps Claim. 4-10s: instead of Seed Vault, a red Tripwire sheet slides up with a hard haptic: 'BLOCKED: this transaction makes 7xKq…9f3a the owner of your USDC account. 23 verified Seekers reported this domain today.' Seed Vault never opened. 10-16s: in Telegram he long-presses an address a 'support admin' sent him. The selection menu shows 'Check with Tripwire', which answers 'Lookalike of your contact bob.skr: address poisoning (first and last 4 characters match, the middle doesn't).' 16-20s: he pulls down Quick Settings, taps Lockdown and double-taps once; the explorer shows every delegation revoked in a single transaction.
ideas.judge_appeal: Voynich and A2nkF (Ethelsec): this is their field turned into a consumer product. It checks authority changes, permanent delegates, durable nonces (the Drift root cause) and address poisoning, and ships a written threat model that includes the case where Tripwire itself is malicious: it never holds vault keys, builds are reproducible, and Seed Vault Wallet still shows the real transaction. Mert: Helius simulation, Parsed Streams and DAS end to end, and explanations generated privately on the device, which fits his 2026 privacy push. Beeman: deep MWA engineering (Tripwire is both a wallet endpoint and a client), exactly the wiring AlignAI checks. Akshay: it makes 'Seeker is the safest place to hold crypto' literally true and fits the upcoming 'Privacy & Security' dApp Spotlight theme. Toly: a sybil-resistant public-good registry built on device identity, tx v1 batching, and a hot/cold split enforced on-chain. Chase: every one of the ~120K owners needs it on day one.
ideas.closest_existing: Phinn (132 reviews) is a manual, after-the-fact 'send it to Phinn' phishing checker, not in the signing path. RugLens (340) scores token risk for pasted mint addresses. SIMGUARD (1) alerts on SIM swaps. Phantom's and Solflare's built-in simulation warnings (Blowfish, Blockaid) live inside their own wallets and use neither Seeker identity nor other wallets' MWA path. Seed Vault Wallet's confirmation screen shows the transaction but carries no community intelligence. Desktop extensions such as Pocket Universe and Web3 Antivirus have no mobile Solana equivalent. Vultisig (573) is a multi-device MPC wallet, a different model. SeekerClaw v2.1's capped burner wallet serves an AI agent, not a user firewall. Swig and Squads smart accounts are policy wallets without consumer threat intelligence. Truecaller is the Web2 model. What is new: a firewall in the on-device MWA path, a Pocket enforced by the audited Allowances program, SGT-verified threat intelligence, and system-wide text-selection checks.
ideas.technical_depth: A Kotlin app implementing mobile-wallet-adapter-walletlib as the endpoint and clientlib-ktx as the relay to Seed Vault Wallet, with explicit package targeting, identity handling, rejection recovery, and auth tokens in Keystore-encrypted storage. A transaction decoding and rules engine covering System, SPL Token and Token-2022 extensions (permanent delegate, transfer hook, confidential transfer), durable nonces, v0 lookup tables and v1 transactions, unit-tested against a corpus of real drainer transactions. LiteRT-LM integration with a template-text fallback; the ML Kit scanner, a PROCESS_TEXT activity, TileServices and a Glance widget. A Pinocchio Sentinel Registry with SGT verification, bond escrow and a dispute state machine, plus fuzz tests and a Codama client. Integration with the Allowances program (create, pull, revoke). Backend: Helius webhooks and Parsed Streams per opted-in wallet, poisoning heuristics (prefix and suffix lookalikes compared against the contact graph and history), FCM fan-out, and a SIWS nonce service. A public THREAT_MODEL.md and reproducible builds.
key_risks: MWA relay feasibility: Seed Vault Wallet sees Tripwire rather than the original dApp as the requesting identity, and may relabel or decline relayed requests. The Android wallet chooser adds a step unless Tripwire is set as the default, and some dApps pin a specific wallet. This must be proven on a real Seeker in week one
Seeker Activity scoring tracks the Seed Vault primary wallet, so farming-motivated owners will resist moving activity to a Pocket address; Guard mode has to be the default
Stickiness is at the level of a utility like antivirus, not a habit, so judges may score 'daily engagement' below games or mining
One missed drainer or one wrongly flagged legitimate app destroys trust. Coordinated real Seekers could game registry labels, and publicly labelling something a 'scam' carries legal exposure
A 'wallet in the middle' is exactly what an attacker would build, so the app needs open source, reproducible builds and ideally Solana Mobile's blessing
Incumbent wallets (Phantom, and the Solflare-designed Seed Vault Wallet) could ship similar warnings; the moat is Seeker identity plus a position across all wallets
Live Updates forbid countdowns to future events, so pending-transfer alerts likely fall back to standard ongoing notifications. On-device LLM latency on the Dimensity 7300 is unverified
SKR bond and dispute mechanics add complexity and could read as staking-adjacent

ideas.name: Punch
ideas.one_liner: Tap in, get paid by the second: your lock screen shows USDC you've already earned, and every cent is a signed voucher you can cash out right now.
ideas.core_concept: Punch is the literal 'Clock In' app: a time clock for the stablecoin-paid workforce, built on Solana's newest audited primitive, Payment Channels (on mainnet since Sept 3, 2026). The payer (a DAO, a startup paying contractors, a shop or a client) opens a USDC channel to the worker once, escrowing for example a week of wages. The payer names a bounded 'voucher signer' that can only ever pay that worker, and never more than the escrow. The worker clocks in by tapping an NFC tag at the site (an NTAG 424 DNA tag that resists cloning), scanning a rotating QR code, entering a geofence, or using a Quick Settings tile for remote roles. The worker's hardware Keystore key signs each clock event. While the worker is clocked in, cumulative Ed25519 vouchers stream to their phone every few seconds. The phone verifies each one locally, and a Live Update on the lock screen shows the total the worker can already redeem: money, not a promise. The worker can settle mid-shift ('pay me now') or at clock-out. One transaction settles thousands of vouchers, and the account rent goes back to the operator, so the worker never needs SOL. Every clock-in and clock-out is signed by the device, keyed to the worker's Seeker Genesis Token, and anchored on-chain through the secp256r1 precompile. That produces a tamper-evident, portable work history and rules out ghost workers. Why now: Payment Channels has no consumer mobile app yet, the Solana Foundation just hired a GM of Payments, stablecoin supply on Solana is at an all-time high, and earned-wage access is a proven Web2 habit (DailyPay, Payactiv). Of the 1,422 dApp Store apps, none handles clock-in, shifts or attendance.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: the workday itself, whether arriving at the office or shop NFC tag, a scheduled-shift reminder, or the payer's 'you're on today' push. Action: one tap on the NFC tag or the Quick Settings tile; clocking in needs no wallet popup because the device key signs. Variable reward: watching the lock-screen meter climb, instant 'pay me now' cash-outs, bonus bumps from the payer that arrive as larger vouchers ('+5 USDC from ada.skr'), and on-time streaks. Investment: a growing, verifiable on-chain work history (hours, payers, reliability) the worker can show for loans, visas and the next client, plus saved payer relationships and auto top-up schedules. With no airdrop in play, it is simply how you get paid, and people open their pay app every workday.
mobile_native_surfaces: NFC tag clock-in: an Android Application Record launches the app from a cold start, and NTAG 424 DNA secure-message authentication (a fresh CMAC on every tap) blocks cloned or photographed tags. NFC is unconfirmed on Seeker, so fallbacks are a rotating signed QR code (ML Kit scanner), a BLE beacon or a geofence
Android 16 Live Update (ProgressStyle): 'On shift · 3h12m of 8h · 41.60 USDC earned', a user-started, time-bound session like a rideshare or workout
Quick Settings tile 'Clock in/out' for remote roles, plus App Shortcuts
Glance widgets: one for the worker (earned today and this week, next shift) and one for the payer (live roster of who is on shift, and burn rate against escrow)
Android Keystore P-256 device key that signs every clock event (optionally bound to biometrics), verified on-chain through the secp256r1 precompile
Seed Vault double-tap for the payer to open or top up a channel and for the worker to sweep earnings to the vault, through a trampoline MWA activity
Voucher transport over a websocket or a Nostr relay (off-chain, end-to-end)
.skr names for payers and workers, and dApp Store deep-link invites from payer to worker
ideas.solana_integration: Payment Channels program (CHNLxYvVA28MJP9PrFuDXccuoGXAx7jBacfLEkahyGsX): the payer's open instruction escrows USDC with authorized_signer set to Punch's payer-side voucher key. That key is hot but bounded: the channel PDA fixes the payee and mint, and cumulative vouchers can never exceed the deposit. Vouchers are the program's canonical 50-byte Ed25519 messages (channel_id, cumulative_amount, expires_at). The worker settles through the Ed25519 precompile followed by settle, and distribute pays out while the channel stays Open. The payer's weekly double-tap calls top_up; request_close and seal handle disputes; rent_payer is the operator, so workers hold only USDC. Punch's own Pinocchio program, 'punch', holds a Job PDA [b'job', payer, worker_sgt_mint] with the rate, schedule, channel and site keys, and verifies the worker's SGT in-program. Its ShiftLog records clock-in and clock-out events signed by the worker's P-256 Keystore key together with the site's rotating code. It verifies them through secp256r1 precompile introspection and rolls them up daily as a Merkle root to keep costs low. Helius streams send settlement notifications, and Kora or an operator fee payer sponsors transaction fees. Why on-chain: escrow removes the freelancer's biggest fear, non-payment, and limits the payer's risk to a few seconds of work. Paying per second without a transaction per second is only possible with channels. And the device-signed shift log is a portable, verifiable income record that no single employer controls.
ideas.ore_detail: None. ORE would dilute the payments story and could not be the primary product here.
ideas.skr_role: Light and optional: payers can add SKR bonuses or tips through a second channel denominated in SKR, for example Seeker-ecosystem projects paying community contributors in SKR per hour. It is not core; don't chase the SKR prize with this idea.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: a contractor walks up to a coworking door in Lagos and taps her Seeker on a small NFC sticker (or scans the rotating QR code). The phone buzzes once, and her lock screen shows a Live Update chip: 'On shift · 0.00 USDC'. 5-12s: time-lapse of her working while the chip counts up cent by cent in real time, with the overlay 'each tick is a signed voucher, verified on this phone'. 12-17s: she taps 'Pay me now' mid-shift; the explorer shows one settle transaction covering 4,300 vouchers, and USDC lands in her account. 17-20s: split screen with the employer's widget showing the live roster and escrow burn. Title card: 'Clock in. Get paid by the second.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Toly: the purest demonstration of Solana payments at scale, with millions of off-chain vouchers, one settlement, 250 ms slots and no speculation. Chase (Solana Foundation): the Foundation's brand-new Payment Channels and pay-kit get their first consumer mobile app, exactly what its new GM of Payments needs to point to. Mert: Helius-driven settlement notifications, with salary privacy via Helius Rings as the natural roadmap (Squads' Altitude already plans payroll on Rings). Akshay and Beeman: 'real-time payments' and real-world utility straight from the Solana Mobile grants page, a product that is the hackathon's name, and NFC, Live Update and Quick Settings tiles done properly. Voynich and A2nkF: a bounded authorized signer, monotonic cumulative vouchers, new channel addresses per open_slot to prevent replay, no custody, device-signed timesheets verified on-chain, and a clear dispute path. Founder story: a builder in Nigeria, where freelancers often wait weeks for invoices to clear.
ideas.closest_existing: Zebec (streaming payroll on Solana since 2021, now card-focused) and Streamflow (vesting and payroll streams) are web-first on-chain streams that accrue whether or not the worker is present. Punch pays only while the worker is clocked in, per second, off-chain, with one settlement. Sablier and Superfluid are EVM streams. DailyPay and Payactiv (earned-wage access), Deel, Rise and Request Finance (USDC payroll), and Homebase and Clockify (time clocks) are Web2 products that keep the clock and the pay separate; Punch merges them. Clock In competitor repos: nuntius/mandatum (capped recurring payments through Seed Vault, i.e. subscriptions, not metered time), TapWifSol and Seeker PAY (tap to pay), Legwork (paid real-world missions) and ChainWitness (proof of presence without pay). pay.sh uses the same channels for machine payments (x402 and MPP), not human wages. No dApp Store app handles clock-in, shifts or attendance.
ideas.technical_depth: A Kotlin client for the Payment Channels program generated with Codama (or the TypeScript client inside Expo), plus on-device voucher verification: Ed25519 over the canonical 50-byte message, with monotonicity and expiry checks. A payer-side voucher streamer in Rust that signs only while valid worker heartbeats arrive, with rate limits and a guard on the escrow watermark. A Pinocchio program, 'punch', covering SGT verification, Job and ShiftLog accounts, secp256r1 precompile introspection, Merkle roll-ups and dispute flags, tested with LiteSVM. Android: NFC with NTAG 424 message verification over IsoDep, a rotating-QR site app, geofencing through GeofencingClient, a ProgressStyle Live Update, a TileService, two Glance widgets, and Keystore P-256 keys with attestation. Backend: SIWS nonce service, Helius webhooks and a Kora fee relayer. An economic-security README that states the worst case for every key.
key_risks: Two-sided cold start: every worker needs a payer. Judges will ask for real payer and worker pairs, so recruit 5-10 real teams (Superteam chapters, DAOs, the builder's own network) during the build month
Resonance with the Seeker community is only moderate, because most owners are not paid hourly in USDC; the pitch has to prove the contributor and DAO niche is real among Seeker owners
Crypto doesn't solve trust: a worker can fake presence and a payer can stop sending vouchers. Exposure is bounded to seconds of work, but management disputes stay off-chain

Tooling: Payment Channels ships only TypeScript and Rust clients, so Kotlin needs Codama generation or a JNI bridge. The program is new (audited in July 2026), and proposed v2 changes could shift the API
Regulation: payroll, tax withholding and labour law vary by country, so position Punch as contractor and freelancer payments, not employment payroll
Unverified on Seeker: NFC hardware, Live Update eligibility for an earnings meter, and activation of the secp256r1 precompile on mainnet
Stickiness evidence is harder to generate in 30 days than for a consumer game

ideas.name: Receipts
ideas.one_liner: Your Seeker stamps a receipt every time you actually use a dApp, and only people with receipts can review, so you finally see what real humans use and trust.
ideas.core_concept: Receipts is a verified-human discovery and reputation layer for the 1,422-app Seeker dApp Store: Letterboxd or Untappd for dApps, except that fake reviews are cryptographically impossible. After linking a passport verified by the user's Seeker Genesis Token, the phone automatically stamps a receipt whenever one of the user's wallets genuinely interacts with an app's registered programs. When the app keeps user state on-chain (for example an ORE Miner account or a Kamino obligation), the receipt is trustless: the Receipts program reads that account directly. Otherwise the receipt is attested by the indexer and carries the transaction signatures, so anyone can audit it. Only people holding a receipt for an app can rate or review it. Each night, one Seed Vault double-tap seals the day's ratings on-chain ('close the book'). The home-screen widget shows what verified Seekers used today, what your .skr friends are stamping, and safety flags on apps you have touched, and every card deep-links straight into the dApp Store listing. Developers claim their app with its on-chain dApp Store publisher wallet and register their program IDs and account schemas. In return they get a public 'Verified Human DAU' figure and can read receipts to reward genuine users instead of farmers. Why now: store ratings were inflated by Season 1 'rate apps' tasks; users can't browse or trust the 263 apps added in September alone; Solana Mobile re-weighted activity scoring on Aug 20 to fight bot-like activity; and the SKR whitepaper's 'Ecosystem Curators' is still unbuilt.
ideas.daily_loop: Trigger: organic dApp use (73% of Seeker signers make 5 or more transactions a day). Receipts land with a stamp animation and a haptic thunk, and the widget surfaces friends' fresh receipts and what is trending with verified humans. Action: rate today's receipts in two taps and seal them with one nightly double-tap, or tap a friend's receipt to open that app through a dApp Store deep link. Variable reward: 'Early Receipt' status when an app you stamped early climbs the verified-human charts, SKR tips on helpful reviews, rare holographic stamps for the first 100 verified users of a new app, and safety saves ('an app you used was just flagged'). Investment: a growing passport of stamps that works as identity, like a Letterboxd diary, plus reviewer reputation and followers. With no airdrop, you open it to decide which app to try next and whether it is safe, the way people check Letterboxd before picking a film.
mobile_native_surfaces: Glance widget showing what is trending with verified Seekers today and friends' latest receipts; every tap is a dApp Store deep link (solanadappstore://details?id=<package>)
Nightly Seed Vault double-tap that seals all of the day's ratings in one tx v1 transaction ('clock out')
Holographic stamp cards rendered with an AGSL RuntimeShader driven by the gyroscope, exported as share images for X and Telegram
ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT and a share target: select an app name, domain or program ID anywhere to see verified reviews and safety status
Haptic stamp feedback, plus notifications when a receipt lands or an app you used gets flagged
SGT verified on-chain, with the .skr social graph for follows and the friends feed
App Shortcuts ('Today's receipts', 'Seal the day')
ideas.solana_integration: The app's own Pinocchio program, 'receipts', has five parts. (1) A Passport PDA [b'passport', sgt_mint], created only after the program verifies the SGT; extra wallets are linked with signatures from both wallets, so activity in Phantom or Backpack counts too. (2) An App PDA keyed by the dApp Store app NFT. A developer claims it by signing with the on-chain publisher wallet, then registers program IDs and a proof-of-use account schema (PDA seeds plus owner program). (3) A Receipt PDA [b'receipt', app, sgt_mint] in one of two modes. In trustless mode the program reads the user's state account owned by the app's program (for example the ORE Miner account [b'miner', authority]) and checks its owner and derivation. In attested mode the indexer signs an Ed25519 attestation over the transaction signatures, which the program verifies through the Ed25519 precompile and anyone can audit. (4) A Review PDA that requires a Receipt and stores the rating and an Arweave hash of the text; a night's reviews are written in a batch under a single user signature. (5) SKR bond escrow for curators, with a dispute-and-slash state machine and a tip router. Helius Parsed Events and Streams (3,600+ programs decoded) map opted-in wallets' activity to apps in real time, and the dApp Store catalog and app NFTs are synced for metadata. Why on-chain: receipts and reviews must be publicly verifiable and composable so any dApp, or Solana Mobile itself, can consume them, and the sybil resistance has to come from device identity rather than a server's word.
ideas.ore_detail: Not a feature. ORE only appears as the showcase 'trustless receipt' (read from the Miner account) in the demo. Not an ORE-prize play.
ideas.skr_role: Core, non-staking, and the strongest SKR-prize fit of the four ideas. It implements the SKR whitepaper's unbuilt 'Ecosystem Curators': (a) curator bonds, where reviewers may lock SKR in the program's own escrow to weight their reviews, and reviews that an SGT-quorum dispute judges paid or spam are slashed; (b) SKR tips to helpful reviewers by .skr name; (c) an 'Early Receipt' curator pool, funded by apps and sponsors, that rewards reviewers whose early ratings predicted later verified-human growth; and (d) SKR-funded genuine-use quests, where eligibility is a trustless receipt, so farmers can't qualify. None of this touches the SKR staking program.
ideas.wow_demo_moment: 0-5s: on a real Seeker he swaps on Jupiter, mines one ORE round, and returns to the home screen. 5-10s: the Receipts widget stamps 'ORE ✓ verified receipt #1,204' with a haptic thunk; he tilts the phone and the holographic stamp shimmers. 10-16s: split screen. One store app shows 4.9★ from 3,000 store reviews, while Receipts shows '0 verified users, 2 Sentinel flags'. Next to it, Kamino shows '4.6★ from 812 verified Seekers who actually deposited'. 16-20s: at night one double-tap seals the day's three ratings on-chain. Title card: 'Reviews you can't fake.'
ideas.judge_appeal: Akshay and Beeman: it fixes the store's biggest trust and discovery gaps (inflated reviews, 'I can't browse all the apps'), sends traffic through dApp Store deep links, and gives developers a sybil-proof 'Verified Human DAU' that Solana Mobile does not publish. It also implements the SKR whitepaper's curators, which puts it on-thesis for the SKR prize. Chase: it helps every Seeker app find its first 10k real users. Mert: Helius Parsed Events and Streams are the backbone of the product, and it works as an anti-bot public good. Toly: device identity used as sybil resistance for reputation, with receipts that other programs can read on-chain. Voynich and A2nkF: trustless proof of use via PDA re-derivation, Ed25519 precompile introspection for attested receipts, rigorous SGT checks and slashing logic. It also hedges the alternate Align rubric (SKR Integration 20, Ecosystem Impact 15).
ideas.closest_existing: The dApp Store's own ratings, AI review digests and Spotlight: anyone can review, Season 1 'rate apps' tasks inflated the counts, and there is no proof of use. Seeker Scout (56 reviews), AardAppvark Toolkit (280) and SeekerTracker are catalogs and explorers without verified reviews. SkrBoost and Seeker Airdrop Oracle are farming helpers, and Receipts must not be mistaken for one. DappRadar is web-based and its usage numbers are bot-inflated. Galxe and Layer3 credentials are farmable quests. Letterboxd, Untappd and Beli are the Web2 loops being borrowed. Stampd, a Clock In competitor repo, is a merchant loyalty passport in a different domain. What is new: reviews gated by trustless or auditable on-chain proof of use, one per Seeker device, readable by any program.
ideas.technical_depth: A Pinocchio 'receipts' program covering SGT verification, multi-wallet linking, trustless proof of use via PDA re-derivation and owner checks, attested receipts verified through the Ed25519 precompile, a review state machine, SKR bond escrow with dispute and slashing, and batched instructions in tx v1, with Mollusk/LiteSVM tests and fuzzing. An indexer on Helius Parsed Streams that maps program IDs to apps, runs backfills, and syncs the dApp Store catalog and app NFTs (Arweave metadata). On Android: a Glance widget, an AGSL holographic shader driven by the rotation-vector sensor, PROCESS_TEXT and share targets, deep-link routing, and a nightly batch-sign flow over MWA. A public read API and SDK so other dApps can gate perks on receipts.
key_risks: Perception: judges may read it as an activity-farming helper or meta tooling, which is on the avoid list. The framing must be anti-farm (proof of genuine use), and stamps must not reward raw transaction counts
Stickiness is moderate: review and discovery apps rarely become daily habits unless the social feed and charts are genuinely useful
Attested receipts depend on trusting the indexer, because an on-chain program cannot verify historical transactions; only apps that keep user-state PDAs get trustless receipts
Privacy: tying SGT and .skr identity to app usage aggregates public data into a doxxing surface. It must be opt-in, with per-receipt visibility controls
Platform risk: Solana Mobile could build verified reviews natively (the whitepaper plans curation), which would make Receipts redundant or turn it into a partnership
Cold start: it needs many developers to claim their apps and register programs, and enough reviewers per app to be meaningful
The SKR bond mechanics could be judged staking-adjacent
